سلسلة «خِطبة تتمحور حول المسيح» هي مجموعة من الخطب حول الخِطبة التقوية ألقاها بول هيرشبيرغر. لقد ألقاها عدة مرات في أماكن مختلفة على مدى السنوات العشر الماضية. مؤخراً، قمنا بنقلها إلى نص وتلخيصها من أجل وضوح القراءة. بعد طباعة المقالات الست كلها في The Heartbeat of the Remnant، سننشرها في كتيب. هذه هي المقالة الأولى من ست مقالات.

مقدمة

نِلْتُ أنا وزوجتي امتياز أن نَمُرَّ بخِطبةٍ بلا ندامات أو ذِمَّة. لقد باركَنا والدان قاداْنا في الطريق الصحيح ومنحانا فرصاً لم تكن متاحة لهما.

إذا لم تكن لديك شهادة أو ذكرى من هذا النوع، فلا تدخل في شعور بالذنب. لكن صلاتي لك هي أن تتوفر في قلبك عبء ورغبة ملتهبة لتحصل أنت على هذا لأولادك. هذا يمكن أن يكون مكافأتك.

الخِطبة التي تتمحور حول المسيح هي فترة زمنية بين حياة العزوبية وحياة الزواج. القرارات التي تتخذها في هذه الفترة ستؤثر عليك لباقي حياتك. مع بركة الله على حياتكم، يمكن أن تنتهي بلا ندم أو ذنب.

خمسة أهداف لسلسلة الخِطبة هذه المُتمحورة حول المسيح.

الهدف رقم 1. أن يرجع قلوب الآباء إلى أولادهم.

الهدف رقم 2. أن يرجع قلوب الأولاد إلى آبائهم.

الهدف رقم 3. أن يحمل الوالدان عبئًا لقيادة كل واحد من أولادهم إلى مشيئة الله الكاملة لحياتهم.

الهدف رقم 4. أن يحصل الشباب على عبء للسعي وراء الله، وإيجاد الإشباع والغرض في السير مع الله، وأن تسعوا للنضج في أخلاقكم وشخصيتكم.

الهدف رقم 5. أن يقوم الشبان والشابات ليكونوا آباءً تقويين وأمهات تقويات برؤية لتربية جيل تقوى آخر، وليستمر إنجيل يسوع المسيح.

خطة الله للرجل والمرأة

يكلم حكيم 12:1 يقول: «اذكر خالقك في أيام شبابك، قبل أن تأتي الأيام الشِدَّة، ولا تقترب السنين التي تقول فيها: ليس لي فيها سرور». رغبتي أن يذكر كل واحد منكم خالقه في أيام شبابه. ادر قلبك وتركيزك وحياتك للسعي وراء خالقك، الله القدير في السماء.

ماذا يقصد بكلامه «قبل أن تأتي الأيام الشِّدَّة» و«ولا تقترب السنين»؟ يعني أن تطلب الرب ما أنت شاب. خُذ طاقة شبابك واطلب الله. أيها الشباب، أنتم شباب وممتلئون بالأفكار والرؤى والخطط والأحلام. أشكّ أن يكون أحد منكم يكتفي بالجلوس في كرسي مريح، ويضع قدميه، ويحلم فقط كم ستكون الحياة فظيعة ومريعة. نحن لا نفعل ذلك، أليس كذلك؟ لكن إن لم نسِر مع الله ونتبع خطة الله، فالأمور الصعبة ستأتي علينا. عندما تأتي الأشياء الصعبة في الحياة، لن يكون لنا ملجأ نلوذ إليه. نحلم أن تنتهي الحياة بخير. القرارات والأفعال في شبابنا تؤثر في بقية حياتنا. الخبر السار أنها قد تؤثر لصالحنا. الخبر السيئ أنها قد تؤثر علينا سلباً. ذلك يعتمد على القرارات والخيارات التي نتخذها. لكن أيها الشباب، أنتم شباب، ولديكم فرصة للاختيار.

لنذهب إلى بداية سفر التكوين.

«فقال الرب الإله: ليس جيدًا أن يكون الإنسان وحده، أصنع له معينًا نظيره. فأشكل الرب الإله من الأرض كل برية الميدان وكل طائر السماء، وأحضرهم إلى آدم ليرى ماذا يدعو كل واحد منهم. وأيما سماه آدم نفس حي فذلك اسمه. فأعطى آدم أسماء لجميع البهائم وطير السماء ولكل وحش الحقل، أما لنفس آدم فلم يوجد معين نظيره. فأوقع الرب الإله غشاوة على آدم فنام، فأخذ إحدى أضلاعه، وسدّ اللحم مكانها. فأبنى الرب الإله الضلع التي أخذها من آدم امرأة، وأتى بها إلى الرجل. فقال آدم: هذه الآن عظم من عظامي ولحم من لحمي، لذلك يدعى اسمها امرأة، لأنها من الرجل أُخذت. من أجل هذا يترك الرجل أباه وأمه ويلصق بزوجته، ويكونان جسدًا واحدًا» (التكوين 2:18-24).

«وقال الله: لنصنع الإنسان على صورتنا كمثالنا، وليتسلط على سمك البحر وعلى طير السماء وعلى البهائم وعلى كل الأرض وعلى كل دابة تدب على الأرض. فخلق الله الإنسان على صورته، على صورة الله خلقه، ذكرًا وأنثى خلقهما. وباركهم الله وقال لهم: اثمروا وأكثروا واملأوا الأرض وسبّطوها، وتسلطوا على سمك البحر وعلى طير السماء وعلى كل دابة تحيا على الأرض» (التكوين 1:26-28).

«وقال الرب الإله: ليس جيدًا أن يكون الرجل وحده، أصنع له معينًا نظيره» (التكوين 2:18). «أصنع له معينًا يصلح له». قال الله إنه سيفعل ذلك.

«فخلق الله الإنسان على صورته، على صورة الله خلقه، ذكرًا وأنثى خلقهما» (التكوين 1:27). الله صنع. الله خلقنا ذكرًا وأنثى. يلزم قدر كبير من الإيمان الأعمى للاعتقاد أننا تطورنا تمامًا كذكور وإناث بدون خالق. خلق الذكر والأنثى هو خطة الله. إنه أحد الأدلة الحية على الخلق. الله صنع. الله خلق. إنها خطة الله. الله هو المؤلف. وخطة الله تجلب البركة.

أودُّ أن أنظر إلى عشرة جوانب مختلفة من هذه البركة في خطة الله.

1) الله يُقدِم حواء إلى آدم.

«وأبنى الرب الإله الضلع التي أخذها من آدم امرأة، وأتى بها إلى الرجل. فقال آدم: هذه الآن عظم من عظامي ولحم من لحمي، لذلك يدعى اسمها امرأة، لأنها من الرجل أُخذت» (التكوين 2:22-23).

أوقع الله غشاوة على آدم فنام، ثم خلق حواء وأحضرها إلى آدم. استيقظ آدم وأدرك: «هذه لي!» لقد رأى كل الحيوانات تمرّ عندما كان يُسَمّيها. الآن يقرب الله له شخصًا هو له. كما أدرك قائلاً: «أُخذَت من جنبِي». إنها قريبة من قلبه. «هذه الآن عظم من عظامي ولحم من لحمي». ليست كلبًا؛ ليست زرافة أو قرد أو إنسان قرد. هذه التي جلبها له الله مثلُه. لخطة الله بركة.

لم يكن لدى آدم وحواء مرافقة من قبل. لم يطلقا عواطف قلوبهما للآخرين قبل ذلك. حدث شيء في قلوب آدم وحواء. كان آدم رجل امرأة واحدة، وكانت حواء امرأة رجل واحد. لم يقدما عواطف قلبيهما لغير بعضهما. لدى الله خطة لنا أيضًا. خطة الله تجلب البركة.

2) ترك والتصاق في وحدة مدى الحياة.

«من أجل هذا يترك الرجل أباه وأمه ويلتصق بزوجته، ويكونان جسدًا واحدًا» (التكوين 2:24).

هذه الآية تقول: «من أجل هذا يترك الرجل أباه وأمه»، لكن آدم وحواء لم يكن لهما أبوان. ما يقصده الله أن الالتصاق لا يحدث دون ترك. أيضًا، في مرقس 10:7 نقرأ: «من أجل هذا يترك الرجل أباه وأمه ويلتصق بزوجته». هذه خطة الله، وخطة الله تجلب البركة.

الترك يعني التخلي، أو البعد عن. «من أجل هذا يترك الرجل أباه وأمه» يعني أن يترك الوالدان خلفه. فكر في شاب له حياة منزلية جيدة جدًا. مُبارك ولديه كل ما يحتاجه. ومع ذلك، متى جلب الله حوته إلى حياته، يقوم شيء في داخله ويقول: «أنا أرحل!» لكن هذه هي خطة الله. وخطة الله تجلب البركة.

ليس فقط أن يترك أباه وأمه؛ بل أيضًا أن يلتحق بزوجته. الالتصاق يعني «الالتصاق، الالتصاق كالغراء». نحن نعرف ألواح الخشب المركبة بالغراء. تُصنع كل أنواع الأثاث الصلب من ألواح ملصوقة. وإذا لُصقت بشكل صحيح، فلن تنفصل عند المفاصل. إذا مزقتها، فستضطر إلى تمزيق الخشب نفسه. غراء الله مشابه في طريقة عمله، عنده يلصق إنسانين معًا. الطريقة الوحيدة لتمزيقهما هي بالتشظي والتمزيق، والله لا يبارك ذلك. لكن الترك والالتصاق، البقاء معًا والالتصاق بالغراء، هذه خطة الله وتجلب البركة.

3) يصيران جسدًا واحدًا.

«من أجل هذا يترك الرجل أباه وأمه ويلتصق بزوجته، ويكونان جسدًا واحدًا» (التكوين 2:24). شخصان غير متزوجين يصبحان زوجين، يصبحان وحدة واحدة أمام الله، ويصبحان أسرة واحدة أمام الله. يصيران جسدًا واحدًا، حيث يراهما الله معًا كواحد.

«يكونان الإثنان جسدًا واحدًا. فإذا لم يعدا الإثنان فإِنَّهما جسد واحد. فالذي جمعه الله لا يفرقه الإنسان» (مرقس 10:8-9). خطة الله للرجل والمرأة هي أنه يقدِم حواء إلى آدم. ثم يحدث الترك والالتصاق. يجعلهم يصيران جسدًا واحدًا. التمزق ليس بركة على الإطلاق بل يجلب العذاب والألم والمحنة والأذى. لا بركة في الانفصال. لكن خطة الله تجلب البركة.

4) لا نِير غير متكافئ.

«لا تُشكِّلوا مع غير المؤمنين نيرًا لا متكافئًا، لأنَّ ما له الجوار مع البر؟ وما له الشركة مع الظلمة؟» (2 كو 6:14-15). «المرأة مربوطة بالقانون ما دام زوجها حيًّا، أما إذا مات زوجها فحرٌّة أن تتزوج من تَشاء، لكن في الرب فقط» (1 كو 7:39).

خطة الله أن يكون الزواج نيرًا متكافئًا. الله لن يقدِم حواء لآدم في زواج نيرٌ فيه عدم تكافؤ. لنفكر في الترك والالتصاق، والالتصاق بالغراء، وتحول اثنين إلى واحد. في الزواج، هذان الاثنان الآن هما واحد أمام الله. تخيّل أن تكون في علاقة زواج سيئة هكذا — عائلة من هذا النوع تحاول أن تعمل معًا. لن تكون هناك بركة.

لكن النير المتكافئ يجلب البركة! يطلب الله أن نكون متحدين جسدًا واحدًا، قلبًا واحدًا، وفكرًا واحدًا. يريد أن يرانا متحدين في القلب والعقل واللحم — الكل بذاته، كوننا واحدًا. خطة الله تجلب البركة.

5) خطط الله لنا أن يكون لنا أولاد.

«وباركهم الله وقال لهم: اثمروا وأكثروا واملأوا الأرض وسبّطوها، وتسلطوا على سمك البحر وعلى طير السماء وعلى كل دابة تحيا على الأرض» (التكوين 1:28). فكّر في الفرح والمعجزة في كل مرة يولد فيها طفل آخر في بيت مسيحي. الله خطط ذلك هكذا. وإذا جلب الله لآدم حوته، وتركوا والتصقوا، وصارا جسدًا واحدًا، قلبًا واحدًا، عقلًا واحدًا. إن كانوا مكلوبين بنير متكافئ وباركهم الله بالأولاد، فتصبح دارًا مفرحة يمكن لله أن يحل فيها. «وبارك الله نوحًا وبنيه وقال لهم: اثمروا وأكثروا واملأوا الأرض» (التكوين 9:1). «وأما أنتم فاثمروا وأكثروا وتكاثروا في الأرض» (التكوين 9:7). خطة الله تجلب البركة.

6) ترتيب الرئاسة (الرأس).

«وإني أريد أن تعلموا أن رأس كل رجل المسيح، ورأس المرأة الرجل، ورأس المسيح الله» (1 كو 11:3). هو الله، ثم المسيح، ثم الرجل، ثم المرأة. أقام الله ترتيبًا للرئاسة، وهذا الترتيب هو بركة. إنها خطة الله، وهي بركة.

«يا أولادي أطيعوا والديكم في الرب لأنه هذا الحق. أكرم أباك وأمك: هذه الوصية الأولى بوعد، لكي تكون لك أيام طويلة على الأرض» (أف 6:1-3). الطاعة للوالدين في الرب هي جزء من ترتيب الرئاسة. هذا ليس صعب الفهم، أليس كذلك؟ بيت يتَّبع خطة الله هو ببساطة حالة مباركة. يتعلم الشبان أن يكونوا تحت سلطة. اجعل ذلك أولوية قصوى. كلما أسرعتم في تعلم أن تكونوا تحت سلطة، كلما استعددتم أفضل للمسؤوليات في الحياة.

أتذكّر أنني كنت أتأمل الحياة الزوجية وكانت لدي طموحات بتعليم الأولاد وتربية أسرة تقية. استمعت إلى سلسلة «البيت التقوي» وظننت أنني مستعد للانطلاق. لكن جاء اليوم الذي صار دوري ومسؤوليتي، وفجأة رغبت قلبي أن يذبل. المسؤولية ليست كما في الحلم. يجب أن تَفعل شيئًا أنت! أنت المسؤول. يجب أن تجعلها تحدث. وماذا بعد؟ ليس فقط أن تجعلها تحدث؛ بل يجب أن تجعلها تحدث بطريقة مسيحية. يجب أن تجعلها تحدث بطريقة يمكن أن ينزل بها مسح روح الله على أسرتك. كلما تعلمنا أفضل كيف نكون تحت سلطة، كلما استعددنا أفضل لتلك المسؤوليات. كلما أدركنا أننا بحاجة إلى الله أكثر، كنا أفضل حالًا. اجعلوا من تعلم أن تكونوا تحت سلطة أولوية عالية كأطفال وشبان. «يا ابني لا تنس تعليمي، ويحفظ قلبك وصاياي، لأن طول الأيام، والسنة الحيات، والسلام، يزيدونك» (أمثال 3:1-2).

سيضيف الله بركته إذا بقينا في ترتيب الرئاسة هذا. كلما تعلمت كيف تكون تحت سلطة، كلما بُركت أكثر عندما تُؤسس بيتك. خطة الله لها بركات.

7) زواج تقوِي.

أف 5:21،22،24 تقول: «اخضعوا لبعضكم بعضًا في رهبة المسيح. يا نساء أخضعن لأنفسكن لرجالكن كما للرب... لذلك كما الكنيسة خاضعة للمسيح فهكذا يجب أن تكن النساء لأزواجهن في كل شيء».

انظروا أولًا إلى الآية 21، «اخضعوا بعضكم لبعضًا». هناك مزج يجب أن يحدث في بيت تقوِي. ينبغي أن يحدث هذا المزج في رهبة الله. إذا كنا نخضع بعضنا لبعض في رهبة الله، فسوف نُطيع الله لأننا نريد بركاته.

أف 5:22،24 «يا نساء أخضعن لأنفسكن لرجالكن كما للرب... لذلك كما الكنيسة خاضعة للمسيح فهكذا يجب أن تكن النساء لأزواجهن في كل شيء». أيها الشابات، يمكنكن الاعتماد على هذا: الخضوع للأب يساوي الخضوع للزوج. يمكنك أن تتدرّبي وأنت عزباء. هذا سيساعد في بناء شخصيتك. كونك امرأة متمردة وعنيدة لن تجلب بركة الله.

ويتابع في أف 5:25،28،29: «يا رجال أحبّوا نساءكم كما أحب المسيح أيضًا الكنيسة وأعطى نفسه لأجلها... كذلك يجب أن يحب الرجل زوجته كجسده، من يحب زوجته يحب نفسه. لأن لم يبغض أحد لحمه بل يعتني به ويحمله كما يفعل الرب بالكنيسة». أيها الشبان، هذا يقول إن على الأزواج أن يحبّوا زوجاتهم. فمن تعتقدون أن الله وضعه في حياتكم ليعدّكم على محبة الزوجة؟ أمكم! هل تريد أن تتعلّم كيف تحب زوجتك؟ تعلّم كيف تتفاهم مع أمك، أحب أمك، واهتم بها. هل تريد أن تتدرّب على محبة زوجتك المستقبلية؟ ابدأ بحب أمك.

الآية 33، «ولكن ليحب كل واحد منكم زوجته كما نفسه، لتكن المرأة مكرمة جدًا لزوجها». خطة الله تجلب البركات.

8) أن تكونا وارثين معًا نعمة الحياة.

1 بطرس 3:7 «كذلك أيها الرجال ساكنوا معهن بعِلم مُعطين شرفًا للمرأة كوعاء أضعف، كمشاركة في نعمة الحياة، لكي لا تتعطل صلواتكم». كأزواج، نعطي الشرف للزوجة. هي الوعاء الأضعف وهي التي تلد الأولاد! لقد مرت بتغييرات مؤلمة في حياتها. هي التي تتعب وتنفد طاقتها أسرع.

ويقول أيضًا: «يا رجال اسكنوا معهن بعِلم».

أيها الشبان، تعلّموا أن تفهموا أمكم وأخواتكم. سيساعدكم ذلك بعد أن تتزوجوا. لا تستنتجوا قائلين—آه، هذا مجرد نساء. لا، أنتم تريدون بركة الله. تعلّموا أن تعرفوهن وتفهموهن.

«كمشاركة في نعمة الحياة». يريدنا الله أن نكون وارثين معًا نعمة الحياة. إن لم نكن وارثين معًا نعمة الحياة، هل يمكن أن نكون وارثين مفصولين عن نعمة الحياة؟ لا أظن ذلك. يقول إننا ينبغي أن نكون وارثين معًا حتى لا تتعطل صلواتنا. فإذا كنا وارثين منفصلين، هل يمكن أن نقول إن صلواتنا ستتعرقل؟ نعم، ستتعرقل صلواتنا. أعطوا الشرف للزوجة كوعاء أضعف. كل قدرٍ تكسبه في هذا الجانب سيباركك لاحقًا فقط. إنه يستحق. خطة الله تجلب البركة.

9) بيت مبارك وآمن.

هذا ينبع جزئيًا من 1 بطرس 3:7، ولكن أيضًا من مزمور 144:12 «ليكن بنونا كالنباتات في شبابهن، لتكن بناتنا كركائز محفوفة بلمعان، على شبه قصر». نعمة الله على بيت آمن حيث توجد وحدة. حيث الأب يفهم الأم، حيث يهتم الأب بالأم. الأب يخدم ويوجه، موجود ليعطي الإرشاد بقلب حنون. خطة الله للرجل والمرأة — خطة الله تجلب البركات.

10) كمسيح والكنيسة.

«لذلك كما الكنيسة خاضعة للمسيح فهكذا يجب أن تكن النساء لأزواجهن في كل شيء. أيها الرجال أحبّوا نساءكم كما أحب المسيح الكنيسة وأعطى نفسه لأجلها، لكي يقدسها بعد غسل الماء بالكلمة، لكي يقدمها لنفسه كنيسة مجيدة غير مخطوفة ولا مجعدة ولا شيء من هذا القبيل، بل تكون مقدسة وبلا لوم. هكذا يجب أن يحب الرجال نساءهم كنُفوسهم. من يحب زوجته يحب نفسه. لأنه لم يبغض أحد جسده بل يُغذيه ويحتضنه كما يفعل الرب بالكنيسة» (أف 5:24-29).

«يا رجال أحبّوا نساءكم كما أحب المسيح الكنيسة وأعطى نفسه لأجلها». الله يبحث عن رجال مستعدين أن يهبوا حياتهم. أيها الشبان العزاب، هل أنتم مستعدون أن تلبّوا النداء وتُعطوا حياتكم؟ هذا نداء سامٍ من الله. إنها خطة الله.

أيها الشبان، هل أنتم مستعدون أن تضعوا حياتكم، جدولكم، وتلك الأشياء المستقلة التي تحبون فعلها؟ هل أنتم مستعدون أن تكونوا صبورين، رقيقين، وفاهمين؟ هل أنتم مستعدون أن تفقدوا النوم وتستمروا حتى وإن شعرتم بالتعب؟ هل أنتم مستعدون أن تظلوا هادئين ولا تتفاعل بردود فعل أثناء الظروف المجهِدة؟ هل أنتم مستعدون أن تقودوا وتهدوا زوجةً وأولادًا، نفوسًا أبدية، خلال هذه الحياة؟

لكن ندائي أن تتطوعوا وتقولوا: «أنا مستعد أن أكرس نفسي لكلمة الله، لمشيئة الله، لخطة الله، وسأعطي حياتي. أنا مستعد أن أضعها على المذبح». أعطانا يسوع حياته من أجلنا، ويُقارن هنا الزواج بالكنيسة وبالمسيح.

كما أن هناك حاجة لأمهات خاضعات ومُسلِمات للسلطة. أمهات لا يتبعن حركات تحرير المرأة في زماننا بل يرضين بأن يكنَّ حافظات للبيت.

أيها الشابات، هل أنتن مستعدات أن تتجندن؟ هل ستعطين قلبك لتُهدَي وتُرشد؟ هل أنتن مستعدات أن تتبعن وتخضعن بفرح لسلطتك؟ هل أنتن مستعدات أن تخدمن وتبدين مهدرات لأسرتكن؟ هل أنتن مستعدات أن تخدمن وتبدين مهدرات من أجل عائلتكن؟ إن تزوجتن يوماً ما، ستكون أسرتكن أنتنّ من تخدمن لأجلها. هل أنتن مستعدات أن تتحمّلن الألم والانزعاج؟ هل أنتن مستعدات أن تكن معينًا، تعطين نفسك لحموله ورؤيته؟

ولكن إذ ننظر إلى خطة الله وبركاته، أيها الشباب أنتم تريدون بركة الله! لكن هذا يعني أن عليكم أن تتخذوا خيارات تتوافق معها. انهضوا واتخذوا قرارات تؤدي إلى النضج. النضج يأتي بعملية السعي وراء الله. التزموا في قلوبكم أن تفتحوا أنفسكم لمبادئ وبركات الله. أشجعكم أن تسيروا مع الله، أن تتمتعوا بعلاقة مع يسوع المسيح، وأن تفعلوا ذلك بخشوع.

اطلبوا طابع المسيح واعملوا ذلك عن قصد. من السهل جدًا أن نعيش حياتنا كيفما اتفق. لكن إذا اتخذنا قرارات عن قصد، فستقودنا إلى مكان! تلك القرارات مهمة. افعلوا الأمور وفقًا لخطة الله.

لله خطة للرجل والمرأة وله خطة لك.

Eight-year-old Jamin wasn’t very smart. Or at least that’s what his older brother told him. Almost daily, brother Kenny found ways to remind Jamin of his shortcomings and laugh at his blunders.

“Jamin, you will never be smart”, Kenny said. Deep inside Jamin felt resigned to a life of muddled trip-ups. Would he always be clumsy? Would he always say things wrong? That’s what Kenny said.

Jamin believed Kenny’s lectures with wide-eyed belief. Kenny was three years older than him, so he must be right. Very well, then Jamin would be simple. Kenny would be smart. Life was not fair. Dad and Mom disliked Kenny’s proud talk and punished him whenever they walked in on one of his speeches. But Kenny had a way of avoiding earshot. So he continued mocking Jamin.

Grandma Otto watched these trials from her rocker on the porch. She was a quiet old lady.

“Jamin, do you know where Kenny is?” Mom asked with a smile. “It’s almost supper time.”

“He went to check his coyote traps. I’ll go find him.”

There was a chill in the air as he tramped up over the lawn, and the sun was growing old as he crossed the border of the woods. The fleeting shadows scurried over the hills. The chill deepened as he stumped further in. He breathed the rich air and followed Kenny’s trail. Eventually, the trail would end up in a meadow, but Jamin hoped he would find Kenny before he had to go that far. The various traps had been checked already, so Jamin knew Kenny had come this way. Jamin trudged on resolutely. His golden head caught the tired beams that fled from the sun as they flickered through the trees. And soon those too had faded leaving behind the musky smell of the woods. The fall webworms had been at work, and their web curtains shuttered from branches overhead.

At length, as the trees subdued and thinned, and the meadow appeared Jamin knew this was the end of his brother’s trap route. If Kenny wasn’t here, he wouldn’t know where else to look.

But Kenny was there. As Jamin clumped into the meadow, he could see a frustrated heap to his right. The heap’s voice had a familiar ring. The heap’s face was lit in pain. The heap was Kenny. “Are you alright? What happened?” Jamin felt strange, seeing Kenny scrunched in the dirt. Kenny was smart. “Did you step in a trap?”

“Yes, Jamin. I..I wasn’t looking where I was going. Help me. Please.”

Jamin bent and found an ankle firmly held in the jaws of a steel trap. Darkness stained the ground around Kenny. Quickly, Jamin’s strong arms pried open the jaws. Kenny reeled free. “Can you walk?”

“Yes. I think so. If you support me, I can hobble along.”

“Dad and Mom will be worried. We’ve missed supper.”

Sure enough, as the brothers hobbled back through the woods, they heard the long calling of their father. Jamin called back, and he was by their side in a moment, seeing the ankle and scooping up Kenny like a hurt sheep. The odd little band hurried home, and the screen door banged shut as Dad swept across the porch. Jamin went to the wash house and scrubbed his hands. He headed for the front door.

“Jamin.” It was Grandma. The porch light showed her in her old rocker. A heavy comforter lay on her shoulders.

“Yes, Grandma?”

“Do you think you are not very smart?”

“That’s what Kenny says.” Jamin squirmed.

“You were strong enough to open the trap, and Kenny wasn’t. You were brave enough to find him in the dark. Lots of young boys wouldn’t be.” Jamin was silent. Grandma Otto rocked some more, then smiled. “God made you the way you are for a reason, Jamin. He made Kenny the way he is for a reason. He has a plan for you, and a place only you can fill, you know.”

Jamin turned and walked into the warm kitchen. He was smiling.

Jamin, de oito anos, não era muito inteligente. Ou pelo menos era isso que o irmão mais velho lhe dizia. Quase diariamente, o irmão Kenny encontrava maneiras de lembrar Jamin de suas falhas e rir de seus tropeços.

“Jamin, você nunca será inteligente”, dizia Kenny. Lá no fundo, Jamin sentia-se resignado a uma vida de confusos enganos. Será que ele seria sempre desajeitado? Será que sempre diria as coisas erradas? Foi o que Kenny disse.

Jamin acreditava nas lições de Kenny com uma fé de olhos arregalados. Kenny era três anos mais velho do que ele, portanto devia estar certo. Muito bem, então Jamin seria simples. Kenny seria esperto. A vida não era justa. Papai e Mamãe desgostavam da conversa orgulhosa de Kenny e o puniam sempre que os surpreendiam em uma de suas falas. Mas Kenny tinha um jeito de evitar ser ouvido. Assim, continuou zombando de Jamin.

A avó Otto observava essas provações da sua cadeira de balanço na varanda. Era uma senhora quieta.

“Jamin, você sabe onde está o Kenny?” perguntou a mãe com um sorriso. “Está quase na hora do jantar.”

“Ele foi checar as armadilhas de coiote. Eu vou procurá‑lo.”

Havia um arrepio no ar enquanto ele atravessava o gramado, e o sol estava envelhecendo ao cruzar a beira da floresta. As sombras fugidias corriam sobre as colinas. O frio aumentou à medida que ele avançava. Respirou o ar denso e seguiu a trilha de Kenny. Eventualmente, a trilha terminaria em um prado, mas Jamin esperava encontrar Kenny antes de ter que ir tão longe. As várias armadilhas já haviam sido verificadas, então Jamin sabia que Kenny passara por ali. Jamin caminhou resoluto. Sua cabeça dourada apanhava os raios cansados que fugiam do sol enquanto tremulavam através das árvores. E logo esses também se extinguiram, deixando o cheiro musgoso da mata. As lagartas tecelãs do outono tinham trabalhado, e suas cortinas de teia pendiam dos galhos acima.

Ao fim, conforme as árvores se acalmaram e rarearam, e o prado apareceu, Jamin soube que ali terminava a rota das armadilhas do irmão. Se o Kenny não estivesse ali, ele não saberia onde mais procurar.

Mas Kenny estava ali. Quando Jamin entrou no prado, viu um amontoado frustrado à sua direita. A voz do amontoado tinha um timbre familiar. O rosto do amontoado estava iluminado pela dor. O amontoado era Kenny. “Você está bem? O que aconteceu?” Jamin sentiu‑se estranho ao ver Kenny encolhido na terra. Kenny era esperto. “Você pisou numa armadilha?”

“Sim, Jamin. Eu… eu não estava olhando por onde andava. Me ajude. Por favor.”

Jamin se curvou e encontrou um tornozelo firmemente preso nas mandíbulas de uma armadilha de aço. A escuridão manchas rodeava o chão ao redor de Kenny. Rapidamente, os braços fortes de Jamin abriram as mandíbulas. Kenny recuou livre. “Você consegue andar?”

“Sim. Acho que sim. Se você me apoiar, consigo mancar.”

“Papai e Mamãe vão ficar preocupados. Perdemos o jantar.”

De fato, enquanto os irmãos mancavam de volta pela mata, ouviram a longa chamada do pai. Jamin respondeu, e ele estava ao lado deles em um instante, vendo o tornozelo e pegando Kenny como uma ovelha ferida. A estranha turminha apressou‑se para casa, e a porta de tela bateu enquanto o pai atravessava a varanda. Jamin foi até a casa de lavar e esfregou as mãos. Dirigiu‑se à porta da frente.

“Jamin.” Era a avó. A luz da varanda a mostrava em sua velha cadeira de balanço. Um pesado cobertor descansava sobre seus ombros.

“Sim, vovó?”

“Você acha que não é muito inteligente?”

“É isso que o Kenny diz.” Jamin se contorceu.

“Você teve força suficiente para abrir a armadilha, e Kenny não teve. Você teve coragem de encontrá‑lo no escuro. Muitos meninos jovens não teriam.” Jamin ficou em silêncio. A avó Otto balançou mais um pouco a cadeira e sorriu. “Deus fez você do jeito que é por um motivo, Jamin. Ele fez Kenny do jeito que é por um motivo. Ele tem um plano para você, e um lugar que só você pode ocupar, sabe.”

Jamin virou‑se e entrou na cozinha quente. Estava sorrindo.

Our Father’s world is a world unspoiled by human invention and intervention. While sin and technology have warped and stolen many lovely things from the human race, there abide still a few that remain unmarred by civilization. Little children in the fresh innocence of their unsoiled morning top the ranks as a bit of heaven on earth and call all observers heavenward. Another is the fowl of the air as prescribed in Genesis. Paul pleaded with the Corinthian church, “Doth not nature itself teach you?” We are exhorted to consider the lilies, the ravens, and the grass of the field. Each of these bears a significant dimension of the eternal God in their existence and gives us definition to their Creator. Perhaps all of nature can give us snapshots into heavenly places if we had the time and eyes to observe it.

Birds hold a unique place in God’s creation, for their sphere is in the heavens. Man may mount on the wings of a plane and evade the lower earth for a few hours, but the heavens will never be a place of his common dominion. The birds are a picture of a heavenly race, for they are at home there. They are a natural representation of the saints and angels of God and so we do well to give them due attention. While there may be dozens of lessons to be drawn from these vessels of grace and beauty, one of the most prominent and outstanding virtues will be observed in the song that they raise. Many animals dwelling on the earth are virtually mute. Of the ones that do speak, it is often to threaten or express complaint. “Doth the wild ass bray when he hath grass? Or loweth the ox over his fodder?” (Job 6:5). When they are happy and content, they have no message to convey. The dog barks at an intruder to drive him away, while the cat mews for attention. They speak when they are threatened or dissatisfied, in fear or in pain. Similarly, the earthly human shares its nature with the mammals of the field.

Birds are diverse. They exercise their joyous vocals so much that they are the epitome of happiness. The expression “happy as a lark” is so common a term that it is used by people who have never even ventured to the meadow to see or hear a lark. While some may inform us that these songs are mere mating calls and have little to do with their feelings, we cannot escape the inner conviction that, whether mating or not, these birds delight in bearing a jubilant expression of joy and we do well to let them teach us. “Is any merry? Let him sing psalms” (James 5:13). The birds do this incessantly and it seems impossible to draw any other conclusion but that they are happy while doing so. Wander near the nest of a swallow and you will find that they have ways of expressing depreciation as well. The killdeer also has no qualms with expressing rash disfavor to those who intrude their domain, but these are not to be mistaken as songs. The singing birds are a beautiful painted picture of the saints and angels of God.

How little knowledge of heaven is committed to our understanding. The scenes of heavens described and laid out before us in Revelations can hardly bring our finite minds into its infinite realm. One dimension that we can connect with is that it is a place filled with singing. Little wonder, for it is the culminating end of the contented and joy-filled saints of God, and there they will sing a new song. Nearly every scene at the throne in Revelations is marked by some dimension of praise. “And he hath put a new song in my mouth, even praise unto our God” (Ps 40:3). On 22 occasions, the Scriptures reiterate the phrase, I will sing.

It is the nature of the birds to sing. It is their waking thought as morning guilds the sky, and it flows from within them like a fountain. Not all of their songs are alike. Some are elaborate in their duration, meter, and pitch, while others are plain. Some merely chirp with a merry heart. The robin opens up the choir in early spring, but his song is soon surpassed in beauty by the song sparrow and again by the rose-breasted grosbeak. The song of the wren trumps them all for longevity and vibrancy. The canary sings in a cage, while the nightingale sings in the dark. The robins sing in the rain. The buntings fill in the heat of the day when other birds are silent. As diverse as their song may be, they all commonly burst forth in exuberant happiness. It is here that they shall instruct us.

“Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord” (Eph 5:19). The advent of Christ was marked by the angelic host announcing peace and goodwill toward men. All those who will bear His name must deliver the same tidings. In John 4, we happen upon the scene at Jacob’s well, where Christ asks the woman for a drink. Her reply seems to bear a tinge of bitterness. “Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.” Though she esteemed herself as a spiritual person and willingly followed Him into religious discourse, she had no song. Like the well that they speak over, her water was buried deep below the surface and how laborious the effort to bring it forth. Christ offers another alternative. “But the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life” (John 4:14).

The well of Christ is an artesian well. One needs neither pitcher nor labor to draw it out, for it spews forth abundantly on its own accord. While Christ is probably speaking of the Spirit as in John 7:38, surely this may be just as applicable to a joy-laden heart. What is a more apt outpouring to flow from a Christ-inspired wellspring than the rapture of a song? “Behold, my servants shall sing for joy of heart” (Is 65:14). Now this should all seem plain enough to understand and easy enough to do but, alas, we find we have a constant and persistent adversary who seeks to thwart our song. We are not unaware of his devices...

Sin. Not all birds sing. There are some whose visage is black as sin. These only seem to screech and scream and are no example for the saints of God to emulate. The babbling noise we hear emanating from many passing vehicles certainly parallels the songs of such foul fowl. “Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen, and is become the habitation of devils, and the hold of every foul spirit, and a cage of every unclean and hateful bird” (Rev 18:2). These abundant creatures are the fallen spirits, the fowls waiting to devour the seed sown by the wayside. Of such are the worthless blackbirds, starlings, and grackles. The crows show themselves also at the roadside, feeding on rotting carcasses. Often you will find them in large numbers feeding themselves on the corn the farmer painstakingly planted for himself. So transgresses the selfish soul in his pursuit of happiness, feeding gleefully on the calamity of another and exploiting their sin. He bears no song, for his day is constantly clouded by the misdeeds of others who cross his path.

Neglect. The cowbird is also black (the female is brown/gray). She will be found sitting on a high vantage, shamelessly calling to her lovers by her shrill screeching. She then has the audacity to lay her egg in another bird’s nest, forcing them to raise her offspring. This is certainly a fitting emblem for a good number of females in our day. Though justified by circumstances, these women care not for their own, but are products of neglect. They have no lullaby to share with their young, for they have escorted them to the nest of another while her mind is preoccupied with work and business. “But thou art he that took me out of the womb: thou didst make me hope when I was upon my mother’s breasts” (Ps 22:9). No doubt that the singing mother can implant copious songs in her infant and set the stage for a happy and hope-filled life. While we may show mercy to a woman in dire circumstances, the major song of modern women bears chords that are but dissident and melancholy. These are stopped-up wells like unto the wells that Isaac found upon his return to Gerar. The Philistines “had filled them with earth” (Gen 26:15). So run the spiritually neglected homes of many families today, who pack their schedules so full of earthly commitments that they have no time to spend an hour in song together. If the birds stopped singing, would they even notice?

Ingratitude. Find a soul bathed in unthankfulness, and you will find a soul without a song. If the canary were to refuse to sing in captivity, few of us would ever have heard his rollicking melody. “We hanged our harps upon the willows in the midst thereof. For there they that carried us away captive required of us a song; and they that wasted us required of us mirth, saying, Sing us one of the songs of Zion. How shall we sing the LORD’S song in a strange land?” (Ps 137:2-4). God’s people had been instructed by Jeremiah to build houses, plant gardens, and raise families. “… And seek the peace of the city whither I have caused you to be carried away captives, and pray unto the LORD for it: for in the peace thereof shall ye have peace” (Jer. 29:5-7). But they could see no worth in it. With their eyes fixed upon the dismal scene around them, they lost their song. Israel had within its history a rich tradition of song. Their singing erupted at the passage of the Red Sea in the days of Jehoshaphat and had been known to defeat armies. Earthly discomfort is no excuse to withhold gratitude, for our God reigns, and we are His children. Such were the conditions of the Philippian prison where two jailbirds, Paul and Silas, opened the concert at midnight and rocked the corridors with their joyful singing.

When we open our mouths and stretch our vocals in praise, we enact the grace of God. We join the faithful choir alongside Miriam, Deborah, and Hannah, and blend harmoniously with Moses, David, Paul, and Barnabas. At evening, we sing with our Lord and His disciples after supper, and with legions of angels “giving glory to God in the highest.” If that isn’t enough, perhaps we should consider rising at early dawn and singing with the innumerable hosts of our feathered friends who are thankful for God’s loving providence. “Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord … And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men” (Col 3:16, 23).

Ulimwengu wa Baba yetu ni ulimwengu usiobovu kutokana na uvumbuzi na uingiliaji wa binadamu. Ingawa dhambi na teknolojia vimepindua na kuiba mambo mengi mazuri kutoka kwa jamaa ya binadamu, bado zipo baadhi ambazo hazijakandamizwa na ustaarabu. Watoto wadogo katika uzuri mchanga wa asubuhi yao isiyochafuka wamo juu katika orodha kama kipande kidogo cha mbinguni hapa duniani na huwaita watazamaji wote kuelekea mbinguni. Kingine ni ndege wa angani kama ilivyoelezwa katika Mwanzo. Paulo aliomba kwa kanisa la Korintho, “Doth not nature itself teach you?” Tunasukumwa kutafakari juu ya maua ya lili, tai na nyasi za uwanja. Kila moja ya haya ina kipengele muhimu cha Mungu wa milele katika kuwepo kwake na hutupatia ufafanuzi kuhusu Muumbaji wao. Labda asili yote inaweza kutupa picha za maeneo ya mbinguni ikiwa tungetokuwa na muda na macho ya kuizizia.

Ndege wanashikilia nafasi ya kipekee katika uumbaji wa Mungu, kwa kuwa wenzake ni katika mbingu. Mtu anaweza kupanda kwenye ndege au kwa mabawa ya ndege na kuepuka dunia ya chini kwa saa chache, lakini mbingu hazitawahi kuwa eneo la mamlaka yake ya kawaida. Ndege ni picha ya uzazi wa mbinguni, kwa kuwa wapo nyumbani palipo. Wao ni uwakilishi wa kawaida wa watakatifu na malaika wa Mungu na hivyo ni vema kuwapa kipaumbele. Ingawa huenda kuna mafundisho mamia yanayoweza kuchukuliwa kutoka kwa vyombo hivi vya neema na uzuri, mojawapo ya wema unaoonekana zaidi utaonekana katika wimbo wanaonilea. Wanyama wengi wanaoishi duniani kwa kawaida ni kimya. Kwa wale wanaoongea, mara nyingi ni kuonya au kuonyesha malalamiko. “Doth the wild ass bray when he hath grass? Or loweth the ox over his fodder?” (Job 6:5). Wakiwa na furaha na kuridhika, hawana ujumbe wa kusambaza. Mbwa huwauwa mduku kwa mgeni kumzuilia, wakati paka anakatia sauti kuomba umakini. Hawaongea wanapothibitishwa au kukosa kuridhika, kwa hofu au kwa maumivu. Vivyo hivyo, mwanadamu wa hapa duniani anashiriki tabia ya wanyama wengine wa shamba.

Ndege ni wengi na wanatofautiana. Wanatumia sauti zao za furaha kiasi kwamba wao ni mfano wa furaha. Kauli “furaha kama shujaa wa shambani” ni istilahi ya kawaida kiasi kwamba hutumika na watu ambao hawajawahi hata kwenda shambani kuona au kusikia shujaa wa shambani. Wakati wengine watushauri kwamba nyimbo hizi ni tu vishindo vya kugeuza wapenzi na hazihusiani sana na hisia zao, hatuwezi kuepuka imani ya ndani kwamba, kama walivyokuwa wanatafuta mpenzi au la, ndege hawa hufurahia kutoa shauku ya furaha na ni vema tuwazia kuwajifunza. “Is any merry? Let him sing psalms” (James 5:13). Ndege hufanya hivi bila kuacha na inaonekana haiwezekani kutoa hitimisho lingine isipokuwa kwamba wanakuwa wakifurahia wakati wa kufanya hivyo. Tembea karibu ndege wa makalacha na utagundua kwamba wana njia za kuonyesha dharau pia. Killdeer pia hana aibu kuonyesha chuki ya ghafla kwa wale wanaovuruga eneo lao, lakini haya yasichukuliwe kama nyimbo. Ndege wanaopiga nyimbo ni picha nzuri iliyopambwa ya watakatifu na malaika wa Mungu.

Ni kiasi gani cha maarifa kuhusu mbinguni kimewekwa katika uelewa wetu. Mandhari za mbinguni zilizoelezewa na kuwekwa mbele yetu katika Ufunuo hayawezi kuleta kwa urahisi akili zetu za kikomo katika ufalme wake usio na mipaka. Kipengele kimoja ambacho tunaweza kuunganishwa nacho ni kwamba ni mahali palipojaa kuimba. Hakuna mshangao, kwa kuwa ni mwisho wa watakatifu wenye kuridhika na ambao wamejazwa na furaha, na huko wataimba wimbo mpya. Karibu kila mandhari kando ya kiti cha enzi katika Ufunuo ina alama ya kipengele fulani cha sifa. “And he hath put a new song in my mouth, even praise unto our God” (Ps 40:3). Mara 22, Maandiko yanarudia kifungu, I will sing.

Ni asili ya ndege kuimba. Ni wazo lao wa kufungua macho wakati asubuhi inavyopendeza anga, na hutiririsha kutoka ndani yao kama chemchemi. Sio nyimbo zao zote zinafanana. Baadhi ni zenye utaraji mkubwa kwa muda, kipimo na sauti, wakati nyingine ni za kawaida. Baadhi tu hupiga kelele kwa moyo wa furaha. Robin huanzisha kwaya mapema msimu wa kuchipua, lakini wimbo wake huharibika haraka katika uzuri na song sparrow na tena na rose-breasted grosbeak. Wimbo wa wren huwa juu yao wote kwa urefu na uhai. Canary huimba ndani ya kifungo, wakati nightingale huimba gizani. Robins huimba mvulani. Buntings hujazana wakati wa joto la mchana wakati ndege wengine wanakuwa kimya. Iwapo wimbo wao unaweza kutofautiana, wote kwa pamoja hurushwa kwa furaha isiyodhibitiwa. Hapa ndipo watatufundisha.

“Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord” (Eph 5:19). Kuja kwa Kristo kulionyeshwa na jeshi la malaika kutangaza amani na wema kwa wanadamu. Wote walioitwayo kubeba Jina lake lazima walete habari hizo. Katika Yohana sura ya 4, tunakutana na tukio karibu na kisima cha Yakobo, ambako Kristo anamuomba mwanamke maji. Jibu lake linaonekana kuwa na ladha ya uchungu. “Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.” Ingawa alijiona kuwa mtu wa kiroho na kwa hiari kumfuata Yule katika mazungumzo ya kidini, hakuwa na wimbo. Kama kisima walichokuwa wakiongea, maji yake yalizikwa chini ya uso na ilikuwaje kazi ngumu kuifichua. Kristo anatoa mbadala mwingine. “But the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life” (John 4:14).

Kisima cha Kristo ni kisima cha artesian. Hakuna haja ya jugi wala kazi ya kuchota, kwa kuwa kinapiga mwando kwa wingi kwa hiari yake mwenyewe. Ingawa Kristo huenda alikuwa akizungumza kuhusu Roho kama ilivyo Yohana 7:38, bila shaka hili linaweza kuweza kutumika kwa moyoni iliyojazwa furaha pia. Nini kinatiririka kwa uzuri kutoka chemchemi inayochochewa na Kristo isipokuwa msongamano wa wimbo? “Behold, my servants shall sing for joy of heart” (Is 65:14). Hili linapaswa kuonekana wazi kuelewa na kuwa rahisi kufanya lakini, apana, tunapata adui wetu wa kudumu na mwenye msukumo anayejaribu kuzuia wimbo wetu. Hatuwezi kusahau viwango vyake...

Dhambi. Sio ndege wote huimba. Kuna baadhi ambao uso wao ni mweusi kama dhambi. Hawa wanaonekana kupiga kelele na kulia tu na si mfano kwa watakatifu wa Mungu kuiga. Kelele za uvurugu tunazosikia zikiwasili kutoka kwa magari mengi zinatafananisha nyimbo za ndege waliochafu kama hao. “Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen, and is become the habitation of devils, and the hold of every foul spirit, and a cage of every unclean and hateful bird” (Rev 18:2). Viumbe hawa wengi ni roho zilizoporomoka, ndege wanaosubiri kula mbegu zilizopandwa kando ya njia. Miongoni mwao ni blackbirds wasio na thamani, starlings, na grackles. Kunguru pia wanaonekana kando ya barabara, wakila na miili iliyochakaa. Mara nyingi watakukuta kwa wingi wakijikizia mahindi aliyopanda mkulima kwa bidii mwenyewe. Hivyo nafsi mwenye kujiletea dhulma anavyovuruga katika kutafuta furaha, akila kwa raha kwenye maafa ya mwingine na kuchochea dhambi yao. Hana wimbo, kwa kuwa siku yake imejaa mawingu kutokana na mabaya ya wengine waliomkuta njiani.

Uupuzi. Cowbird pia ni mweusi (kike ni kahawia/ kijivu). Ataonekana amekaa juu katika nafasi ya juu, bila aibu akiwaita wapenzi wake kwa kelele kali. Kisha ana ujasiri wa kuweka yai lake kwenye kiota cha ndege mwingine, kuwaweka walifunze watoto wake. Hili ni nembo inayofaa kwa idadi nzuri ya wanawake wa wakati wetu. Ingawa wanaweza kueleweka kwa mazingira, wanawake hawa hawajali wake wao wenyewe, bali ni matokeo ya uupuzi. Hawana wimbo wa kulala kushiriki na watoto wao, kwa kuwa wamewachukua hadi kwa kiota cha mwingine wakati akili yao imefungwa na kazi na biashara. “But thou art he that took me out of the womb: thou didst make me hope when I was upon my mother’s breasts” (Ps 22:9). Hakika mama mwenye kuimba anaweza kupandia mtoto wake nyimbo nyingi na kuweka hatua ya maisha yenye furaha na tumaini. Ingawa tunaweza kuwa na huruma kwa mwanamke katika hali mbaya, wimbo mkuu wa wanawake wa kisasa una mizizi ambayo ni tofauti na huzuni. Haya ni visima vimeziba kama vile visima ambavyo Isaki alipata aliporudi Gerari. Wafilisti “had filled them with earth” (Gen 26:15). Hivyo zinavyokwenda nyumba zilizoachwa kiroho za familia nyingi leo, ambazo zimejazwa ratiba zao kwa shughuli za kidunia kiasi kwamba hawana muda wa kutumia saa moja kuimba pamoja. Ikiwa ndege wangekoma kuimba, je, wangeweza hata kugundua?

Kutojali shukrani. Ukutane na nafsi iliyofunikwa na kutokwenda shukrani, na utapata nafsi bila wimbo. Iwapo canary angekataa kuimba huku akiwa kifungoni, wachache wetu tungeweza kusikia melodi yake ya furaha. “We hanged our harps upon the willows in the midst thereof. For there they that carried us away captive required of us a song; and they that wasted us required of us mirth, saying, Sing us one of the songs of Zion. How shall we sing the LORD’S song in a strange land?” (Ps 137:2-4). Watu wa Mungu waliwaamriwa na Yeremia kujenga nyumba, kupanda bustani, na kulea familia. “… And seek the peace of the city whither I have caused you to be carried away captives, and pray unto the LORD for it: for in the peace thereof shall ye have peace” (Jer. 29:5-7). Lakini hawakuona thamani yake. Wakitazama kwa macho matukio ya kusikitisha yakizunguka, walikosa wimbo wao. Israeli ilikuwa na ndani ya historia yake utamaduni tajiri wa wimbo. Wimbo wao ulilipuka wakati wa kuvuka Bahari Nyekundu katika siku za Jehoshaphat na ulikuwa maarufu kushinda majeshi. Mfadhaiko wa dunia si sababu ya kukataa kutoa shukrani, kwa kuwa Mungu wetu afalme, na sisi ni watoto wake. Hivyo zilikuwa hali za gerezani za Filipi ambapo wafungwa wawili, Paulo na Silasi, walifungua tamthilia katikati ya usiku na kuwazungusha mwanya kwa nyimbo zao za furaha.

Tunapofungua midomo yetu na kupanua sauti zetu kwa sifa, tunafanya neema ya Mungu. Tunaungana na kwaya ya waja watiwa imani sambamba na Miriam, Deborah, na Hannah, na kuoanisha vizuri na Musa, Daudi, Paulo, na Barnaba. Nyakati za jioni, tunaimba na Bwana wetu na wanafunzi wake baada ya chakula, na na majeshi ya malaika “giving glory to God in the highest.” Ikiwa hilo halitoshi, labda tunapaswa kufikiria kuinuka alfajiri na kuimba pamoja na jeshi lisilohesabika la marafiki zetu wenye manyoya ambao wamejaa shukrani kwa ulinzi wa upendo wa Mungu. “Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord … And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men” (Col 3:16, 23).

The urgency of the last minute is something that many homemakers deal with regularly. No matter how organized we are, sometimes we put off tasks because we dislike them or wait until we are under pressure.

Habitual procrastination potentially leads to higher levels of stress. Maybe I’m odd, but it is hard for me to stay calm and collected when the pressure is mounting. By the time the last minute things are completed I’m too exhausted to enjoy the planned event.

Toothaches and Road Trips

It is a mystery to me why a family member ends up in a dentist chair a day or two before we leave on a trip. Maybe it hasn’t happened as often as I think, but the frustration of an unplanned trip to the dentist at an inopportune time is riveted in my mind. Now I schedule an imaginary appointment before a trip. If it is not a dental emergency, some other issue is bound to fill that time slot.

Deadlines are a normal part of life. Without them we would be unmotivated, and our days would lack purpose. Interruptions are also a normal part of life. They constantly give an unpredictable twist to our days and weeks. If we let too many tasks wait until the last minute, interruptions and deadlines collide, and chaos reigns.

Change the Last-Minute Scenario

Deadlines and interruptions cannot be eliminated but we can limit last-minute tasks. Sometimes it takes some honest looking back to figure out what caused our stress. Often, we blame it on interruptions and fail to realize that poor planning or procrastination might have been the culprit.

For example, if guests are coming and we plan to wash windows and make a dessert along with a dozen more tasks on the day of their arrival, there is no room for disruptions. From experience, we know interruptions will come. So, isn’t it better to “plan” for a bee sting and a stubbed toe?

Why not schedule window washing and dessert another day? That might mean some fingerprints on the windows and a simpler dessert, but isn’t that better than a great deal of stress at the last minute?

Do some tasks ahead of time

Deciding early in the day what to make for supper and packing the diaper bag in advance are little things that can make a big difference at the last minute. When our children were young, I started packing suitcases a day before a trip versus the day of leaving. I was better able to cope with the last-minute rush if that job was out of the way.

Do the most important tasks first

This approach gives freedom to skip jobs of lesser importance when up against a time crunch.

Sometimes not everything on the task list is of equal value. Dropping a task is difficult for a perfectionist, but it is possible to develop new habits.

Break work into smaller bits

Sometimes the enormity of a task makes it seem too huge to start. Break down the large task into smaller components. Completing a smaller task is much more manageable. Deep cleaning my kitchen is a task that I do not enjoy. If my planner says, “deep-clean kitchen,” it’s easy to ignore.

But if my planner says, “clean appliances, wipe out cupboards, and wash windows,” it seems more doable.

There are so many joyful events in life; why be hassled by procrastination? Give yourself the liberty to live life differently. A few minor changes can make the biggest difference between a blessed or stressed last minute.

Η επείγουσα ανάγκη της τελευταίας στιγμής είναι κάτι με το οποίο πολλές νοικοκυρές ασχολούνται τακτικά. Όσο οργανωμένες κι αν είμαστε, μερικές φορές αναβάλλουμε εργασίες επειδή δεν μας αρέσουν ή περιμένουμε μέχρι να νιώσουμε την πίεση.

Η συνήθης αναβλητικότητα μπορεί να οδηγήσει σε υψηλότερα επίπεδα άγχους. Ίσως να είμαι παράξενη, αλλά μου είναι δύσκολο να παραμείνω ήρεμη και συγκροτημένη όταν αυξάνεται η πίεση. Μέχρι να ολοκληρωθούν τα πράγματα της τελευταίας στιγμής είμαι τόσο εξαντλημένη που δεν απολαμβάνω το προγραμματισμένο γεγονός.

Πονόδοντοι και ταξίδια με αυτοκίνητο

Μου είναι μυστήριο γιατί κάποιο μέλος της οικογένειας καταλήγει στην οδοντιατρική καρέκλα μία ή δύο μέρες πριν φύγουμε για ταξίδι. Ίσως δεν έχει συμβεί τόσο συχνά όσο νομίζω, αλλά η απογοήτευση ενός απρογραμμάτιστου ραντεβού στον οδοντίατρο σε ακατάλληλη στιγμή έχει χαραχτεί στο μυαλό μου. Τώρα προγραμματίζω ένα φανταστικό ραντεβού πριν από ένα ταξίδι. Αν δεν πρόκειται για οδοντιατρική έκτακτη ανάγκη, κάποιο άλλο θέμα θα γεμίσει αυτό το κενό στο πρόγραμμα.

Οι προθεσμίες είναι ένα φυσιολογικό κομμάτι της ζωής. Χωρίς αυτές θα ήμασταν χωρίς κίνητρο και οι μέρες μας θα έλειπαν από σκοπό. Οι παρεμβολές επίσης είναι φυσιολογικό κομμάτι της ζωής. Δίνουν διαρκώς μια απρόβλεπτη στροφή στις μέρες και τις εβδομάδες μας. Αν αφήσουμε πάρα πολλές εργασίες για την τελευταία στιγμή, οι παρεμβολές και οι προθεσμίες συγκρούονται και βασιλεύει το χάος.

Αλλάξτε το σενάριο της τελευταίας στιγμής

Δεν μπορούμε να εξαλείψουμε τις προθεσμίες και τις παρεμβολές, αλλά μπορούμε να περιορίσουμε τις εργασίες της τελευταίας στιγμής. Μερικές φορές χρειάζεται ειλικρινής ανασκόπηση για να καταλάβουμε τι προκάλεσε το άγχος μας. Συχνά το ρίχνουμε στις παρεμβολές και δεν συνειδητοποιούμε ότι ο κακός προγραμματισμός ή η αναβλητικότητα μπορεί να ήταν ο ένοχος.

Για παράδειγμα, αν έρχονται επισκέπτες και σκοπεύουμε να πλύνουμε τα παράθυρα και να φτιάξουμε ένα γλυκό μαζί με δώδεκα ακόμη εργασίες την ημέρα της άφιξής τους, δεν υπάρχει χώρος για απρόοπτα. Από την εμπειρία γνωρίζουμε ότι θα υπάρξουν παρεμβολές. Άρα, δεν είναι καλύτερο να «προγραμματίσουμε» ένα τσίμπημα μέλισσας και ένα χτύπημα στο δάχτυλο του ποδιού;

Γιατί να μην προγραμματίσουμε το πλύσιμο των παραθύρων και το γλυκό για άλλη μέρα; Αυτό μπορεί να σημαίνει μερικά δαχτυλικά αποτυπώματα στα παράθυρα και ένα απλούστερο γλυκό, αλλά δεν είναι αυτό καλύτερο από πολύ άγχος την τελευταία στιγμή;

Κάντε μερικές εργασίες νωρίτερα

Η απόφαση νωρίς μέσα στην ημέρα για το τι να ετοιμάσουμε για δείπνο και το να πακετάρουμε την τσάντα της πάνας εκ των προτέρων είναι μικρά πράγματα που μπορούν να κάνουν μεγάλη διαφορά την τελευταία στιγμή. Όταν τα παιδιά μας ήταν μικρά, άρχισα να πακετάρω τις βαλίτσες μια μέρα πριν από ένα ταξίδι αντί την ημέρα της αναχώρησης. Μπορούσα να ανταπεξέλθω καλύτερα στην τελευταία βιασύνη αν αυτή η δουλειά είχε ήδη γίνει.

Κάντε πρώτα τις πιο σημαντικές εργασίες

Αυτή η προσέγγιση δίνει την ελευθερία να παραλείψουμε εργασίες μικρότερης σημασίας όταν είμαστε πιεσμένοι από τον χρόνο.

Μερικές φορές δεν είναι όλα στη λίστα εργασιών εξίσου πολύτιμα. Το να αφήσεις μια εργασία είναι δύσκολο για έναν τελειομανή, αλλά είναι δυνατό να αναπτύξεις νέες συνήθειες.

Χωρίστε τη δουλειά σε μικρότερα κομμάτια

Μερικές φορές το μέγεθος μιας εργασίας την κάνει να φαίνεται υπερβολικά μεγάλη για να ξεκινήσει. Διασπάστε τη μεγάλη εργασία σε μικρότερα μέρη. Η ολοκλήρωση μιας μικρότερης εργασίας είναι πολύ πιο διαχειρίσιμη. Το βαθύ καθάρισμα της κουζίνας μου είναι μια εργασία που δεν απολαμβάνω. Αν το ημερολόγιό μου λέει «βαθύς καθαρισμός κουζίνας», είναι εύκολο να το αγνοήσω.

Αλλά αν το ημερολόγιό μου λέει «καθαρίστε τις συσκευές, σκουπίστε τα ντουλάπια και πλύνετε τα παράθυρα», φαίνεται πιο εφικτό.

Υπάρχουν τόσα πολλά χαρούμενα γεγονότα στη ζωή· γιατί να ταλαιπωρούμαστε από αναβλητικότητα; Δώστε στον εαυτό σας την ελευθερία να ζήσει διαφορετικά. Μερικές μικρές αλλαγές μπορούν να κάνουν τη μεγαλύτερη διαφορά ανάμεσα σε μια ευλογημένη ή μια αγχωμένη τελευταία στιγμή.

Do you believe in miracles? Do you believe in the supernatural? What about divine intervention? Or a better question might be, have you seen God working in your life? Do others see God working in your life?

My brother was working in the greenhouse when a customer walked in and marveled at the beauty of all the plants. He then exclaimed how impressed he was at all our hard work. My brother responded with, “Some plant, some water, but God gives the increase.” To which the customer responded with, “No, no, don’t give the credit to God. You came out here and did all this work. You planted, watered, and fertilized all these plants, and you all deserve the credit, not God!” The reason the man felt this way is because he was a humanist.

What is Humanism?

The dictionary defines humanism like this; an outlook or system of thought attaching prime importance to human rather than divine or supernatural matters. Humanist beliefs stress the potential value and goodness of human beings, emphasize common human needs, and seek solely rational ways of solving human problems.

If God does exist, then we will have to recognize this fact and answer to Him. Humanists attempt to prove that God does not exist, so they can freely live their lives as they please. According to humanism, there is no God. If so, then we, the human race, are superior to God. Everything is for us and our ultimate happiness. This is the definition of humanism.

Two Types of Humanism

There are two types of humanistic beliefs, and we will look at both. The first belief is the theory that there is no God. In reality, this seems to be the only rational way to be a humanist. Everything is created by man and for man. There are no other factors or supernatural involvement. Everything happens by reason and common sense. There is a logical explanation for everything that happens. Of course, some things do not make sense, but humanists brush those aside and look only at the things that can be explained. Like the plants in the greenhouse, they look at all that man does and ignore the supernatural part of a plant springing forth with new life. Scientists around the world are working diligently to put human reasoning into everything that has ever happened, even the creation of the world. Scientists, with all their learning and wisdom, attempt to give logical explanations for why natural disasters and global crises happen. If they can explain everything, then they can rule out God and His existence. This allows the human race to do as it pleases without eternal consequences. This, in turn leads to a great sense of false peace.

The humanists, with all their reasoning, mock the very existence of God. If you go to most colleges in America and talk to people about Christianity, they laugh at you and mock the fact that Christians actually believe in God.

The second type of humanistic belief is a theory of humanism that acknowledges the existence of God. One anthropologist argued that humanism is a project of modernity and a secularized continuation of Western Christian theology. But if you ask people what they think humanism means, you will likely get different responses, and it becomes very confusing. But why the confusion? Because people are trying to be Christian humanists. Christian Humanism has frequently been criticized for its vagueness and difficulty to define. The reason it has become so confusing is that people want to believe in God but also believe in themselves and that the world revolves around them.

In Romans, we read, “For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them. For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse: Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things. Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen. For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections: for even their women did change the natural use into that which is against nature: And likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust one toward another; men with men working that which is unseemly, and receiving in themselves that recompence of their error which was meet. And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient; Being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers, Backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents, Without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful: Who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them” (Romans 1:18-32).

So how can one be a humanist and believe in God? This is where we hit a little closer to home. This type of humanist believes God wants him to be happy. He believes in a Creator God but does not believe he has to serve Him In reality. He doesn’t believe in the true God but, in his mind, created a fictitious god that does not exist. This allows him to live for himself and his own happiness. This type of person will talk about God, go to church, sing songs, and say prayers. However, he will look only to man for all his needs. If he is sick, he calls a doctor. If he needs money, he goes to the banker. If the need is a break from reality, he takes a vacation or retreat. He lives life for his own happiness and then thanks God though he did not look to God for his needs. These people are dependent on themselves. They have confidence in themselves.

Here is an example: A Christian plants a garden and takes care of it each day. He waters and fertilizes weeds and prunes. Finally, his plants all begin to bear fruit, nice fruit. He thanks God for the plentiful harvest. His neighbor, an atheistic humanist, also planted a garden. He, too, went out each day and watered, pruned, weeded, and fertilized. He also received a bountiful harvest. This man, however, boasted of all that he had accomplished. Both men did the same things and had similar results. One gave God the credit, and one credited himself. He will say he accomplished the same thing without God that his neighbor did with God. Christians know that he is wrong and that he actually did need God to grow his garden.

When something happens that requires supernatural intervention, the Christian humanist prays and asks others to pray. However, he does not believe God will answer their prayers and instantly gets to work to solve his problem, with only human reasoning. Then, if the problem is resolved, he thanks God for it. This type of humanism has confused the modern world. It has caused unbelievers to mock the Christian faith and to call it a false religion with no power.

The Christian does not believe in human reasoning. The Christian believes that the God of heaven is the reason for everything. “For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him” (Colossians 1:16). We are nothing without Him, and without Him, we can do nothing. Christianity is the opposite of humanism. When the Christian does something supernatural, something the humanist or atheist cannot do, then we have something that will confound the wise.

When the neighbor sees the Christian loving his enemies, forgiving someone who wronged him, and doing things that he cannot do, he then begins to wonder where the power to do these things came from. This then leads him to the Father. When there is nothing supernatural that we are doing, he is confused.

What About Us?

I fear that we are falling into this trap of ‘Christian Humanism.’ We talk the talk; we say we believe in God. We go to church, sing songs, and say prayers. However, from outward appearances, we trust in ourselves. Because we have centered our lives around ourselves and our well-being, the God of heaven does not hear us. Our prayers are not answered, and the time on our knees is a struggle at best. We go through the motions because that is how we’ve been taught, but our faith lies in human reasoning.

It can be extremely difficult to seek the Lord while living in a humanistic society. A society that has perfected the pursuit of liberty and happiness. Slowly, the church is caving to the ways of this world.

A minister from China was visiting the churches in America. Before departing back to China, he was asked what impressed him most about the churches in America. He replied, “I am amazed at what all they have accomplished without God.”

We would do well to simplify the modern definition of humanism. The humanist proudly denies that there is a God when he boasts of his own strength and abilities. He proclaims the great accomplishments of man and mocks the humble Christian.

The Christian denies himself, picks up his cross, and follows his Master. The Christian thinks nothing of himself or the ability of man, confidently admitting that he is merely dust and back to that dust he will quickly go. The Christian looks for the good in others and trusts God for all his daily needs and cares.

Christians believe they are merely servants to their master. They are hated by the world and despised by most, rejected. “If the world hate you, ye know that it hated me before it hated you. (John 15:18)” To them, this life is not the pursuit of happiness. The things of this world do not even interest them. Their joy and peace comes solely from serving their master, from pleasing their Heavenly Father. To the world, they are strange. Fools. To God, they are His dear children.

God is still looking for people today who will put their trust in Him. He is looking over all the earth for someone, somewhere, who will put aside human reasoning and common sense and obey the voice from heaven. God wants men with faith who will step out into the supernatural, like Abraham, Moses, David, and the thousands of believers that followed. Someone who will deny himself and this world and follow the Savior.

When this life is over, the humanists, whether they say they believe in God or not, will perish. And the Christians will go on to live forever in glory.

Humanist? Christian? Christian Humanist? Which one are you?

Je, unaamini kwa miujiza? Je, unaamini kwa mambo ya ulimwengu wa roho? Vipi kuhusu uingiliaji wa Mungu? Au swali bora linaweza kuwa, umemuona Mungu akifanya kazi katika maisha yako? Je, wengine wanaona Mungu akifanya kazi katika maisha yako?

Ndugu yangu alikuwa akifanya kazi katika kizibazi cha mimea alipokuwa mteja akiingia na kustaajabu uzuri wa mimea yote. Kisha alishtuka kwa jinsi alivyoshangazwa na kazi zetu zote. Ndugu yangu alijibu kwa kusema, “Mtu alifanya mimea, mtu alileta maji, lakini Mungu ndiye anayetoa uzalishaji.” Mteja akajibu, “Hapana, hapana, usimpe Mungu sifa. Ninyi mlikuja hapa na mkafanya kazi hii yote. Mlimwaga mimea, mlimea, mlipatia mbolea mimea hizi, ninyi ndinyi mnafaa kupatiwa sifa, si Mungu!” Sababu gani mtu huyo alihisi hivyo ni kwamba alikuwa mwanadamu-anayetukana (humanisti).

Nini Ni Utu-Tukio (Humanism)?

Kamusi inaelezea utu-tukio (humanism) hivi; mtazamo au mfumo wa mawazo unaoweka umuhimu mkuu kwa mambo ya binadamu badala ya yale ya kimungu au ya kimataifa ya kiroho. Imani za wanadamu-anayetukana zinaangazia thamani na wema wa binadamu, zinaonyesha mahitaji ya kawaida ya binadamu, na kutafuta njia za kimantiki pekee za kutatua matatizo ya binadamu.

Kama Mungu atalipo, basi tutalazimika kutambua ukweli huu na kumjibu. Wanadamu-anayetukana wanajaribu kuthibitisha kwamba Mungu hayupo, ili waweze kuishi maisha yao kwa uhuru kama wanavyotaka. Kwa mujibu wa utu-tukio, hakuna Mungu. Ikiwa hivyo ndivyo ilivyo, basi sisi, binadamu, tuko juu ya Mungu. Kila kitu ni kwa ajili yetu na furaha yetu ya mwisho. Hii ndiyo tafsiri ya utu-tukio.

Aina Mbili za Utu-Tukio

Kuna aina mbili za imani za utu-tukio, na tutajaribu kuzipitia zote. Imani ya kwanza ni nadharia kwamba hakuna Mungu. Kwa kweli, hii inaonekana kuwa njia pekee ya kimantiki ya kuwa mwanadamu-anayetukana. Kila kitu kimeumbwa na mwanadamu na kwa mwanadamu. Hakuna vigezo vingine wala uingiliaji wa kimawimbi. Kila kitu hufanyika kwa sababu na mantiki ya kawaida. Kuna ufafanuzi wa kimantiki kwa kila kitu kinachotokea. Bila shaka, baadhi ya mambo hayafai kueleweka, lakini wanadamu-anayetukana wanayasahau yale na kuangalia tu mambo ambayo yanaweza kueleweka. Kama mimea katika kizibazi, wanaangalia yote ambayo mwanadamu anafanya na kupuuza sehemu ya kimawimbi ya mmea kurukaruka kwa uhai mpya. Wanasayansi duniani kote wanafanya kazi kwa bidii kuweka mantiki ya mwanadamu katika kila kitu kilichowahi kutokea, hata uumbaji wa dunia. Wanasayansi, kwa elimu na busara yao yote, wanajaribu kutoa maelezo ya kimantiki ya kwa nini majanga ya asili na migogoro ya dunia hufanyika. Ikiwa wanaweza kuelezea kila kitu, basi wanaweza kuondoa uwepo wa Mungu. Hii inaruhusu binadamu kuishi kama wanavyotaka bila matokeo ya milele. Hii, kwa upande mwingine, inasababisha hisia kubwa ya amani ya uongo.

Watu-wa-utu, kwa mantiki yao yote, wanatukana hata uwepo wa Mungu. Ukitembea kwenye vyuo vingi nchini Marekani na kuzungumza na watu kuhusu Ukristo, watakutabasamu na kumtukana ukweli kwamba Wakristo kwa kweli wanaamini Mungu.

Aina ya pili ya imani ya utu-tukio ni nadharia ya utu-tukio inayotambua uwepo wa Mungu. Mmoja mtaalamu wa watu (anthropologist) alidai kwamba utu-tukio ni mradi wa kisasa na kuendelea kwa teolojia ya Kiarifa ya Magharibi iliyopunguzwa ya kidini. Lakini ukimuuliza mtu apa anafikiri nini kuhusu utu-tukio, labda utapata majibu tofauti, na kuwaelezea mambo yanapotoka kuwa ya kuchanganya. Lakini kwanini kuchanganyikiwa? Kwa sababu watu wanajaribu kuwa Watu-Wa-Utu Wakristo. Utu-Tukio wa Kikristo mara nyingi umehukumiwa kwa ukosefu wa uelewa na ugumu wa kufafanua. Sababu ambayo imekuwa ya kuchanganya ni kwamba watu wanataka kuamini Mungu lakini pia kuamini wao wenyewe na kwamba dunia inazunguka wao.

Katika waraka wa Warumi, tunasoma, “Kwa sababu hasira ya Mungu inatolewa kutoka mbinguni juu ya wote wasio wa kweli na uovu wa wanadamu, wanaoshikilia ukweli kwa uovu; Kwa sababu kile ambacho kinaweza kujulikana kuhusu Mungu kinaonekana ndani yao; kwa kuwa Mungu amewafunulia. Kwa vitu visivyoonekana kutoka kwa yeye tangu uumbaji wa dunia vinaonekana wazi, vinavyofikiriwa kwa vitu vilivyotengenezwa, hata nguvu yake ya milele na ubinadamu wake; hivyo hawana msamaha: Kwa maana, walipomjua Mungu, hawakumlifu kama Mungu, wala hawakushukuru; bali walitulia wasio na maana katika mawazo yao, na moyo wao wa upumbavu ulikuwa umechacha. Wakiijaribu kuwa wenye busara, walikuwa wajinga, Na kubadilisha utukufu wa Mungu asiyoyeza kuwa sanamu iliyotengenezwa kama mtu anayezeka, na kwa ndege, na wanyama wenye miguu minne, na viumbe vinavyokanyaga. Kwa hivyo Mungu pia aliwaachia wasafi kupitia tamaa za mioyo yao wenyewe, ili kuwadhalilisha miili yao miongoni mwa wao: Ambaye walibadilisha ukweli wa Mungu kuwa uongo, na kuabudu na kutumikia kiumbe zaidi ya Muumba, ambaye amebarikiwa milele. Amina. Kwa sababu hii Mungu aliwaachia tamaa za kupuuza: kwa maana hata wanawake wao walibadilisha matumizi ya asili kuwa yale ambayo ni dhidi ya asili: Na vivyo hivyo pia wanaume, waachilia matumizi ya asili ya mwanamke, waliwaka kwa tamaa miongoni mwa wao; wanaume na wanaume wakifanya yaliyo asiyejulikana, wakipokea ndani yao hiyo malipo ya kosa lao ambayo ilikuwa inafaa. Na kama walivyokataa kumsifu Mungu katika maarifa yao, Mungu aliwaachia katika akili iliyokataliwa, kufanya yale mambo ambayo hayafai; Wakiwa wamejazwa kwa uovu wote, uchumba, uovu, tamaa, ubaya; wakiwa wamejaa wivu, mauaji, mabishano, udanganyifu, uadui; wachochezi, Wakazungumza vibaya, wakiwachukia Mungu, wakiwa wakiwapotosha, wajivuno, wasemaji wa uovu, wabunifu wa mambo mabaya, wasio waaminifu kwa wazazi, bila kuelewa, waovukivu wa ahadi, bila upendo wa asili, wasioweza kuachishwa shinikizo, wasio na rehema: Wakijua hukumu ya Mungu, kwamba wale wanaofanya vitu hivyo wanastahili kifo, hawafanyi hivyo tu, bali pia wanafurahia wale wanaofanya hivyo” (Warumi 1:18-32).

Basi je, mtu anawezaje kuwa mwanadamu-anayetukana na kuamini Mungu? Hapa ndipo tunagonga karibu nyumbani. Aina hii ya mwanadamu-anayetukana anaamini Mungu anamtaka awe na furaha. Anaamini katika Mungu Muumba lakini haamini kwamba lazima amtumikie Kwa uzuri. Hapendi Mungu wa kweli lakini, moyoni mwake, ameunda Mungu wa kufikirika ambaye hajapo. Hii inamruhusu kuishi kwa ajili yake mwenyewe na furaha yake mwenyewe. Aina hii ya mtu atazungumza kuhusu Mungu, ataenda kanisani, ataimba nyimbo, na aseme sala. Hata hivyo, atamtafuta mwanadamu pekee kwa mahitaji yake yote. Ikiwa anaumwa, anapiga simu kwa daktari. Ikiwa anahitaji pesa, anaenda kwa mfanyabiashara. Ikiwa hitaji ni kupumzika kutoka kwa uhalisia, anachukua likizo au kimbilio. Anaishi maisha kwa ajili ya furaha yake mwenyewe na kisha anamshukuru Mungu ingawa hakumtazama Mungu kwa mahitaji yake. Watu hawa wanategemea wao wenyewe. Wana imani kwa uwezo wao wenyewe.

Hapa kuna mfano: Mkristo anapanda bustani na kuitunza kila siku. Anamwagilia, anampatia mbolea, anatupa magugu na kukata. Hatimaye, mimea yake yote inaanza kuzaa, matunda mazuri. Anamshukuru Mungu kwa mavuno mengi. Jirani yake, mwanadamu-anayetukana ambaye ni mtupu wa Mungu (mkanushi wa Mungu), pia alipanda bustani. Yeye pia alitoka kila siku na kumwagilia, kukata, kuondoa magugu, na kupatia mbolea. Pia alipata mavuno mengi. Hata hivyo, mwanaume huyu alijivunia yote aliyofanya. Wote wawili walifanya mambo sawa na walipata matokeo yanayofanana. Mmoja alimpa Mungu sifa, mmoja akajipa sifa yake mwenyewe. Atasema alifanikiwa kufanya kitu hicho bila Mungu kama jirani yake alivyofanya kwa Mungu. Wakristo wanajua kwamba yeye ni mkosefu na kwamba kweli alihitaji Mungu kukuza bustani yake.

Wakati jambo linapotokea ambalo linahitaji uingiliaji wa kimawimbi, mwanadamu-anayetukana Mkristo anaomba sala na kuomba wengine wasali. Hata hivyo, hapati imani kwamba Mungu atajibu sala zao na mara moja anaanza kufanya kazi kutatua shida yake, kwa kutumia mantiki ya mwanadamu pekee. Kisha, ikiwa tatizo litatatuliwa, anamshukuru Mungu kwa hilo. Aina hii ya utu-tukio imechanganya ulimwengu wa kisasa. Imesababisha wasiokuwa waamini kutukana imani ya Kikristo na kuiita dini ya uongo isiyo na nguvu.

Mkristo hakutegemei mantiki ya mwanadamu. Mkristo anaamini kwamba Mungu wa mbinguni ndiye sababu ya kila kitu. “Kwa maana kwa yeye vitu vyote viliumbwa, vilivyomo mbinguni na vilivyomo duniani, vinavyoonekana na visivyoonekana, iwe viti vya enzi, au utawala, au uamaduni, au nguvu: vitu vyote viliumbwa kwa yeye, na kwa ajili yake” (Wakolosai 1:16). Sisi hatuna kitu bila Yeye, na bila Yeye, hatuwezi kufanya chochote. Ukristo ni kinyume kabisa na utu-tukio. Wakati Mkristo anafanya kitu cha kimawimbi, kitu ambacho mwanadamu-anayetukana au mkanushi wa Mungu hawezi kufanya, basi tunakuwa na jambo ambalo litamshangaza mwenye busara.

Wakati jirani anapoona Mkristo akimpenda adui yake, kumwacha msamaha mtu aliyemdhulumu, na kufanya mambo ambayo yeye hawezi kufanya, basi anaanza kujiuliza nguvu za kufanya mambo hayo zilikutoka wapi. Hii basi inamuongoza kwa Baba. Wakati hakuna kitu cha kimawimbi tunachofanya, yeye anachanganyikiwa.

Je, Kuhusu Sisi?

Ninaogopa kwamba tunang’ang’ania katika mtego huu wa ‘Utu-Tukio wa Kikristo.’ Tunazungumza maneno; tunasema tunaamini Mungu. Tunaenda kanisani, kuimba nyimbo, na kuomba sala. Hata hivyo, kutoka kwa muonekano wa nje, tunamtegemea sisi wenyewe. Kwa sababu tumemwekea maisha yetu katikati yetu wenyewe na ustawi wetu, Mungu wa mbinguni hasikii. Sala zetu hazijajibiwa, na muda wetu miguuni ni mapambano kwa ubora. Tunapitia taratibu kwa sababu hivyo ndizo tulivyofundishwa, lakini imani yetu iko katika mantiki ya mwanadamu.

Inaweza kuwa vigumu sana kumtafuta Bwana ukiwa unaishi katika jamii yenye utu-tukio. Jamii ambayo imekamilisha kutafuta uhuru na furaha. Polepole, kanisa linaanza kukubali njia za ulimwengu huu.

Mchungaji kutoka China alikuwa akitembelea makanisa nchini Marekani. Kabla ya kurejea China, aliulizwa kilichomvutia zaidi kuhusu makanisa nchini Marekani. Alijibu, “Nashangazwa na kile walichokifanya bila Mungu.”

Tungefanya vizuri kupunguza tafsiri ya kisasa ya utu-tukio. Mwanadamu-anayetukana kwa fahari anakanusha kuwa kuna Mungu anapojivunia nguvu na uwezo wake mwenyewe. Anatangaza mafanikio makuu ya mwanadamu na kutukana Mkristo mwadilifu.

Mkristo anajinyima, anakunja msalaba wake, na kumfuata Mwalimu wake. Mkristo hahisi chochote kuhusu yeye mwenyewe au uwezo wa mwanadamu, akikiri kwa ujasiri kwamba yeye ni mavumbi tu na harudi katika mavumbi hayo haraka. Mkristo anatafuta wema kwa wengine na kuamini Mungu kwa mahitaji yake yote ya kila siku na wasi yake.

Wakristo wanaamini kuwa wao ni watumishi tu wa bwana wao. Wanachukiwa na dunia na wachukuliwa na wengi, wakataliwa. “Kama dunia inakuchukia, mnajua kuwa iliniondani kabla ilivyokuchukieni. (Yohana 15:18)” Kwawo, maisha haya si kutafuta furaha. Mambo ya ulimwengu huyatawakii. Furaha na amani yao inatokana pekee na kumtumikia bwana wao, kwa kumfurahisha Baba yao wa Mbinguni. Kwa dunia, wao ni wageni. Wajinga. Kwa Mungu, wao ni watoto wake wapendwa.

Mungu bado anatafuta watu leo watakaoweka imani yao kwake. Anatafuta katika dunia yote mtu, mahali fulani, atakayenuia mantiki ya mwanadamu na mantiki ya kawaida na kutii sauti kutoka mbinguni. Mungu anataka wanaume wenye imani watakaotoka katika kimawimbi, kama Abrahamu, Musa, Daudi, na maelfu ya waumini waliofuata. Mtu ambaye atajinyima na dunia hii na kumfuata Mwokozi.

Wakati maisha haya yatakapokoma, wanadamu-anayetukana, iwe wanasema wanaamini Mungu au la, wataangamia. Na Wakristo wataendelea kuishi milele kwa utukufu.

Mwanadamu-anayetukana? Mkristo? Mwanadamu-Anayetukana Mkristo? Wewe ni ipi?

Eight-year-old Jamin wasn’t very smart. Or at least that’s what his older brother told him. Almost daily, brother Kenny found ways to remind Jamin of his shortcomings and laugh at his blunders.

“Jamin, you will never be smart”, Kenny said. Deep inside Jamin felt resigned to a life of muddled trip-ups. Would he always be clumsy? Would he always say things wrong? That’s what Kenny said.

Jamin believed Kenny’s lectures with wide-eyed belief. Kenny was three years older than him, so he must be right. Very well, then Jamin would be simple. Kenny would be smart. Life was not fair. Dad and Mom disliked Kenny’s proud talk and punished him whenever they walked in on one of his speeches. But Kenny had a way of avoiding earshot. So he continued mocking Jamin.

Grandma Otto watched these trials from her rocker on the porch. She was a quiet old lady.

“Jamin, do you know where Kenny is?” Mom asked with a smile. “It’s almost supper time.”

“He went to check his coyote traps. I’ll go find him.”

There was a chill in the air as he tramped up over the lawn, and the sun was growing old as he crossed the border of the woods. The fleeting shadows scurried over the hills. The chill deepened as he stumped further in. He breathed the rich air and followed Kenny’s trail. Eventually, the trail would end up in a meadow, but Jamin hoped he would find Kenny before he had to go that far. The various traps had been checked already, so Jamin knew Kenny had come this way. Jamin trudged on resolutely. His golden head caught the tired beams that fled from the sun as they flickered through the trees. And soon those too had faded leaving behind the musky smell of the woods. The fall webworms had been at work, and their web curtains shuttered from branches overhead.

At length, as the trees subdued and thinned, and the meadow appeared Jamin knew this was the end of his brother’s trap route. If Kenny wasn’t here, he wouldn’t know where else to look.

But Kenny was there. As Jamin clumped into the meadow, he could see a frustrated heap to his right. The heap’s voice had a familiar ring. The heap’s face was lit in pain. The heap was Kenny. “Are you alright? What happened?” Jamin felt strange, seeing Kenny scrunched in the dirt. Kenny was smart. “Did you step in a trap?”

“Yes, Jamin. I..I wasn’t looking where I was going. Help me. Please.”

Jamin bent and found an ankle firmly held in the jaws of a steel trap. Darkness stained the ground around Kenny. Quickly, Jamin’s strong arms pried open the jaws. Kenny reeled free. “Can you walk?”

“Yes. I think so. If you support me, I can hobble along.”

“Dad and Mom will be worried. We’ve missed supper.”

Sure enough, as the brothers hobbled back through the woods, they heard the long calling of their father. Jamin called back, and he was by their side in a moment, seeing the ankle and scooping up Kenny like a hurt sheep. The odd little band hurried home, and the screen door banged shut as Dad swept across the porch. Jamin went to the wash house and scrubbed his hands. He headed for the front door.

“Jamin.” It was Grandma. The porch light showed her in her old rocker. A heavy comforter lay on her shoulders.

“Yes, Grandma?”

“Do you think you are not very smart?”

“That’s what Kenny says.” Jamin squirmed.

“You were strong enough to open the trap, and Kenny wasn’t. You were brave enough to find him in the dark. Lots of young boys wouldn’t be.” Jamin was silent. Grandma Otto rocked some more, then smiled. “God made you the way you are for a reason, Jamin. He made Kenny the way he is for a reason. He has a plan for you, and a place only you can fill, you know.”

Jamin turned and walked into the warm kitchen. He was smiling.
