Åttaårige Jamin var inte särskilt smart. Eller åtminstone var det vad hans storebror sa. Nästan dagligen hittade bror Kenny sätt att påminna Jamin om hans brister och skratta åt hans misstag.

”Jamin, du kommer aldrig att bli smart”, sa Kenny. Djupt inne kände Jamin sig beredd att acceptera ett liv av förvirrade snedsteg. Skulle han alltid vara klumpig? Skulle han alltid säga fel saker? Det var vad Kenny sa.

Jamin trodde på Kennys predikningar med vidöppna ögon. Kenny var tre år äldre än han, så han måste ha rätt. Mycket väl, då skulle Jamin vara enkel. Kenny skulle vara smart. Livet var inte rättvist. Pappa och mamma ogillade Kennys högmodiga prat och straffade honom när de kom på en av hans föreställningar. Men Kenny hade ett sätt att undvika att bli hörd. Så han fortsatte att håna Jamin.

Farmor Otto såg dessa prövningar från sin gungstol på verandan. Hon var en tystlåten gammal dam.

”Jamin, vet du var Kenny är?” frågade mamma med ett leende. ”Det är snart kvällsmat.”

”Han gick för att kolla sina prärievargsfällor. Jag går och hittar honom.”

Det var kyligt i luften när han trampade över gräsmattan, och solen blev gammal när han korsade skogsbrynet. De flyktiga skuggorna susade över kullarna. Kylan fördjupades ju längre han gick in. Han andades den rika luften och följde Kennys spår. Så småningom skulle stigen mynna ut i en äng, men Jamin hoppades hitta Kenny innan han behövde gå så långt. Fällorna hade redan blivit kontrollerade, så Jamin visste att Kenny hade gått här. Jamin traskade vidare beslutsamt. Hans gyllene huvud fångade de trötta strålar som flydde från solen när de fladdrade genom träden. Och snart hade även de bleknat och lämnat kvar skogen doft av mossa. Spindelvävssjoken hade gjort sitt, och deras väggar hängde från grenarna ovanför.

Till sist, när träden tunnades ut och ängen visade sig, visste Jamin att detta var slutet på hans brors fällsträcka. Om Kenny inte fanns här visste han inte var han skulle leta annars.

Men Kenny var där. När Jamin klev in på ängen kunde han se en frustrerad hög till höger. Högens röst hade en bekant klang. Högens ansikte var plågat. Högen var Kenny. ”Är du okej? Vad hände?” Jamin kände sig underlig när han såg Kenny hopkrupen i gräset. Kenny var smart. ”Gick du i en fälla?”

”Ja, Jamin. Jag… jag såg inte vart jag gick. Hjälp mig. Snälla.”

Jamin böjde sig ner och fann en fotled fast i en stålfälla. Mörkret fläckade marken runt Kenny. Snabbt vred Jamin sina starka armar och öppnade käftarna. Kenny föll fri. ”Kan du gå?”

”Ja. Jag tror det. Om du stödjer mig kan jag stappla med.”

”Pappa och mamma kommer att vara oroade. Vi har missat kvällsmaten.”

Mycket riktigt, när bröderna vinglade tillbaka genom skogen hörde de sin fars långa rop. Jamin ropade tillbaka, och han stod vid deras sida på ett ögonblick, såg fotleden och lyfte upp Kenny som ett skadat får. Den konstiga lilla sällskapet skyndade hem, och skärmdörren smällde igen när pappa svepte över verandan. Jamin gick till tvätthuset och skrubbade sina händer. Han gick mot ytterdörren.

”Jamin.” Det var farmor. Verandans lampa visade henne i hennes gamla gungstol. En tung filt låg över hennes axlar.

”Ja, farmor?”

”Tror du att du inte är särskilt smart?”

”Det är vad Kenny säger.” Jamin vred sig obekvämt.

”Du var stark nog att öppna fällan, och Kenny var det inte. Du var modig nog att hitta honom i mörkret. Många unga pojkar skulle inte vara det.” Jamin var tyst. Farmor Otto gungade lite till och log sedan. ”Gud gjorde dig som du är av en anledning, Jamin. Han gjorde Kenny som han är av en anledning. Han har en plan för dig, och en plats som bara du kan fylla, vet du.”

Jamin vände sig om och gick in i det varma köket. Han log.

Circumstantial overload might be the most difficult. We can choose not to go to a Norwex party if we need to give our schedule some space. But if a child breaks a leg in the middle of wedding preparations, we have no choice other than to make the best of the situation.

Circumstantial overload may happen slowly, as in the following story, or it may happen quickly as in the case of an accident in which a family member is injured.

Becky is in her thirties with seven children under seventeen. A few years ago, one of their chicken houses burned down. At the time, they were thankful that the chickens had left the day before and that no one was close by when the propane tank exploded.

“My husband faced the disaster like a man,” says Becky. “His calm spirit helped me relax. I felt certain that we could make the financial adjustments and life would go on as before. But I was wrong. Very wrong.”

“In time the mess was cleaned up, and Rick looked into rebuilding. The quotes were higher than expected, so he opted to do some of the work himself. He also took on a part-time job to provide more income. Our boys were old enough to help, yet they couldn’t do much without Rick’s direction.”

“I first felt the adjustment in my wallet, but I consoled myself that this was only temporary. Then the spark in Rick’s eyes was replaced with a dull stare. He became distant from us. I knew something wasn’t right, but I couldn’t put my finger on it.”

“Then he was elected to finish the last four months of secretarial duties for a brother who spent some time in Bulgaria. That night he came home and wept. ‘Doesn’t anyone understand what I’m going through? Every time I turn around, there is something to do. The boys want to go fishing, you need a new clothesline, and the chicken house needs to be finished in six months! I am not mentally capable of handling one more duty.’”

“That was the straw that broke the camel’s back,” Becky said. “I became alarmed when I heard him yawning in the middle of the night and knew that he was not sleeping.”

“It was clear to me that my perfectionist husband was overloaded. More and more Rick leaned on me. I cut back on my commitments and tried to keep my time free so that I was available to help lessen his load.”

“I felt like a lifeguard trying to keep a man from drowning while taking in a bit too much water myself. Many of the home-life responsibilities fell on my shoulders. Then I was asked to fill the position of food committee for Mrs. ‘Going-to-Bulgaria.’”

Unfortunately, circumstantial stress is often unnoticed. Worse yet, the victim can be misunderstood or misjudged. Becky said, “My darkest day came when I was accused of being selfish with my time because I declined the food committee request.”

Prolonged overload can be emotionally and mentally damaging

Intense, long-lasting pressures or troubles shouldered alone can cause severe stress. Minor stress is normal, but prolonged stress can cause depression, anxiety, heart disease, and high blood pressure. How you handle prolonged stress is important.

Sometimes this type of overload is not public knowledge. Traumatic events in our plain circles tend to receive prayer, finances, and weekly budget updates. At the same time, other saints are suffering deeply on the sidelines with little recognition or financial aid. It could be strained relationships or little bills that add up to a big sum. Betrayal and rejection cause stress beyond measure. There are no quick fixes to circumstantial stress, but little sparks of light can help you navigate the darkness.

Talk about your situation with someone you trust

Sometimes just talking about problems can help you to put issues in perspective. Hearing yourself verbalize a stressful situation somehow clears brain fog and gives a clearer path forward.

Find routine

When stress prevails, racing thoughts, forgetfulness, and inability to focus comes uninvited. Having a routine can bring some rhythm to your mental well-being. The smallest normalcy brings a moment of pleasure, and it is soothing to the soul.

Intentionally seek a breather

Lingering stress can cause agitation, moodiness, and the desire to take control. Sometimes it is hard to think beyond mental fog, but it is so important to find refreshment for your mental wellbeing. Stress hormones can speed up your heart rate and tighten your blood vessels. That temporarily raises your blood pressure. The opposite happens when you relax. Being relaxed helps you have a calmer, clearer mind which improves your concentration and decision-making.

Believe that God cares

Say it. Read the Psalms over and over. Listen to good music. Take short walks and pray aloud. Keep your eyes on Jesus. Believe “Weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning” (Psalm 30:5).

If you are facing circumstantial overload, be patient and realistic. God will make a way for you. Many times, He opens doors just when we are running out of options. He will supply the needed grace for that hour. And the next hour. And the next. At times, surprising opportunities come, and prayers are answered in unexpected ways. However He chooses to work on your behalf, hold to His unchanging hand.

Regardless of the type of overload you might be encountering, turn to your Heavenly Father.

Ask Him for direction and wisdom. And say with the Psalmist, “In thee, O LORD, do I put my trust: let me never be put to confusion” (Psalm 71:1).

Omständighetsmässig överbelastning kan vara det svåraste. Vi kan välja att inte gå på ett Norwex-party om vi behöver ge vårt schema lite utrymme. Men om ett barn bryter benet mitt i bröllopsförberedelserna har vi inget val annat än att göra det bästa av situationen.

Omständighetsmässig överbelastning kan komma långsamt, som i följande berättelse, eller snabbt, som i fallet med en olycka där en familjemedlem skadas.

Becky är i trettioårsåldern och har sju barn under sjutton. För några år sedan brann ett av deras hönshus ner. Då var de tacksamma över att hönsen hade lämnat dagen innan och att ingen befann sig i närheten när gasoltanken exploderade.

“Min man mötte katastrofen som en man,” säger Becky. “Hans lugna sinne hjälpte mig att slappna av. Jag var säker på att vi skulle klara de ekonomiska omställningarna och att livet skulle fortsätta som tidigare. Men jag hade fel. Mycket fel.”

“Så småningom blev röran städad upp, och Rick funderade på att bygga upp igen. Offerten var högre än väntat, så han valde att göra en del av arbetet själv. Han tog också ett deltidsjobb för att få mer inkomst. Våra pojkar var tillräckligt gamla för att hjälpa till, men de kunde inte göra mycket utan Ricks anvisningar.”

“Jag märkte först av omställningen i min plånbok, men tröstade mig med att det bara var tillfälligt. Sedan ersattes gnistan i Ricks ögon av en dov stirrande blick. Han blev avlägsen mot oss. Jag visste att något inte stod rätt till, men jag kunde inte sätta fingret på vad.”

“Sedan valdes han att slutföra de sista fyra månaderna av sekreteraruppgifter för en broder som tillbringade lite tid i Bulgarien. Den kvällen kom han hem och grät. ’Förstår ingen vad jag går igenom? Varje gång jag vänder mig om finns det något att göra. Pojkarna vill fiska, du behöver ett nytt tvättlineställ, och hönshuset måste vara klart om sex månader! Jag är inte mentalt kapabel att hantera en uppgift till.’”

“Det var droppen som fick bägaren att rinna över,” sa Becky. “Jag blev orolig när jag hörde honom gäspa mitt i natten och visste att han inte sov.”

“Det var tydligt för mig att min perfektionistiske make var överbelastad. Mer och mer lutade Rick sig mot mig. Jag minskade mina åtaganden och försökte hålla min tid fri så att jag kunde vara tillgänglig och hjälpa till att lätta hans börda.”

“Jag kände mig som en livräddare som försökte hålla en man från att drunkna medan jag själv svalde lite för mycket vatten. Många av hemuppgifterna föll på mina axlar. Sedan blev jag ombedd att ta posten i matkommittén för fru ’På-väg-till-Bulgarien.’”

Tyvärr går omständighetsmässig stress ofta obemärkt förbi. Ännu värre kan offret missförstås eller dömas. Becky berättade, “Min mörkaste dag kom när jag blev anklagad för att vara självisk med min tid eftersom jag tackade nej till förfrågan från matkommittén.”

Förlängd överbelastning kan skada känslomässigt och mentalt

Intensiva, långvariga påfrestningar eller bekymmer som bärs ensamma kan orsaka allvarlig stress. Mindre stress är normalt, men långvarig stress kan orsaka depression, ångest, hjärtsjukdomar och högt blodtryck. Hur du hanterar långvarig stress är viktigt.

Ibland är denna typ av överbelastning inte allmänt känd. Traumatiska händelser i våra närmaste kretsar får ofta bön, ekonomiskt stöd och veckouppdateringar om budgeten. Samtidigt lider andra troende djupt i kulisserna med lite erkännande eller ekonomisk hjälp. Det kan vara ansträngda relationer eller små räkningar som tillsammans blir en stor summa. Förräderi och avvisande orsakar oerhörd stress. Det finns inga snabba lösningar på omständighetsmässig stress, men små ljusglimtar kan hjälpa dig att navigera i mörkret.

Tala om din situation med någon du litar på

Ibland kan det hjälpa bara att tala om problemen för att få perspektiv. Att höra sig själv formulera en stressande situation rensar på något sätt hjärnans dimma och ger en klarare väg framåt.

Hitta rutiner

När stressen råder kommer springande tankar, glömska och oförmåga att fokusera oinbjudna. Att ha en rutin kan ge lite rytm åt ditt mentala välbefinnande. Den minsta normalitet ger ett ögonblick av glädje, och det är lugnande för själen.

Sök medvetet en andningspaus

Varaktig stress kan orsaka oro, humörsvängningar och viljan att ta kontroll. Ibland är det svårt att tänka bortom hjärndimman, men det är så viktigt att finna uppfriskning för ditt mentala välbefinnande. Stresshormoner kan snabba upp din hjärtfrekvens och dra ihop blodkärlen. Det höjer tillfälligt ditt blodtryck. Motsatsen händer när du slappnar av. Att vara avslappnad hjälper dig att få ett lugnare, klarare sinne vilket förbättrar din koncentration och ditt beslutsfattande.

Tro att Gud bryr sig

Säg det. Läs Psaltaren om och om igen. Lyssna på god musik. Ta korta promenader och be högt. Håll dina ögon på Jesus. Tro att “Weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning” (Psalm 30:5).

Om du står inför omständighetsmässig överbelastning, var tålmodig och realistisk. Gud ska bereda en väg för dig. Många gånger öppnar Han dörrar just när våra alternativ tar slut. Han ska förse den nödvändiga nåden för den timmen. Och för nästa timme. Och för nästa. Ibland kommer överraskande möjligheter, och böner besvaras på oväntade sätt. Hur Han än väljer att verka för din räkning, håll fast vid Hans oföränderliga hand.

Oavsett vilken typ av överbelastning du möter, vänd dig till din himmelske Fader.

Be Honom om vägledning och vishet. Och säg med psalmisten, “In thee, O LORD, do I put my trust: let me never be put to confusion” (Psalm 71:1).

“Dr. Waldron, Elsie needs help!” Elsie’s husband was adamant, almost angry, as he stared at me. On the other hand, Elsie stared at the floor, almost as though she wasn’t present. I had never met either of the couple before and was struggling just a little to figure out what was needed from me to help her.

“What is going on?” I asked as I flipped through her chart. This was still in the days of paper charts, and I headed to the lab section of her chart. There wasn’t anything too crazy that I could see there—her liver enzymes were a little elevated, but otherwise, everything seemed OK.

“It’s her drinking!” Her husband told me. “She is drinking more and more every night. She won’t go out except to get whiskey. She drinks till she passes out every night and has to have something every morning to get her started.”

“Is that true?” I asked Elsie, feeling like a judge overseeing a jury trial.

“Yes,” she said. Her face was emotionless, and I couldn’t tell if she wanted to be there or not.

“Do you want help?” I asked her. This was a loaded question. Many people who struggle with alcoholism aren’t ready to break free from its vice-like hold on them. Maybe Elsie was different.

“I guess so,” she said, indifferently. Once again, I couldn’t tell whether she wanted to be there or not.

“At the rate at which you are drinking, you will kill yourself within a year – maybe two at best – if you don’t give up alcohol entirely,” I told her. “If you want to, I will try to find you an inpatient program to detox you and get you off of alcohol.”

“She’s ready,” he husband said firmly.

When dealing with someone who drinks heavily, it is crucial that they don’t simply stop drinking without medical support. Abrupt cessation of alcohol use causes the body to go into withdrawal which can produce a state called Delirium Tremens and even seizures.

I stepped out of the exam room and to make phone calls. It is never easy to find a place for someone to attempt to rehabilitate from any kind of substances, and it was over an hour and a half before I found a facility that was willing to take Elsie and try to help her get off of the whiskey.

I sighed as I reentered her exam room. I had been afraid that I wouldn’t find anywhere for her to go.

I told them about the plan, and her husband nodded vigorously, while Elise continued to stare silently at the floor. “Can we pray together before you go?” I asked them, and when they nodded assent, I prayed with them, asking for freedom and Jesus’ presence in both of their lives.

They left my office with marching orders and directions on where to go. I had a happy glow about me for the rest of the morning, knowing that I had gone the extra mile and had really made a difference in this middle-aged couple’s life.

Around 2 pm, I got a call from the rehab facility. They hadn’t seen even a shadow of Elsie or her husband, which was surprising, since it was a bright sunny day and the facility wasn’t that far away. With a sinking feeling, I dialed the couple’s phone number.

“She won’t go!” Her husband told me. “She tells me that she told me this ahead of time. She’ll try to cut back, but she isn’t willing to go into a rehab facility or any such thing. I guess just tell them that we’ll let them know if she changes her mind.”

My nurse called the rehab facility and told them the bad news, and I sat down in my chair, stunned. What else could I have done? Was there a solution for Elsie—something different that I could have said that would have made a difference in her life?

About a year later, I received the sad news that Elsie had died at home. I was certain that things would have been different if she had gone to rehab and if she had given control to Jesus. None of that had happened, and I felt cynicism pushing into my heart.

Cynicism

We live in an age of cynicism. In ancient Greece, the cynics were an odd assortment of men who specialized in being grouchy and saying mean (they would have said truthful) things to people. They often dressed in rags and behaved in such a way that most of the polite Athenians did not want to be close to them.

Today, cynicism means a tendency to believe the worst about people and circumstances. Cynical people believe that all people are motivated purely by selfishness and that bad events will tend to prevail.

Many young doctors are idealistic and very hopeful. They believe that if they exert the utmost effort, they can make a real, positive impact on their patient’s lives. Unfortunately, as time goes by and they try their hardest and their patients don’t change, they can give up. These doctors still try, but they no longer really hope that their efforts will make much of a difference.

It seems as though people who get involved with politics often have the best of intentions. They see this as a path to changing society for the better. Unfortunately, as time goes by and the faces in charge change, the policies don’t really change, they tend to become cynical.

Sometimes this cynicism is directed against all politicians. Sometimes it is only anger directed against members of the party that opposes their party’s positions. Hope is replaced by cynicism.

Cynicism in the Bible

If there is a book in the Bible that seems to have been written by a cynical man, it is the book of Ecclesiastes. The Preacher, who we understand to be Solomon, lists all of the things that he endeavored in an attempt to find joy.

In chapter 2:17-23 Solomon describes work as futile. He finishes by saying, “For what hath man of all his labour, and of the vexation of his heart, wherein he hath laboured under the sun? For all his days are sorrows, and his travail grief; yea, his heart taketh not rest in the night. This is also vanity.” (Ecclesiastes 2:22,23)

He saw the world as being dominated by tyrants and there was little that the people could do about it. Solomon went so far as to say that political power was meaningless “Better is a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished. For out of prison he cometh to reign; whereas also he that is born in his kingdom becometh poor” (Ecclesiastes 4:13).

In Ecclesiastes 6:6, he seems to disparage long life. “Yea, though he live a thousand years twice told, yet hath he seen no good: do not all go to one place?”

Of course, he finishes his short book with the instruction to remember our Creator in the days of our youth. There is a blessing for those who choose to focus on God when they have a little bit of energy left and not, when they are old and jaded, like Solomon.

Later on, it almost seemed as though God had given up on His people. He still sent prophets to them, but He knew without a doubt that the people would refuse to respond. “Therefore thou shalt speak all these words unto them; but they will not hearken to thee: thou shalt also call unto them; but they will not answer thee” (Jeremiah 7:27).

Even in the New Testament, Paul told Timothy that the time was coming when people would no longer listen to sound doctrine. “For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine; but after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears;” (2 Timothy 4:3).

By picking and choosing these passages, we can come away with a very gloomy view of the future and, more specifically, of human’s willingness to change. It seems there is little point of investing ourselves in the people around us. They are full of woe and are as likely to change as a chipmunk is to master differential calculus.

The Opposite of Cynicism

The opposite of cynicism is hope. It is the belief that the future could be better.

It is interesting that the Apostle Paul spoke of tribulations in the Epistle to the Romans, “And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; and patience, experience; and experience, hope: and hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us” (Romans 5:3-5).

We may not have reached the place where we glory in the trials we experience, but certainly, they should bring us these other things that he mentions. For, we grow in patience and experience, even as we deal with trials, but more than that, we come to realize that we have hope for tomorrow because we serve a great God.

The contrast in the story of the Prodigal Son in Luke 15 teaches us much about hope. The father and the older brother were strikingly different in their attitudes.

The father had never given up hope – he knew that his son had failed him and gone far from what he knew was right and yet, the father still desired to see the prodigal come to himself and return home.

On the other hand, the older brother not only had no hope for his younger brother, but he was also angry with him. The prodigal had wasted his money, he had lived in sin, and now, he had returned home just because he was out of money.

Certainly, there was no reason to trust the younger son. Yet, that is exactly what our Heavenly Father does for us.

Look for Hope in the Right Places

Part of the problem is that we look for hope in the wrong places. A number of years ago, a presidential candidate ran for office under the slogan “Hope and Change,” and yet, even though he was elected, I imagine most folks did not feel that their lives were significantly changed for the better.

Pursuing the things this world values—political power and wealth is guaranteed to bring emptiness. This is Satan’s pattern—he always over-promises and under-delivers.

This was what he did when he tempted Jesus, “All these things will I give thee, if thou wilt fall down and worship me” (Matthew 4:8). All of the things Satan offered, nothing compared with the glory that Jesus eventually received from the road that led to the cross.

In the same way, Satan would like to distract Christians from seeking the things that are valuable, and that will bring hope. Satan tells Christians that politics will not only change the world for the better, it is an easier way to change the world.

The Bible is clear that we build hope as we nurture our relationship with God and then work to help our brothers and sisters build that same relationship in their own lives. The reason that we can hope is not because people are so wonderful—we don’t have to live very long to realize that they aren’t. The reason we hope is because we serve an awesome, faithful God who walks with us through the worst of our trials.

Remember that We Have Undeserved Hope

Jesus’ messages about forgiveness make it clear that one of the major reasons that we have for forgiving others in our lives is that we have received great and undeserved forgiveness. The same is true for hope.

Each one of us was hopeless and without reason to expect to receive hope and we were still given a ray of light in the midst of our darkness. Maybe part of the reason that we have so much trouble hoping for good things for the people around us is that we do not remember how hopeless we were before we found grace.

If Jesus was able to bring hope to our hopeless existence, then certainly He can do wonderful things in the hearts and lives of others around us. The only people we should give up on are the ones that our Savior has given up on as well.

Small Efforts Do Make a Difference

I remember having a conversation with a young person who was planning to go into medicine and had a plan to go to a foreign country and serve the people there. As we were talking, an older man entered the conversation and shared that he saw little hope for change in developing countries.

The people in those countries just weren’t interested in getting better and didn’t do the minimum necessary to stave off things like worms and parasites. Doctors and nurses couldn’t make a difference in such an environment.

I could sense the heart of the youth sinking as this older man shared. He had experience, and he had given up hope. The sad thing was that he was also stealing the hope of someone who still had a desire to serve.

When I was in training, I had a surgeon tell me that family doctors didn’t really do anything. They simply kept their patients alive till their next office visit, whereas surgeons really “fixed” people—taking out (or off) the offending body part.

At the end of the day, small efforts do make a difference. I don’t do brain surgery, but I still can make a difference in someone else’s life— maybe just by spending a little time and listening and praying. This is true for all of us.

More than that, we come to realize that making this effort changes our own lives for the better. Jesus told the sheep that as they ministered to “the least of these my brethren,” they were ministering to Him.

Even if no one’s life is improved, our Savior knows our desires and feels our efforts, and will reward them someday.

A Few Things to Remember

When we face failures, we tend to move in one of two directions. Those of us who are optimists tend to believe that this episode was an isolated event and that the future is still bright. On the other hand, pessimists believe that failures are permanent, personal, and pervasive.

Pessimists believe that their failures are the result of intrinsic character flaws that they have and that these things affect all of their lives and are unlikely to change. Unlike the righteous man who falls to rise again, these people fall and lie where they fall, defeated at the outset.

When we are dealing with other people, we need to give them the same grace that we should give ourselves. They, too, are growing, and if they have a failure today, they will do better tomorrow. Maybe they will fail again, but they will at least “fail better.”

Conclusion

Cynicism is rife in our world. Many have given up hope for a better future, and it is understandable for those who have invested their hope in this world’s institutions. There is no real hope in government or in armies or in bureaucracy.

The song says, “Oh to have no hope in Jesus, how dark this world must be!” For, Jesus is the one who brings light into our darkness and allows us to continue, even when others fail us.

God is the one who redeems us. He is the one who sent the prophets, even though their messages were ignored, and the prophets were persecuted. He is the one who continues to hope for us, even when we have failed Him so many times in the past.

He is the reason we carry on. He is the reason that we have hope, not only for ourselves but also for our brothers.

“Dr. Waldron, Elsie butuh bantuan!” Suami Elsie tegas, hampir marah, saat ia menatapku. Di sisi lain, Elsie menatap lantai, seolah-olah ia hampir tidak ada di sana. Aku belum pernah bertemu keduanya sebelumnya dan agak kebingungan ingin tahu apa yang diperlukan dariku untuk menolongnya.

“Ada apa ini?” aku bertanya sambil membalik-balik catatannya. Ini masih di masa catatan kertas, dan aku menuju bagian laboratorium pada berkasnya. Tidak ada yang terlalu aneh yang kulihat di sana—enzim livernya sedikit meningkat, tetapi selain itu, semuanya tampak baik-baik saja.

“Ini masalah minumnya!” kata suaminya kepadaku. “Dia minum semakin banyak setiap malam. Dia tidak mau pergi ke luar kecuali untuk membeli wiski. Dia minum sampai pingsan setiap malam dan harus minum sesuatu setiap pagi untuk memulainya.”

“Apakah itu benar?” aku bertanya pada Elsie, merasa seperti seorang hakim yang memimpin sidang juri.

“Iya,” katanya. Wajahnya tanpa ekspresi, dan aku tak bisa mengetahui apakah dia ingin berada di sana atau tidak.

“Apakah kamu mau dibantu?” tanyaku padanya. Ini pertanyaan sarat makna. Banyak orang yang berjuang melawan alkoholisme tidak siap melepaskan cengkeramannya. Mungkin Elsie berbeda.

“Kurasa begitu,” katanya, dengan acuh tak acuh. Sekali lagi, aku tak bisa memastikan apakah dia ingin berada di sana atau tidak.

“Dengan tingkat kamu minum seperti ini, kamu akan membunuh diri dalam waktu setahun—mungkin dua paling lama—jika kamu tidak berhenti total dari alkohol,” kukatakan padanya. “Jika kamu mau, aku akan mencoba menemukan program rawat inap untuk mendetoksifikasi dan mengeluarkanmu dari alkohol.”

“Dia siap,” kata suaminya dengan tegas.

Saat berhadapan dengan seseorang yang minum berat, sangat penting agar mereka tidak berhenti minum begitu saja tanpa dukungan medis. Penghentian alkohol secara mendadak menyebabkan tubuh mengalami gejala putus zat yang dapat memicu keadaan yang disebut Delirium Tremens dan bahkan kejang.

Aku keluar dari ruang pemeriksaan untuk melakukan panggilan telepon. Tidak pernah mudah menemukan tempat bagi seseorang untuk menjalani rehabilitasi dari zat apa pun, dan butuh lebih dari satu setengah jam sebelum aku menemukan fasilitas yang bersedia menerima Elsie dan mencoba menolongnya berhenti dari wiski.

Dengan desahan, aku kembali masuk ke ruang pemeriksaannya. Aku takut tidak akan menemukan tempat baginya.

Aku memberitahu mereka tentang rencananya, dan suaminya mengangguk hebat, sementara Elsie terus menatap lantai dalam diam. “Bolehkah kita berdoa bersama sebelum kalian pergi?” tanyaku, dan ketika mereka mengangguk setuju, aku berdoa bersama mereka, memohon pembebasan dan kehadiran Yesus dalam hidup keduanya.

Mereka meninggalkan kantorku dengan perintah tindakan dan petunjuk ke mana harus pergi. Aku merasa senang sepanjang sisa pagi itu, tahu bahwa aku telah berusaha lebih dan benar-benar membuat perbedaan dalam kehidupan pasangan paruh baya ini.

Sekitar pukul 2 siang, aku menerima panggilan dari fasilitas rehab. Mereka bahkan tidak melihat bayangan Elsie atau suaminya, yang mengejutkan, karena hari itu cerah dan fasilitasnya tak begitu jauh. Dengan perasaan tenggelam, aku menekan nomor telepon pasangan itu.

“Dia tidak mau pergi!” kata suaminya padaku. “Dia bilang dia sudah memberitahuku sebelumnya. Dia akan mencoba mengurangi, tapi dia tidak mau masuk fasilitas rehab atau hal semacam itu. Kurasa bilang saja pada mereka bahwa kami akan memberi tahu jika dia berubah pikiran.”

Perawatku menelepon fasilitas rehab dan memberi kabar buruk itu, dan aku duduk di kursiku, terpana. Apa lagi yang bisa kulakukan? Adakah solusi untuk Elsie—sesuatu yang berbeda yang bisa kukatakan yang akan membuat perbedaan dalam hidupnya?

Kira-kira setahun kemudian, aku menerima kabar duka bahwa Elsie meninggal di rumah. Aku yakin keadaan akan berbeda jika dia pergi ke rehab dan menyerahkan kendali kepada Yesus. Semua itu tidak terjadi, dan aku merasakan sinisme merayap ke dalam hatiku.

Cynicism

Kita hidup di zaman sinisme. Di Yunani kuno, para sinis adalah sekumpulan orang aneh yang ahli dalam bersikap pemarah dan mengucapkan hal-hal menyakitkan (mereka akan mengatakan kebenaran) kepada orang lain. Mereka sering berpakaian compang-camping dan berperilaku sedemikian rupa sehingga kebanyakan warga Athena yang sopan tidak ingin dekat dengan mereka.

Saat ini, sinisme berarti kecenderungan untuk mempercayai hal terburuk tentang orang dan keadaan. Orang sinis percaya bahwa semua orang hanya dimotivasi oleh kepentingan diri sendiri dan bahwa peristiwa buruk cenderung menang.

Banyak dokter muda idealis dan sangat penuh harap. Mereka percaya jika mereka berusaha sekuat tenaga, mereka bisa membuat dampak nyata dan positif dalam kehidupan pasien mereka. Sayangnya, seiring berjalannya waktu dan mereka berusaha keras namun pasiennya tidak berubah, mereka bisa menyerah. Para dokter ini masih berusaha, tetapi mereka tidak lagi benar-benar berharap usaha mereka akan banyak berpengaruh.

Tampaknya orang yang terlibat dalam politik seringkali bermula dengan niat terbaik. Mereka memandangnya sebagai jalan untuk mengubah masyarakat menjadi lebih baik. Sayangnya, seiring waktu berganti dan wajah-wajah yang memegang kekuasaan berubah, kebijakan tak benar-benar berubah, mereka cenderung menjadi sinis.

Terkadang sinisme ini ditujukan kepada semua politisi. Kadang hanya kemarahan terhadap anggota partai yang berseberangan. Harapan digantikan oleh sinisme.

Cynicism in the Bible

Jika ada kitab di Alkitab yang tampak seolah ditulis oleh seorang yang sinis, itu adalah kitab Pengkhotbah. Sang Pengkhotbah, yang kita pahami sebagai Salomo, mencantumkan semua hal yang dicobanya untuk mencari sukacita.

Dalam pasal 2:17-23 Salomo menggambarkan kerja sebagai sia-sia. Ia mengakhiri dengan berkata, “For what hath man of all his labour, and of the vexation of his heart, wherein he hath laboured under the sun? For all his days are sorrows, and his travail grief; yea, his heart taketh not rest in the night. This is also vanity.” (Ecclesiastes 2:22,23)

Ia melihat dunia dikuasai tiran dan sedikit yang bisa dilakukan orang-orang tentang hal itu. Salomo bahkan mengatakan bahwa kekuasaan politik tidak berarti: “Better is a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished. For out of prison he cometh to reign; whereas also he that is born in his kingdom becometh poor” (Ecclesiastes 4:13).

Dalam Pengkhotbah 6:6, ia tampak merendahkan hidup panjang. “Yea, though he live a thousand years twice told, yet hath he seen no good: do not all go to one place?”

Tentu saja, ia mengakhiri buku pendeknya dengan perintah untuk mengingat Pencipta kita di masa muda kita. Ada berkat bagi mereka yang memilih untuk berfokus pada Tuhan ketika mereka masih memiliki sedikit tenaga, dan bukan ketika mereka sudah tua dan muak, seperti Salomo.

Kemudian, tampak seolah-olah Allah telah menyerah pada umat-Nya. Ia masih mengutus nabi kepada mereka, tetapi Ia tahu tanpa ragu bahwa umat itu akan menolak untuk merespons. “Therefore thou shalt speak all these words unto them; but they will not hearken to thee: thou shalt also call unto them; but they will not answer thee” (Jeremiah 7:27).

Bahkan dalam Perjanjian Baru, Paulus memberitahu Timotius bahwa waktunya akan datang ketika orang tidak lagi mendengarkan doktrin yang sehat. “For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine; but after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears;” (2 Timothy 4:3).

Dengan memilih dan mengambil kutipan-kutipan ini, kita bisa pulang dengan pandangan yang sangat suram tentang masa depan dan, lebih khusus, tentang kesediaan manusia untuk berubah. Tampak tak ada gunanya berinvestasi pada orang-orang di sekitar kita. Mereka penuh nestapa dan seolah-olah sama kemungkinannya berubah seperti seekor tupai kecil menguasai kalkulus diferensial.

The Opposite of Cynicism

Lawannya sinisme adalah pengharapan. Yaitu keyakinan bahwa masa depan bisa lebih baik.

Menarik bahwa Rasul Paulus berbicara tentang kesengsaraan dalam suratnya kepada jemaat di Roma, “And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; and patience, experience; and experience, hope: and hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us” (Romans 5:3-5).

Kita mungkin belum sampai pada tempat di mana kita memuliakan pencobaan yang kita alami, tetapi tentu saja, pencobaan itu seharusnya membawa kita hal-hal lain yang disebutnya. Karena kita bertumbuh dalam kesabaran dan pengalaman, bahkan saat kita menghadapi pencobaan, tetapi lebih dari itu, kita sampai pada kesadaran bahwa kita memiliki pengharapan untuk esok karena kita melayani Allah yang besar.

Kontras dalam kisah Anak yang Hilang dalam Lukas 15 mengajarkan banyak hal tentang pengharapan. Sikap sang ayah dan saudara sulung sangat berbeda.

Ayah itu tidak pernah kehilangan harapan—ia tahu anaknya telah mengecewakannya dan pergi jauh dari apa yang ia anggap benar, namun sang ayah masih ingin melihat si terhilang segera sadar dan kembali pulang.

Sementara itu, saudara sulung tidak hanya tidak punya harapan untuk adiknya, tetapi ia juga marah kepadanya. Sang terhilang telah menyia-nyiakan uangnya, hidup dalam dosa, dan kini kembali hanya karena telah kehabisan uang.

Tentu saja, tidak ada alasan untuk mempercayai anak yang lebih muda itu. Namun, itulah yang Bapa Surgawi kita lakukan bagi kita.

Look for Hope in the Right Places

Salah satu masalah adalah kita mencari harapan di tempat yang salah. Beberapa tahun lalu, seorang calon presiden maju dengan slogan “Hope and Change,” namun meskipun ia terpilih, kurasa kebanyakan orang tidak merasakan kehidupan mereka berubah secara signifikan menjadi lebih baik.

Mengejar hal-hal yang dihargai dunia ini—kekuasaan politik dan kekayaan—jaminan membawa kehampaaan. Ini pola Setan—ia selalu melebih-lebihkan janji dan mengecewakan.

Itulah yang dilakukannya saat ia mencobai Yesus, “All these things will I give thee, if thou wilt fall down and worship me” (Matthew 4:8). Semua yang ditawarkan Setan, tak ada yang sebanding dengan kemuliaan yang akhirnya diterima Yesus dari jalan yang menuju salib.

Dengan cara yang sama, Setan ingin mengalihkan orang Kristen dari mencari hal-hal yang berharga dan yang membawa pengharapan. Setan mengatakan kepada orang Kristen bahwa politik tidak hanya akan mengubah dunia menjadi lebih baik, tapi juga merupakan cara yang lebih mudah untuk mengubah dunia.

Alkitab jelas bahwa kita membangun pengharapan saat kita memelihara hubungan kita dengan Allah dan kemudian bekerja membantu saudara-saudari kita membangun hubungan yang sama dalam hidup mereka. Alasan kita bisa berharap bukan karena orang begitu hebat—kita tidak perlu hidup lama untuk menyadari bahwa mereka tidak demikian. Alasan kita berharap adalah karena kita melayani Allah yang luar biasa dan setia yang berjalan bersama kita melalui masa-masa tersulit.

Remember that We Have Undeserved Hope

Pelajaran Yesus tentang pengampunan menegaskan bahwa salah satu alasan utama kita mengampuni orang lain adalah karena kita telah menerima pengampunan yang besar dan tidak pantas. Hal yang sama berlaku untuk pengharapan.

Setiap dari kita tadinya tanpa harapan dan tanpa alasan untuk mengharapkan mendapatkan pengharapan, namun kita tetap diberi secercah cahaya di tengah kegelapan kita. Mungkin sebagian alasan kita begitu sulit mengharapkan kebaikan bagi orang di sekitar kita adalah karena kita tak mengingat betapa putus harapnya kita sebelum kita menemukan kasih karunia.

Jika Yesus mampu membawa pengharapan ke dalam kehidupan kita yang tanpa harapan, maka tentu Dia dapat melakukan hal-hal ajaib di hati dan hidup orang-orang di sekitar kita. Satu-satunya orang yang harus kita putuskan adalah orang yang juga telah ditinggalkan oleh Juruselamat kita.

Small Efforts Do Make a Difference

Aku ingat percakapan dengan seorang muda yang berencana menekuni dunia kedokteran dan bercita-cita pergi ke negara asing untuk melayani orang di sana. Saat kami berbicara, seorang pria yang lebih tua masuk dan berkata bahwa ia melihat sedikit harapan untuk perubahan di negara berkembang.

Orang-orang di negara-negara itu tidak tertarik memperbaiki diri dan tidak melakukan hal minimal yang perlu untuk mencegah hal-hal seperti cacing dan parasit. Dokter dan perawat tak bisa membuat perbedaan dalam lingkungan seperti itu.

Aku bisa merasakan semangat si muda merosot saat pria tua itu berbagi pendapat. Dia punya pengalaman, dan dia telah kehilangan harapan. Hal menyedihkan adalah ia juga mencuri harapan dari seseorang yang masih punya keinginan untuk melayani.

Waktu aku masih dalam pelatihan, seorang ahli bedah pernah mengatakan bahwa dokter keluarga sebenarnya tidak melakukan apa-apa. Mereka hanya menjaga pasien tetap hidup sampai kunjungan berikutnya, sedangkan ahli bedah benar-benar “memperbaiki” orang—mengangkat (atau memotong) bagian tubuh yang bermasalah.

Pada akhirnya, usaha kecil memang membuat perbedaan. Aku tidak melakukan operasi otak, tetapi aku tetap dapat membuat perbedaan dalam kehidupan orang lain—mungkin hanya dengan meluangkan sedikit waktu untuk mendengarkan dan berdoa. Ini berlaku bagi kita semua.

Lebih dari itu, kita menyadari bahwa melakukan usaha ini mengubah hidup kita sendiri menjadi lebih baik. Yesus mengatakan kepada domba-domba bahwa ketika mereka melayani “yang paling hina di antara saudara-Ku ini,” mereka sedang melayani Dia.

Bahkan jika tidak ada kehidupan yang membaik, Juruselamat kita mengetahui keinginan kita dan merasakan usaha kita, dan akan memberi upah suatu hari nanti.

A Few Things to Remember

Ketika kita menghadapi kegagalan, kita cenderung bergerak ke salah satu dari dua arah. Mereka dari kita yang optimis cenderung percaya bahwa episode ini hanyalah kejadian terpisah dan bahwa masa depan masih cerah. Sebaliknya, pesimis percaya bahwa kegagalan bersifat permanen, personal, dan menyeluruh.

Pesimis percaya bahwa kegagalan mereka adalah akibat cacat karakter intrinsik yang mereka miliki dan bahwa hal-hal ini memengaruhi seluruh hidup mereka dan tidak mungkin berubah. Berbeda dengan orang benar yang jatuh lalu bangkit kembali, orang-orang ini jatuh dan tetap terbaring di tempat mereka jatuh, kalah sejak awal.

Saat kita berurusan dengan orang lain, kita perlu memberi mereka kasih karunia yang sama yang seharusnya kita berikan pada diri sendiri. Mereka pun sedang bertumbuh, dan jika hari ini mereka gagal, besok mereka akan melakukan lebih baik. Mungkin mereka akan gagal lagi, tetapi setidaknya mereka akan “gagal dengan lebih baik.”

Conclusion

Sinisme merajalela di dunia kita. Banyak yang telah kehilangan harapan akan masa depan yang lebih baik, dan hal itu dapat dimengerti bagi mereka yang menaruh harapan pada lembaga-lembaga dunia ini. Tidak ada harapan sejati dalam pemerintahan atau dalam tentara atau dalam birokrasi.

Lagu mengatakan, “Oh to have no hope in Jesus, how dark this world must be!” Sebab Yesuslah yang membawa terang ke dalam kegelapan kita dan memungkinkan kita terus berjalan, bahkan ketika orang lain mengecewakan kita.

Allahlah yang menebus kita. Dialah yang mengutus para nabi, meskipun pesan mereka diabaikan dan para nabi dianiaya. Dialah yang terus berharap bagi kita, bahkan ketika kita telah berkali-kali mengecewakan-Nya di masa lalu.

Dialah alasan kita terus maju. Dialah alasan kita memiliki pengharapan, bukan hanya untuk diri kita sendiri tetapi juga untuk saudara-saudara kita.

Eight-year-old Jamin wasn’t very smart. Or at least that’s what his older brother told him. Almost daily, brother Kenny found ways to remind Jamin of his shortcomings and laugh at his blunders.

“Jamin, you will never be smart”, Kenny said. Deep inside Jamin felt resigned to a life of muddled trip-ups. Would he always be clumsy? Would he always say things wrong? That’s what Kenny said.

Jamin believed Kenny’s lectures with wide-eyed belief. Kenny was three years older than him, so he must be right. Very well, then Jamin would be simple. Kenny would be smart. Life was not fair. Dad and Mom disliked Kenny’s proud talk and punished him whenever they walked in on one of his speeches. But Kenny had a way of avoiding earshot. So he continued mocking Jamin.

Grandma Otto watched these trials from her rocker on the porch. She was a quiet old lady.

“Jamin, do you know where Kenny is?” Mom asked with a smile. “It’s almost supper time.”

“He went to check his coyote traps. I’ll go find him.”

There was a chill in the air as he tramped up over the lawn, and the sun was growing old as he crossed the border of the woods. The fleeting shadows scurried over the hills. The chill deepened as he stumped further in. He breathed the rich air and followed Kenny’s trail. Eventually, the trail would end up in a meadow, but Jamin hoped he would find Kenny before he had to go that far. The various traps had been checked already, so Jamin knew Kenny had come this way. Jamin trudged on resolutely. His golden head caught the tired beams that fled from the sun as they flickered through the trees. And soon those too had faded leaving behind the musky smell of the woods. The fall webworms had been at work, and their web curtains shuttered from branches overhead.

At length, as the trees subdued and thinned, and the meadow appeared Jamin knew this was the end of his brother’s trap route. If Kenny wasn’t here, he wouldn’t know where else to look.

But Kenny was there. As Jamin clumped into the meadow, he could see a frustrated heap to his right. The heap’s voice had a familiar ring. The heap’s face was lit in pain. The heap was Kenny. “Are you alright? What happened?” Jamin felt strange, seeing Kenny scrunched in the dirt. Kenny was smart. “Did you step in a trap?”

“Yes, Jamin. I..I wasn’t looking where I was going. Help me. Please.”

Jamin bent and found an ankle firmly held in the jaws of a steel trap. Darkness stained the ground around Kenny. Quickly, Jamin’s strong arms pried open the jaws. Kenny reeled free. “Can you walk?”

“Yes. I think so. If you support me, I can hobble along.”

“Dad and Mom will be worried. We’ve missed supper.”

Sure enough, as the brothers hobbled back through the woods, they heard the long calling of their father. Jamin called back, and he was by their side in a moment, seeing the ankle and scooping up Kenny like a hurt sheep. The odd little band hurried home, and the screen door banged shut as Dad swept across the porch. Jamin went to the wash house and scrubbed his hands. He headed for the front door.

“Jamin.” It was Grandma. The porch light showed her in her old rocker. A heavy comforter lay on her shoulders.

“Yes, Grandma?”

“Do you think you are not very smart?”

“That’s what Kenny says.” Jamin squirmed.

“You were strong enough to open the trap, and Kenny wasn’t. You were brave enough to find him in the dark. Lots of young boys wouldn’t be.” Jamin was silent. Grandma Otto rocked some more, then smiled. “God made you the way you are for a reason, Jamin. He made Kenny the way he is for a reason. He has a plan for you, and a place only you can fill, you know.”

Jamin turned and walked into the warm kitchen. He was smiling.

Der achtjährige Jamin war nicht sehr klug. Oder zumindest sagte sein älterer Bruder das von ihm. Fast täglich fand Kenny Wege, Jamin an seine Schwächen zu erinnern und über seine Missgeschicke zu lachen.

„Jamin, du wirst nie klug sein“, sagte Kenny. Tief in seinem Inneren fühlte sich Jamin einem Leben voller verlegener Patzer ergeben. Würde er immer unbeholfen sein? Würde er immer Dinge falsch sagen? So sagte es Kenny.

Jamin glaubte Kennys Belehrungen mit weit aufgerissenen Augen. Kenny war drei Jahre älter als er, also musste er wohl recht haben. Na gut, dann würde Jamin eben einfältig sein. Kenny würde klug sein. Das Leben war nicht fair. Vater und Mutter missfielen Kennys stolze Reden und bestraften ihn, wann immer sie eine seiner Vorträge unterbrachen. Aber Kenny wusste, wie er aus der Hörweite blieb. Also machte er weiter und verspottete Jamin.

Oma Otto beobachtete diese Prüfungen von ihrem Schaukelstuhl auf der Veranda aus. Sie war eine stille alte Dame.

„Jamin, weißt du, wo Kenny ist?“ fragte Mutter mit einem Lächeln. „Es ist fast Abendessenzeit.“

„Er ist losgegangen, um seine Kojotenfallen zu prüfen. Ich werde ihn finden.“

Es war kühl, als er über den Rasen stapfte, und die Sonne wurde alt, als er die Grenze des Waldes überquerte. Flüchtige Schatten huschten über die Hügel. Die Kühle verstärkte sich, je weiter er hineinstampfte. Er atmete die schwere Luft ein und folgte Kennys Spur. Schließlich würde die Spur in einer Wiese enden, aber Jamin hoffte, Kenny zu finden, bevor er so weit gehen musste. Die verschiedenen Fallen waren bereits geprüft worden, also wusste Jamin, dass Kenny diesen Weg gekommen war. Jamin stapfte entschlossen weiter. Sein goldenes Haar fing die müden Strahlen ein, die vor der Sonne aus den Bäumen flackerten. Und bald waren auch diese verschwunden und hinterließen den moschusartigen Geruch des Waldes. Die Herbstspinner hatten gearbeitet, und ihre Netzvorhänge hingen von den Ästen über ihm herab.

Als die Bäume sich schließlich lichteten und die Wiese erschien, wusste Jamin, dass dies das Ende von Kennys Fallenroute war. Wenn Kenny nicht hier war, würde er nicht wissen, wo sonst er suchen sollte.

Aber Kenny war da. Als Jamin in die Wiese stapfte, sah er zu seiner Rechten einen frustrierten Haufen. Die Stimme des Haufens klang vertraut. Das Gesicht des Haufens war vor Schmerz verzogen. Der Haufen war Kenny. „Geht es dir gut? Was ist passiert?“ Jamin fühlte sich merkwürdig, Kenny so zusammengesunken im Dreck zu sehen. Kenny war doch klug. „Bist du in eine Falle getreten?“

„Ja, Jamin. Ich… ich habe nicht darauf geachtet, wo ich hintrat. Hilf mir. Bitte.“

Jamin beugte sich und fand einen Knöchel, der fest in den Backen einer Stahlfalle gehalten wurde. Dunkelheit zeichnete den Boden um Kenny herum. Schnell presste Jamin seine kräftigen Arme in die Falle und sprengte die Backen auseinander. Kenny stürzte heraus. „Kannst du laufen?“

„Ja. Ich glaube schon. Wenn du mich stützt, kann ich hinkend gehen.“

„Vater und Mutter werden sich sorgen. Wir haben das Abendessen verpasst.“

Und tatsächlich, als die Brüder humpelnd durch den Wald zurückgingen, hörten sie den weiten Ruf ihres Vaters. Jamin rief zurück, und im nächsten Moment war er an ihrer Seite, sah den Knöchel und nahm Kenny auf wie ein verletztes Schaf. Die eigentümliche kleine Schar eilte nach Hause, und die Fliegengittertür schlug zu, als Vater über die Veranda schritt. Jamin ging zum Waschhaus und wusch sich die Hände. Dann ging er zur Haustür.

„Jamin.“ Es war Oma. Das Verandalicht zeigte sie in ihrem alten Schaukelstuhl. Eine schwere Decke lag über ihren Schultern.

„Ja, Oma?“

„Denkst du, du bist nicht sehr klug?“

„Das sagt Kenny.“ Jamin wand sich.

„Du warst stark genug, die Falle zu öffnen, und Kenny war es nicht. Du warst mutig genug, ihn im Dunkeln zu finden. Viele junge Jungen wären es nicht.“ Jamin schwieg. Oma Otto schaukelte noch ein wenig, dann lächelte sie. „Gott hat dich so gemacht, wie du bist, aus einem Grund, Jamin. Er hat Kenny so gemacht, wie er ist, aus einem Grund. Er hat einen Plan für dich und einen Platz, den nur du füllen kannst, weißt du.“

Jamin drehte sich um und ging in die warme Küche. Er lächelte.

How unbelievable it is that God can take a wretched sinner, void of the fear of the Lord, and turn him into a blood-washed saint and preacher of the gospel! In this story, we see God’s life-changing power at work in our hymn writer’s life.

In the small cemetery of a churchyard in Olney, England, stands a granite tombstone with this inscription, written by Newton himself before his death:

John Newton, once an infidel and libertine, a servant of slaves in Africa, was, by the rich mercy of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, preserved, restored, pardoned, and appointed to preach the faith he had long labored to destroy!

This epitaph aptly describes the unusual and colorful life of this man, one of the great evangelical preachers of the eighteenth century. His testimony was, “By the grace of God, I am what I am!”

“Amazing Grace” was a hymn published in 1779, with words written in 1772 by the English poet and Anglican clergyman John Newton (1725–1807). “Amazing Grace” is probably the most beloved hymn of the last two centuries. This hymn is estimated to be performed 10 million times annually. It has appeared on over 11,000 albums and translated into about 60 languages. It was referenced in Harriet Beecher Stowe’s anti-slavery novel Uncle Tom’s Cabin. It had a surge in popularity during two of America’s greatest crises: the Civil War and the Vietnam War.

Ironically, this stirring song, closely associated with the African-American community, was written by a former slave trader, John Newton.

John was born on July 24, 1725, in Wapping, England, to a seafaring father, John Newton, Sr., and a devout Christian mother, Elizabeth Newton. His father loved him but was gone at sea most of the time. On the other hand, his mother was tender and nurturing, teaching him the Word of God. She would instruct him in memorizing the Bible whole chapters at a time and took him to church. Unfortunately, when he was almost seven, his mother died of tuberculosis. His father remarried a short time later and sent him to a boarding school. During his time at the boarding school, he made bad friends. His character disintegrated to the point that he was dismissed from one school and moved to another. By the time he was 11 years old, the boarding schools didn’t want him, so his father took him along to sea. He spent the next six years on the Atlantic Ocean with his father.

When John was 17, his father arranged to send him to Jamaica for a well-paying job overseeing a plantation. On his way, while waiting for the ship’s departure, John received an invitation to the home of some old-time friends, the Catletts. It was in this home that John’s mother had died ten years earlier. As he reacquainted himself with them, he got to know their daughter, Mary. John and Mary’s mothers were best of friends. John had been invited to stay four days, but he stayed two weeks and missed the ship to Jamaica.

At age 18, John was conscripted into the Royal Navy, and his life went from bad to worse. He wanted to return and see Mary, so he deserted the ship but was caught, publicly flogged, and laid in irons. His life on the ship was so profane that even the other ungodly sailors cringed at his curses and blasphemies. He gained the title “The Great Blasphemer” and was such an unwanted man on the ship that he was sent to work on a slave ship.

One of the owners of the slave ship where he now worked, offered John a job once they reached the African coast. However, once on shore, he was tied up and forced to work with little food, clothing, or shelter. He sent several letters back to his father during this time, pleading for help.

A ship called The Greyhound was sailing near the coast, which John had now called home. The captain had been instructed by John’s father to look for his son. The ship, while being almost too far from shore to trade, decided to give trading a try. A friend of John’s rowed out from shore to trade. As he turned to leave, the captain asked him whether he knew anyone named John Newton. He did to the captain’s surprise, and John was brought on board to go home.

On board the ship, Newton picked up a copy of Thomas á Kempis’s Christian classic, The Imitation of Christ. He had never encountered anything like it, and he began to wonder if the Christian claims might be true. That night, on March 10, 1748, a fierce storm nearly swamped the ship. Men, animals, and provisions were swept overboard. The storm awakened Newton, the ship’s rotten timbers broken by the waves and floodwater swirling into his cabin. John prayed for the first time in years.

The Greyhound thrashed about in the North Atlantic storm for over 11 days. With little hope of survival, the sailors mechanically worked the pumps, trying to keep the vessel afloat. On the eleventh day of the storm, John was too exhausted to pump, so he was tied to the helm, where he did his best to hold the ship to its course. From one o’clock until midnight, he was at the helm. He feared he was going to die, and if the Christian faith were true, then he surely would not be forgiven. He reflected on all he had done over the past few years. His life seemed as ruined and wrecked as the battered ship he was trying to steer through the storm. During those long and grueling hours, Newton cried out to God like he never had before, and that was the turning point in his life.

That was a day John Newton remembered ever after. “On that day, the Lord sent from on high and delivered me out of deep waters.” Over 50 years later, John wrote in his diary on March 21, 1805: “Not well able to write; but I endeavor to observe the return of this day with humiliation, prayer, and praise.”

Only God’s amazing grace could take a rude, profane, slave-trading sailor and transform him into a child of God. John never ceased to stand in awe of God’s work in his life. He took an interest in prayer, reading and meditating on the Scriptures, and only speaking words pleasing to God.

On his return home, Mary and her parents recognized the change the Lord had brought in John. The two were married on February 1, 1750.

For the next four years, Newton was captain of his own slave ship. This occupation kept him separated from Mary for months at a time. While they were apart, the two corresponded constantly. In his letters, John repeatedly wrote how their love and marriage increased his thankfulness and gratefulness to the Lord. “... When I indulge myself with a particular thought of you, it usually carries me on farther and brings me upon my knees to bless the Lord for giving me such a treasure and to pray for your peace and welfare”

John endeavored to “Christianize” his slave ship by holding Sunday services for his crew of 30 sin-hardened men. He made three more voyages to bring slaves from Africa to North America. As he planned his fourth trip, he became sick with malaria. God used this sickness to end his involvement in the slave trade.

As John began a new chapter in his life, he felt called to be a minister. For more than 50 years, he preached the gospel and was one of the most influential men of his day.

John Newton often composed a hymn to go with his Sunday evening services. In 1779, 280 of these were collected and combined with 68 hymns by Newton’s friend and parishioner, William Cowper, and published as the Olney Hymns. The most famous of all the Olney Hymns, “Faith’s Review and Expectation”, grew out of David’s exclamation in 1 Chronicles 17:16-17. We know it today as “Amazing Grace”. “Amazing Grace” originally had six stanzas, and the last verse was added about a century later. Most hymnals have four or five of these verses.

As minister in the church, John continued to be more and more troubled by the slave trade that was still going on. In 1788, 34 years after he left the slave trade, He wrote a book entitled Thoughts Upon the African Slave Trade and sent it to all the members of parliament. This book brought an awareness to the public of the evils of the slave trade. He quotes this, “Needless to say, the capturing, selling and transporting of black slaves to the plantations in the West Indies and America was a cruel and vicious way of life.” With the help and providence of God, John saw the day, several months before his death, in 1807, when slavery was officially banned from England.

When John was in his sixties, his beloved wife Mary passed away. This was a great trial for John, and he spent the remaining 17 years of his life without her.

After John suffered a stroke and shortly before his death, a spokesman for the church encouraged Newton to consider retiring from preaching because of failing health, eyesight, and memory. John replied, “What, shall the old African blasphemer stop while he can still speak? I will continue to preach. Although my memory’s fading, I remember two things very clearly: I am a great sinner, and Christ is a great Savior.”

The last words of John Newton as he lay on his deathbed were as follows: “I am still in the land of the dying; I shall be in the land of the living soon.”

The tune “Amazing Grace” is an early American folk melody. It was first known as a plantation melody entitled “Loving Lambs”. This tune was first published in 1831 in the book The Virginia Harmony. The majority of hymn books published after this time included this song. In 1910, Edwin O. Excell added the last verse, which eventually replaced the last three original verses of the song. His edition of the song is most common in our hymnals today. Several other Olney hymns by Newton continue to be sung today, including “How Sweet the Name of Jesus Sounds” and “Glorious Things of Thee are Spoken”.

Ni jambo la kushangaza mno kwamba Mungu anaweza kumchukua mwenye dhambi mnyonge, asiye na hofu ya Bwana, na kumgeuza kuwa mtakatifu aliyeoshwa kwa damu na mhubiri wa injili! Katika simulizi hili, tunaona nguvu za Mungu zinazobadili maisha zikifanya kazi katika maisha ya mwandishi wetu wa tenzi.

Katika makaburi madogo yaliyo kwenye uwanja wa kanisa huko Olney, Uingereza, kuna jiwe la kaburi la graniti lenye maandishi haya, yaliyoandikwa na Newton mwenyewe kabla ya kifo chake:

John Newton, ambaye zamani alikuwa asiyeamini na mwenye maisha ya uasherati, mtumishi wa watumwa barani Afrika, kwa rehema nyingi za Bwana na Mwokozi wetu Yesu Kristo, alihifadhiwa, akarejeshwa, akasamehewa, na kuteuliwa kuhubiri imani ambayo kwa muda mrefu alikuwa amejitahidi kuiangamiza!

Maandishi haya ya kaburini yanaeleza vizuri maisha yasiyo ya kawaida na yaliyojaa matukio ya mtu huyu, mmoja wa wahubiri wakuu wa kiinjili wa karne ya kumi na nane. Ushuhuda wake ulikuwa, “Kwa neema ya Mungu, mimi ni hivi nilivyo!”

“Neema ya Ajabu” ni wimbo uliochapishwa mwaka 1779, wenye maneno yaliyoandikwa mwaka 1772 na mshairi Mwingereza na kasisi wa Kianglikana John Newton (1725–1807). Huenda “Neema ya Ajabu” ndio wimbo unaopendwa zaidi katika karne mbili zilizopita. Inakadiriwa kwamba wimbo huu huimbwa au kuchezwa mara milioni 10 kila mwaka. Umeonekana kwenye albamu zaidi ya 11,000 na kutafsiriwa katika lugha karibu 60. Ulitajwa katika riwaya ya Harriet Beecher Stowe inayopinga utumwa, Uncle Tom’s Cabin. Umaarufu wake uliongezeka sana wakati wa majanga mawili makubwa zaidi ya Marekani: Vita vya Wenyewe kwa Wenyewe na Vita vya Vietnam.

Kwa namna ya kushangaza, wimbo huu unaogusa moyo, unaohusishwa kwa karibu na jamii ya Waamerika wenye asili ya Afrika, uliandikwa na mtu aliyekuwa mfanyabiashara wa watumwa, John Newton.

John alizaliwa tarehe 24 Julai 1725, huko Wapping, Uingereza, kwa baba aliyekuwa baharia, John Newton, Sr., na mama aliyekuwa Mkristo mwenye bidii, Elizabeth Newton. Baba yake alimpenda lakini muda mwingi alikuwa baharini. Kwa upande mwingine, mama yake alikuwa mpole na mwenye kumlea kwa upendo, akimfundisha Neno la Mungu. Alimfundisha kukariri Biblia kwa sura nzima moja baada ya nyingine na kumpeleka kanisani. Kwa bahati mbaya, alipokaribia kutimiza miaka saba, mama yake alikufa kwa kifua kikuu. Baba yake alioa tena muda mfupi baadaye na kumpeleka shule ya bweni. Akiwa shuleni humo, alipata marafiki wabaya. Tabia yake iliharibika kiasi kwamba alifukuzwa katika shule moja na kuhamishiwa nyingine. Alipofikisha umri wa miaka 11, shule za bweni hazikumtaka, hivyo baba yake akaenda naye baharini. Alitumia miaka sita iliyofuata katika Bahari ya Atlantiki pamoja na baba yake.

John alipokuwa na miaka 17, baba yake alipanga kumpeleka Jamaica kwa kazi yenye mshahara mzuri ya kusimamia shamba kubwa. Akiwa njiani, alipokuwa akisubiri meli iondoke, John alipata mwaliko wa kwenda nyumbani kwa marafiki wa zamani, familia ya Catlett. Ni katika nyumba hiyo ambapo mama yake John alikuwa amefariki miaka kumi iliyotangulia. Alipokuwa akifahamiana nao tena, alimjua binti yao, Mary. Mama zake John na Mary walikuwa marafiki wa karibu sana. John alikuwa amealikwa kukaa siku nne, lakini alikaa wiki mbili na kuachwa na meli ya kwenda Jamaica.

Akiwa na umri wa miaka 18, John aliandikishwa kwa lazima katika Jeshi la Wanamaji la Kifalme, na maisha yake yakazidi kuwa mabaya. Alitaka kurudi kumwona Mary, hivyo akatoroka melini, lakini alikamatwa, akapigwa mijeledi hadharani, na kufungwa kwa minyororo ya chuma. Maisha yake melini yalikuwa ya kufuru kiasi kwamba hata mabaharia wengine wasiomcha Mungu walishtushwa na matusi na kufuru zake. Alipewa jina “Mkufuru Mkuu” na alikuwa mtu asiyetakiwa melini kiasi kwamba alitumwa kufanya kazi katika meli ya watumwa.

Mmoja wa wamiliki wa meli ya watumwa ambamo sasa alikuwa akifanya kazi alimwahidi John kazi mara tu watakapofika pwani ya Afrika. Hata hivyo, alipofika nchi kavu, alifungwa na kulazimishwa kufanya kazi akiwa na chakula, mavazi, na makazi haba. Wakati huo alimtumia baba yake barua kadhaa, akiomba msaada kwa kusihi.

Meli iliyoitwa The Greyhound ilikuwa ikisafiri karibu na pwani ambayo sasa John alikuwa akiita nyumbani. Nahodha alikuwa ameagizwa na baba yake John amtafute mwanawe. Ingawa meli ilikuwa karibu mbali mno na ufuo kufanya biashara, waliamua kujaribu kufanya biashara. Rafiki mmoja wa John alipiga makasia kutoka ufuoni kwenda kufanya biashara. Alipogeuka kuondoka, nahodha alimuuliza ikiwa alimjua mtu aliyeitwa John Newton. Kwa mshangao wa nahodha, alimjua, na John akaletwa melini ili arudi nyumbani.

Akiwa melini, Newton alichukua nakala ya kitabu maarufu cha Kikristo cha Thomas á Kempis, The Imitation of Christ. Hakuwahi kukutana na kitu kama hicho, na akaanza kujiuliza kama madai ya Ukristo yanaweza kuwa ya kweli. Usiku huo, tarehe 10 Machi 1748, dhoruba kali ilikaribia kuizamisha meli. Watu, wanyama, na mahitaji ya safari yalisombwa na kutupwa baharini. Dhoruba ilimwamsha Newton, huku mbao zilizooza za meli zikivunjwa na mawimbi na maji yakizunguka na kuingia katika chumba chake. John aliomba kwa mara ya kwanza baada ya miaka mingi.

The Greyhound ilirushwa huku na huku katika dhoruba ya Atlantiki ya Kaskazini kwa zaidi ya siku 11. Wakiwa na tumaini dogo la kuokoka, mabaharia waliendesha pampu kwa mazoea tu, wakijaribu kuifanya meli iendelee kuelea. Katika siku ya kumi na moja ya dhoruba, John alikuwa amechoka sana asiweze kusukuma pampu, hivyo akafungwa kwenye usukani, ambako alijitahidi kadiri alivyoweza kuifanya meli ibaki kwenye njia yake. Kuanzia saa saba mchana hadi usiku wa manane, alikuwa kwenye usukani. Aliogopa kwamba angekufa, na kama imani ya Kikristo ilikuwa ya kweli, basi bila shaka asingesamehewa. Alitafakari yote aliyokuwa amefanya katika miaka michache iliyopita. Maisha yake yalionekana kuharibika na kuvunjika kama meli iliyopigwa vibaya ambayo alikuwa akijaribu kuiongoza katika dhoruba. Katika saa hizo ndefu na zenye kuchosha sana, Newton alimlilia Mungu kwa namna ambayo hakuwahi kufanya hapo awali, na huo ukawa wakati wa mabadiliko makubwa katika maisha yake.

Hiyo ilikuwa siku ambayo John Newton aliikumbuka daima baadaye. “Siku hiyo, Bwana alituma msaada kutoka juu na kuniokoa katika maji yenye kina kirefu.” Zaidi ya miaka 50 baadaye, John aliandika katika shajara yake tarehe 21 Machi 1805: “Siwezi kuandika vizuri; lakini ninajitahidi kuadhimisha kurudi kwa siku hii kwa kujinyenyekeza, maombi, na sifa.”

Ni neema ya ajabu ya Mungu pekee ambayo ingeweza kumchukua baharia mkorofi, mwenye kufuru, mfanyabiashara wa watumwa, na kumgeuza kuwa mtoto wa Mungu. John hakuacha kamwe kustaajabia kazi ya Mungu katika maisha yake. Alianza kupendezwa na maombi, kusoma na kutafakari Maandiko, na kusema maneno yanayompendeza Mungu pekee.

Aliporudi nyumbani, Mary na wazazi wake walitambua mabadiliko ambayo Bwana alikuwa ameleta ndani ya John. Wawili hao walioana tarehe 1 Februari 1750.

Kwa miaka minne iliyofuata, Newton alikuwa nahodha wa meli yake mwenyewe ya watumwa. Kazi hii ilimtenganisha na Mary kwa miezi kadhaa kila mara. Walipokuwa mbali, wawili hao waliandikiana barua daima. Katika barua zake, John aliandika mara kwa mara jinsi upendo na ndoa yao zilivyoongeza shukrani zake kwa Bwana. “... Ninapojipa nafasi ya kukuwaza kwa namna ya pekee, kwa kawaida mawazo hayo hunipeleka mbali zaidi na kunifanya nipige magoti kumhimidi Bwana kwa kunipa hazina kama hii na kuombea amani na ustawi wako”

John alijitahidi kuifanya meli yake ya watumwa iwe ya “Kikristo” kwa kuendesha ibada za Jumapili kwa wafanyakazi wake 30 waliokuwa wameshupazwa na dhambi. Alifanya safari nyingine tatu kuleta watumwa kutoka Afrika kwenda Amerika ya Kaskazini. Alipokuwa akipanga safari yake ya nne, aliugua malaria. Mungu alitumia ugonjwa huu kukomesha ushiriki wake katika biashara ya watumwa.

John alipoanza ukurasa mpya wa maisha yake, alihisi kuwa ameitwa kuwa mhudumu wa kanisa. Kwa zaidi ya miaka 50, alihubiri injili na alikuwa mmoja wa watu wenye ushawishi mkubwa zaidi wa wakati wake.

Mara nyingi John Newton alitunga wimbo uendane na ibada zake za Jumapili jioni. Mwaka 1779, nyimbo 280 kati ya hizo zilikusanywa na kuunganishwa na nyimbo 68 za rafiki wa Newton na mshiriki wa parokia yake, William Cowper, na kuchapishwa kama Olney Hymns. Wimbo maarufu zaidi kati ya Olney Hymns zote, “Kutazama Nyuma na Matarajio ya Imani”, ulitokana na mshangao wa Daudi katika 1 Mambo ya Nyakati 17:16-17. Leo tunaujua kama “Neema ya Ajabu”. Awali “Neema ya Ajabu” ulikuwa na beti sita, na ubeti wa mwisho uliongezwa karibu karne moja baadaye. Vitabu vingi vya tenzi vina beti nne au tano kati ya hizo.

Akiwa mhudumu katika kanisa, John aliendelea kusumbuliwa zaidi na zaidi na biashara ya watumwa iliyokuwa bado ikiendelea. Mwaka 1788, miaka 34 baada ya kuacha biashara ya watumwa, aliandika kitabu kilichoitwa Thoughts Upon the African Slave Trade na kukituma kwa wabunge wote. Kitabu hiki kiliwafanya watu wafahamu maovu ya biashara ya watumwa. Ananukuu hivi, “Bila shaka, kuwakamata, kuwauza na kuwasafirisha watumwa weusi kwenda kwenye mashamba makubwa katika visiwa vya West Indies na Amerika ilikuwa njia ya maisha ya ukatili na uovu.” Kwa msaada na uongozi wa Mungu, John aliiona siku, miezi kadhaa kabla ya kifo chake mwaka 1807, ambapo utumwa ulipigwa marufuku rasmi nchini Uingereza.

John alipokuwa katika miaka yake ya sitini, mke wake mpendwa Mary alifariki. Hili lilikuwa jaribu kubwa kwa John, naye alitumia miaka 17 iliyobaki ya maisha yake bila yeye.

Baada ya John kupata kiharusi na muda mfupi kabla ya kifo chake, msemaji wa kanisa alimhimiza Newton afikirie kustaafu kuhubiri kwa sababu afya, uwezo wa kuona, na kumbukumbu zake zilikuwa zikidhoofika. John alijibu, “Eti nini, yule mkufuru wa zamani wa Afrika aache wakati bado anaweza kusema? Nitaendelea kuhubiri. Ingawa kumbukumbu zangu zinafifia, ninakumbuka mambo mawili kwa uwazi kabisa: Mimi ni mwenye dhambi mkubwa, na Kristo ni Mwokozi mkuu.”

Maneno ya mwisho ya John Newton alipokuwa amelala kitandani akikaribia kufa yalikuwa haya: “Bado niko katika nchi ya wanaokufa; hivi karibuni nitakuwa katika nchi ya walio hai.”

Melodia ya “Neema ya Ajabu” ni melodia ya zamani ya kimapokeo ya Marekani. Kwanza ilijulikana kama melodia ya mashambani iliyoitwa “Wanakondoo Wenye Upendo”. Melodia hii ilichapishwa kwa mara ya kwanza mwaka 1831 katika kitabu The Virginia Harmony. Vitabu vingi vya tenzi vilivyochapishwa baada ya wakati huo vilijumuisha wimbo huu. Mwaka 1910, Edwin O. Excell aliongeza ubeti wa mwisho, ambao hatimaye ulichukua nafasi ya beti tatu za mwisho za awali za wimbo huo. Toleo lake la wimbo ndilo linalopatikana zaidi katika vitabu vyetu vya tenzi leo. Nyimbo nyingine kadhaa za Newton katika Olney hymns zinaendelea kuimbwa leo, zikiwemo “Jinsi Jina la Yesu Linavyosikika kwa Utamu” na “Mambo ya Utukufu Yanasemwa Kukuhusu”.
