Hvor utrolig er det ikke at Gud kan ta en elendig synder uten frykt for Herren og gjøre ham til en hellig, renset i blodet, og en forkynner av evangeliet! I denne fortellingen ser vi Guds livsforvandlende kraft i virksomhet i salmedikterens liv.

På den lille kirkegården i Olney i England står en gravstein av granitt med denne innskriften, skrevet av Newton selv før hans død:

John Newton, en gang en vantro og en utsvevende mann, en tjener for slaver i Afrika, ble ved vår Herre og Frelser Jesu Kristi rike barmhjertighet bevart, gjenopprettet, tilgitt og utpekt til å forkynne den troen han lenge hadde arbeidet for å ødelegge!

Denne gravskriften beskriver treffende det uvanlige og fargerike livet til denne mannen, en av de store evangeliske forkynnerne på 1700-tallet. Hans vitnesbyrd var: «Ved Guds nåde er jeg det jeg er!»

«Amazing Grace» er en salme som ble utgitt i 1779, med tekst skrevet i 1772 av den engelske dikteren og anglikanske presten John Newton (1725–1807). «Amazing Grace» er sannsynligvis den mest elskede salmen fra de siste to århundrene. Det anslås at denne salmen fremføres 10 millioner ganger i året. Den har vært med på over 11 000 album og er oversatt til omtrent 60 språk. Den ble omtalt i Harriet Beecher Stowes roman mot slaveriet, Onkel Toms hytte. Populariteten steg kraftig under to av Amerikas største kriser: borgerkrigen og Vietnamkrigen.

Ironisk nok ble denne gripende sangen, som er nært knyttet til det afroamerikanske samfunnet, skrevet av en tidligere slavehandler, John Newton.

John ble født 24. juli 1725 i Wapping i England. Faren, John Newton, Sr., var sjømann, og moren, Elizabeth Newton, var en hengiven kristen. Faren elsket ham, men var til sjøs det meste av tiden. Moren var derimot øm og omsorgsfull og lærte ham Guds ord. Hun lærte ham å huske hele kapitler fra Bibelen utenat og tok ham med i kirken. Dessverre døde moren av tuberkulose da han var nesten sju år gammel. Faren giftet seg igjen kort tid senere og sendte ham på internatskole. Mens han var der, fikk han dårlige venner. Karakteren hans forfalt så mye at han ble utvist fra én skole og flyttet til en annen. Da han var blitt 11 år, ville ikke internatskolene ha ham, så faren tok ham med til sjøs. De neste seks årene tilbrakte han på Atlanterhavet sammen med faren.

Da John var 17 år, ordnet faren det slik at han skulle reise til Jamaica for å få en godt betalt stilling som oppsynsmann på en plantasje. Underveis, mens han ventet på at skipet skulle gå, ble John invitert hjem til noen gamle venner, familien Catlett. Det var i dette hjemmet moren til John hadde dødd ti år tidligere. Da han fornyet bekjentskapet med dem, ble han kjent med datteren deres, Mary. Mødrene til John og Mary hadde vært bestevenninner. John var invitert til å bli i fire dager, men han ble i to uker og gikk glipp av skipet til Jamaica.

Som 18-åring ble John tvangsinnrullert i den britiske marinen, og livet hans gikk fra vondt til verre. Han ville dra tilbake for å se Mary, så han deserterte fra skipet, men ble tatt, pisket offentlig og lagt i jern. Livet hans om bord var så ugudelig at selv de andre gudløse sjøfolkene krympet seg ved hans banning og gudsbespottelser. Han fikk tilnavnet «Den store gudsbespotteren» og var så uønsket om bord at han ble sendt for å arbeide på et slaveskip.

En av eierne av slaveskipet der han nå arbeidet, tilbød John en jobb når de kom til Afrikas kyst. Men straks han kom i land, ble han bundet og tvunget til å arbeide med lite mat, klær eller husly. I denne tiden sendte han flere brev hjem til faren og bønnfalt ham om hjelp.

Et skip som het The Greyhound, seilte nær kysten som John nå kalte sitt hjem. Kapteinen hadde fått beskjed av Johns far om å lete etter sønnen hans. Selv om skipet var nesten for langt fra land til å drive handel, bestemte de seg for å gjøre et forsøk. En venn av John rodde ut fra land for å handle. Da han snudde seg for å dra, spurte kapteinen om han kjente noen som het John Newton. Til kapteinens overraskelse gjorde han det, og John ble hentet om bord for å reise hjem.

Om bord tok Newton opp et eksemplar av Thomas á Kempis’ kristne klassiker, Om Kristi etterfølgelse. Han hadde aldri møtt noe lignende, og han begynte å undre seg over om det kristendommen hevdet, kunne være sant. Den natten, 10. mars 1748, var en voldsom storm nær ved å senke skipet. Menn, dyr og proviant ble skylt over bord. Stormen vekket Newton; bølgene hadde knust skipets råtne treverk, og vann strømmet virvlende inn i lugaren hans. John ba for første gang på mange år.

The Greyhound ble kastet omkring i stormen i Nord-Atlanteren i over 11 dager. Med lite håp om å overleve arbeidet sjøfolkene mekanisk ved pumpene og prøvde å holde fartøyet flytende. På stormens ellevte dag var John for utmattet til å pumpe, så han ble bundet til roret, der han gjorde sitt beste for å holde skipet på kurs. Fra klokken ett til midnatt sto han ved roret. Han fryktet at han kom til å dø, og at hvis den kristne troen var sann, ville han helt sikkert ikke bli tilgitt. Han tenkte over alt han hadde gjort de siste årene. Livet hans virket like ødelagt og havarert som det medtatte skipet han forsøkte å styre gjennom stormen. I disse lange og utmattende timene ropte Newton til Gud som aldri før, og det ble vendepunktet i livet hans.

Det var en dag John Newton husket resten av livet. «På den dagen sendte Herren hjelp fra det høye og reddet meg ut av dype vann.» Over 50 år senere, 21. mars 1805, skrev John i dagboken sin: «Jeg makter ikke å skrive særlig godt; men jeg prøver å markere denne dagen når den kommer igjen, med ydmykelse, bønn og lovprisning.»

Bare Guds forunderlige nåde kunne ta en rå, gudsbespottende sjømann som drev slavehandel, og forvandle ham til et Guds barn. John sluttet aldri å undre seg over Guds verk i livet hans. Han fikk interesse for bønn, for å lese og grunne på Skriften og for bare å tale ord som var til behag for Gud.

Da han kom hjem, så Mary og foreldrene hennes den forandringen Herren hadde gjort i John. De to giftet seg 1. februar 1750.

De neste fire årene var Newton kaptein på sitt eget slaveskip. Dette arbeidet holdt ham borte fra Mary i flere måneder om gangen. Mens de var fra hverandre, brevvekslet de stadig. I brevene skrev John gjentatte ganger om hvordan kjærligheten og ekteskapet deres økte hans takknemlighet overfor Herren. «... Når jeg tillater meg å dvele særlig ved tanken på deg, fører det meg vanligvis videre og får meg ned på kne for å velsigne Herren for at han har gitt meg en slik skatt, og for å be om din fred og ditt vel.»

John forsøkte å «kristne» slaveskipet sitt ved å holde søndagsgudstjenester for besetningen på 30 menn som var forherdet av synd. Han foretok ytterligere tre reiser for å føre slaver fra Afrika til Nord-Amerika. Mens han planla sin fjerde reise, ble han syk av malaria. Gud brukte denne sykdommen til å avslutte hans deltakelse i slavehandelen.

Da John begynte på et nytt kapittel i livet, følte han seg kalt til å bli prest. I mer enn 50 år forkynte han evangeliet og var en av de mest innflytelsesrike mennene i sin tid.

John Newton skrev ofte en salme til kveldsgudstjenestene sine på søndager. I 1779 ble 280 av disse samlet sammen med 68 salmer av Newtons venn og sognebarn William Cowper og utgitt som Olney Hymns. Den mest kjente av alle salmene i Olney Hymns, «Troens tilbakeblikk og forventning», sprang ut av Davids utrop i 1. Krønikebok 17:16-17. I dag kjenner vi den som «Amazing Grace». «Amazing Grace» hadde opprinnelig seks strofer, og det siste verset ble lagt til omtrent et århundre senere. De fleste salmebøker har fire eller fem av disse versene.

Som prest i kirken ble John stadig mer plaget av slavehandelen som fremdeles pågikk. I 1788, 34 år etter at han hadde forlatt slavehandelen, skrev han en bok med tittelen Thoughts Upon the African Slave Trade og sendte den til alle parlamentsmedlemmene. Denne boken gjorde offentligheten oppmerksom på slavehandelens onder. Han sier dette: «Det sier seg selv at det å fange, selge og frakte svarte slaver til plantasjene i Vestindia og Amerika var en grusom og ondartet levemåte.» Med Guds hjelp og forsyn fikk John oppleve den dagen i 1807, noen måneder før sin død, da slaveriet offisielt ble forbudt i England.

Da John var i sekstiårene, døde hans elskede kone Mary. Dette var en stor prøvelse for John, og han tilbrakte de siste 17 årene av livet uten henne.

Etter at John hadde fått slag, og kort tid før hans død, oppfordret en talsmann for kirken Newton til å vurdere å slutte å forkynne på grunn av sviktende helse, syn og hukommelse. John svarte: «Hva, skal den gamle gudsbespotteren fra Afrika slutte mens han ennå kan snakke? Jeg vil fortsette å forkynne. Selv om hukommelsen min svikter, husker jeg to ting svært tydelig: Jeg er en stor synder, og Kristus er en stor Frelser.»

John Newtons siste ord da han lå på dødsleiet, var disse: «Jeg er fremdeles i de døendes land; snart skal jeg være i de levendes land.»

Melodien til «Amazing Grace» er en tidlig amerikansk folkemelodi. Den var først kjent som en plantasjemelodi med tittelen «Loving Lambs». Denne melodien ble først utgitt i 1831 i boken The Virginia Harmony. De fleste salmebøker som ble utgitt etter dette, tok med denne sangen. I 1910 la Edwin O. Excell til det siste verset, som etter hvert erstattet sangens tre siste opprinnelige vers. Hans utgave av sangen er den vanligste i salmebøkene våre i dag. Flere andre av Newtons Olney-salmer synges fortsatt i dag, blant annet «Hvor liflig Jesu navn lyder» og «Herlighet tales om deg».

Eight-year-old Jamin wasn’t very smart. Or at least that’s what his older brother told him. Almost daily, brother Kenny found ways to remind Jamin of his shortcomings and laugh at his blunders.

“Jamin, you will never be smart”, Kenny said. Deep inside Jamin felt resigned to a life of muddled trip-ups. Would he always be clumsy? Would he always say things wrong? That’s what Kenny said.

Jamin believed Kenny’s lectures with wide-eyed belief. Kenny was three years older than him, so he must be right. Very well, then Jamin would be simple. Kenny would be smart. Life was not fair. Dad and Mom disliked Kenny’s proud talk and punished him whenever they walked in on one of his speeches. But Kenny had a way of avoiding earshot. So he continued mocking Jamin.

Grandma Otto watched these trials from her rocker on the porch. She was a quiet old lady.

“Jamin, do you know where Kenny is?” Mom asked with a smile. “It’s almost supper time.”

“He went to check his coyote traps. I’ll go find him.”

There was a chill in the air as he tramped up over the lawn, and the sun was growing old as he crossed the border of the woods. The fleeting shadows scurried over the hills. The chill deepened as he stumped further in. He breathed the rich air and followed Kenny’s trail. Eventually, the trail would end up in a meadow, but Jamin hoped he would find Kenny before he had to go that far. The various traps had been checked already, so Jamin knew Kenny had come this way. Jamin trudged on resolutely. His golden head caught the tired beams that fled from the sun as they flickered through the trees. And soon those too had faded leaving behind the musky smell of the woods. The fall webworms had been at work, and their web curtains shuttered from branches overhead.

At length, as the trees subdued and thinned, and the meadow appeared Jamin knew this was the end of his brother’s trap route. If Kenny wasn’t here, he wouldn’t know where else to look.

But Kenny was there. As Jamin clumped into the meadow, he could see a frustrated heap to his right. The heap’s voice had a familiar ring. The heap’s face was lit in pain. The heap was Kenny. “Are you alright? What happened?” Jamin felt strange, seeing Kenny scrunched in the dirt. Kenny was smart. “Did you step in a trap?”

“Yes, Jamin. I..I wasn’t looking where I was going. Help me. Please.”

Jamin bent and found an ankle firmly held in the jaws of a steel trap. Darkness stained the ground around Kenny. Quickly, Jamin’s strong arms pried open the jaws. Kenny reeled free. “Can you walk?”

“Yes. I think so. If you support me, I can hobble along.”

“Dad and Mom will be worried. We’ve missed supper.”

Sure enough, as the brothers hobbled back through the woods, they heard the long calling of their father. Jamin called back, and he was by their side in a moment, seeing the ankle and scooping up Kenny like a hurt sheep. The odd little band hurried home, and the screen door banged shut as Dad swept across the porch. Jamin went to the wash house and scrubbed his hands. He headed for the front door.

“Jamin.” It was Grandma. The porch light showed her in her old rocker. A heavy comforter lay on her shoulders.

“Yes, Grandma?”

“Do you think you are not very smart?”

“That’s what Kenny says.” Jamin squirmed.

“You were strong enough to open the trap, and Kenny wasn’t. You were brave enough to find him in the dark. Lots of young boys wouldn’t be.” Jamin was silent. Grandma Otto rocked some more, then smiled. “God made you the way you are for a reason, Jamin. He made Kenny the way he is for a reason. He has a plan for you, and a place only you can fill, you know.”

Jamin turned and walked into the warm kitchen. He was smiling.

আট বছর বয়সী জামিন খুব বেশি বুদ্ধিমান ছিল না। বা অন্তত এমনটাই বলত তার বড় ভাই। প্রায় প্রতিদিনই কেনি জামিনকে তার ত্রুটিগুলো মনে করিয়ে দেয়ার উপায় খুঁজে পেত এবং তার ভুলগুলোয় হাস্যরস্য করত।

“জামিন, তুই কখনই বুদ্ধিমান হবে না”, কেনি বলত। জামিনের ভিতরে গভীরে মনে হয়েছিল যে তার জীবনটি ভুলে-চুসে ভরা থাকবে। সে কি সবসময়ই অনর্গল থাকবে? কি সবসময়ই ভুল কথা বলবে? কেনিই তো তাই বলছিল।

জামিন কেনির উপদেশগুলো বিস্মিত চোখে বিশ্বাস করে নিত। কেনি তার থেকে তিন বছর বড়, সুতরাং সে ঠিক বলতেই হবে। ভালো, তাহলে জামিন সাদাসিধে থাকবে। কেনি বুদ্ধিমান হবে। জীবন কোনভাবেই ন্যায্য ছিল না। বাবা-মা কেনির গর্বিত কথাবার্তা পছন্দ করে না এবং তাদের কারও এক বক্তৃতার সময় ঢুকে পড়লে তাকে শাস্তি দিত। কিন্তু কেনির একটি উপায় ছিল কানে কেউ শুনতে না পারে এমন জায়গায় চলে যাওয়ার। তাই সে জামিনকে তিরস্কার করা চালিয়ে গেল।

ওটো দিদিমা তাদের আড়াল থেকে পাইকারির কুঁড়ো চেয়ারে বসে এই পরীক্ষাগুলো দেখতেন। তিনি শান্ত একজন বৃদ্ধা মহিলা ছিলেন।

“জামিন, তুমি জানো কেনি কোথায় আছে?” মা হাসি মুখে জিজ্ঞেস করলেন। “একটা দিনধরা খাওয়ার সময় হয়ে এসেছে।”

“সে কoyote ফাঁদগুলো চেক করতে গেছিল। আমি তাকে খুঁজে নিয়ে আসব।”

ঘাসের ওপর দিয়ে তিনি পায়চারি করে উপরে উঠার সঙ্গে সঙ্গে বাতাস ঠান্ডা হয়ে এসেছিল, আর সুর্যও বয়সে পড়ে যাচ্ছিল যখন তিনি বনসীমা পার হলেন। ক্ষণস্থায়ী ছায়াগুলো টিলার ওপর চটকচট করে ছড়িয়ে পড়ছিল। যত বেশি তিনি অগভীর জঙ্গলভাগে হাঁটলেন ততই ঠান্ডা বাড়তে থাকল। তিনি সমৃদ্ধ বায়ু শ্বাস নিলেন এবং কেনির পদচিহ্ন অনুসরণ করলেন। শেষপর্যন্ত পথটা এক মাঠে পৌঁছাবে, কিন্তু জামিন আশা করলো সে সেখানে পৌঁছানোর আগেই কেনিকে পেয়ে যাবে। বিভিন্ন ফাঁদগুলো ইতিমধ্যে দেখা হয়েছিল, তাই জামিন জানত কেনি এই পথে গেছে। জামিন দৃঢ়ভাবে হাঁটতে থাকল। তার সোনালী চুল ধবধবে আলো আঁকড়ে ধরল যা গাছপালার মধ্য দিয়ে সরে যাচ্ছিল। দ্রুতই সেগুলোও ম্লান হয়ে গেল এবং পশুচিহ্নতলা গন্ধ আর গাছগাছালির গন্ধ রেখে গেল। শরৎকালের ওয়েবওর্মরা কাজ করেছিল এবং তাদের জালগুলি উপরের শাখা থেকে ঝুলে পড়েছিল।

অবশেষে, যখন গাছগুলো শান্ত ও পাতলা হয়ে এলো, এবং মাঠটি দেখা দিল, জামিন জানল এটি কেনির ফাঁদ ঘোরার শেষ প্রান্ত। কেনি যদি এখানে না থাকে, তাহলে সে আর কোথায় খুঁজে পাবে তা জানত না।

কিন্তু কেনি সেখানে ছিল। জামিন যখন মাঠে ঢুকল, সে ডানদিকে বিরক্ত এক কচকচে ভাঁজ দেখতে পেল। ভাঁজটির কন্ঠ স্বরটি পরিচিত ছিল। ভাঁজটির মুখ বেদনার আলোয় ছড়িয়ে ছিল। ভাঁজটি কেনি ছিল। “তুই ঠিক আছিস? কী হয়েছে?” জামিন অচেনা রকম অনুভব করল, কেনিকে মাটিতে সঙ্কুচিত অবস্থায় দেখে। কেনি বুদ্ধিমান। “তুই কি কোনো ফাঁদে পা দিয়েছিস?”

“হ্যাঁ, জামিন। আমি.. আমি দেখে চলিনি। আমাকে সাহায্য কর। অনুগ্রহ করে। ”

জামিন নত হয়ে একটি টাখনা পেল যা ইস্পাত ফাঁদের দন্তে শক্তভাবে আটকে ছিল। মাটিতে কালের চারপাশে অন্ধকার লেগে ছিল। দ্রুত, জামিনের শক্ত বাহুগুলো দন্তগুলো খুলে দিল। কেনি ছুটি করে বেরিয়ে এল। “তুই হাঁটতে পারবি?”

“হ্যাঁ। আমার মনে হয় পারব। যদি তুই আমাকে সমর্থন করিস, আমি লঙ্গড়ে হেটে চলতে পারব।”

“বাবা-মা চিন্তিত থাকবে। আমরা রাতের খাবার ছুঁয়ে ফেলেছি।”

নিশ্চিতভাবেই, ভাইরা বন পেরিয়ে ফিরে আসার পথে তাদের পিতার দীর্ঘ ডাক শোনাল। জামিন ডাক দিল, এবং মুহূর্তের মধ্যে তিনি তাদের পাশে উপস্থিত হলেন, টাখনাটি দেখে কেনিকে ভেঙে কৃশ একটি ভেড়ার মত কাঁধে তুলে নিলেন। অদ্ভুত সেই ক্ষুদ্র দলটা তাড়াতাড়ি বাড়ি ফিরল, এবং পর্দা দরজাটা ধাক্কা খেয়ে বন্ধ হয়ে গেল যখন বাবা বারান্দা পার হয়ে এলেন। জামিন ধোয়ার ঘরে গিয়ে তার হাত ধুয়ে নিল। সে সামনের দরজার দিকে গেল।

“জামিন।” এটি দিদিমা। বারান্দার আলোতে তিনি তার পুরনো কুঁড়ো চেয়ারে দেখা গেলেন। তার কাঁধে একটি ভারী কমফোর্টার ছিল।

“জি, দিদিমা?”

“তুমি কি মনে করো তুমি খুব বুদ্ধিমান নও?”

“এটাই কেনি বলে।” জামিন ঐকান্তিকভাবে ঘোরলেন।

“তুই ফাঁদটা খোলার জন্য যথেষ্ট শক্ত ছিলি, আর কেনি সেটা ছিল না। অন্ধকারে তাকে খুঁজে পেতে তুই যথেষ্ট সাহসী ছিলি। অনেক ছোট ছেলেরা তা করতে পারত না।” জামিন চুপ করে ছিল। ওটো দিদিমা আর একটু দোল দিলেন, তারপর হাসলেন। “সৃজনহীনের কারণে ঈশ্বর তোর মতো করে তোর সৃষ্টি করেছেন, জামিন। তিনি কেনির মতো করে কেনিকে সৃষ্টি করেছেন। তাঁর একটি পরিকল্পনা আছে তোর জন্য়, এবং একটি স্থান আছে যা কেবল তুইই পূরণ করতে পারিস, জানিস কি।”

জামিন ঘোরে ঘরে গিয়ে উষ্ণ রান্নাঘরে ঢুকল। সে হাসছিল।

Our Father’s world is a world unspoiled by human invention and intervention. While sin and technology have warped and stolen many lovely things from the human race, there abide still a few that remain unmarred by civilization. Little children in the fresh innocence of their unsoiled morning top the ranks as a bit of heaven on earth and call all observers heavenward. Another is the fowl of the air as prescribed in Genesis. Paul pleaded with the Corinthian church, “Doth not nature itself teach you?” We are exhorted to consider the lilies, the ravens, and the grass of the field. Each of these bears a significant dimension of the eternal God in their existence and gives us definition to their Creator. Perhaps all of nature can give us snapshots into heavenly places if we had the time and eyes to observe it.

Birds hold a unique place in God’s creation, for their sphere is in the heavens. Man may mount on the wings of a plane and evade the lower earth for a few hours, but the heavens will never be a place of his common dominion. The birds are a picture of a heavenly race, for they are at home there. They are a natural representation of the saints and angels of God and so we do well to give them due attention. While there may be dozens of lessons to be drawn from these vessels of grace and beauty, one of the most prominent and outstanding virtues will be observed in the song that they raise. Many animals dwelling on the earth are virtually mute. Of the ones that do speak, it is often to threaten or express complaint. “Doth the wild ass bray when he hath grass? Or loweth the ox over his fodder?” (Job 6:5). When they are happy and content, they have no message to convey. The dog barks at an intruder to drive him away, while the cat mews for attention. They speak when they are threatened or dissatisfied, in fear or in pain. Similarly, the earthly human shares its nature with the mammals of the field.

Birds are diverse. They exercise their joyous vocals so much that they are the epitome of happiness. The expression “happy as a lark” is so common a term that it is used by people who have never even ventured to the meadow to see or hear a lark. While some may inform us that these songs are mere mating calls and have little to do with their feelings, we cannot escape the inner conviction that, whether mating or not, these birds delight in bearing a jubilant expression of joy and we do well to let them teach us. “Is any merry? Let him sing psalms” (James 5:13). The birds do this incessantly and it seems impossible to draw any other conclusion but that they are happy while doing so. Wander near the nest of a swallow and you will find that they have ways of expressing depreciation as well. The killdeer also has no qualms with expressing rash disfavor to those who intrude their domain, but these are not to be mistaken as songs. The singing birds are a beautiful painted picture of the saints and angels of God.

How little knowledge of heaven is committed to our understanding. The scenes of heavens described and laid out before us in Revelations can hardly bring our finite minds into its infinite realm. One dimension that we can connect with is that it is a place filled with singing. Little wonder, for it is the culminating end of the contented and joy-filled saints of God, and there they will sing a new song. Nearly every scene at the throne in Revelations is marked by some dimension of praise. “And he hath put a new song in my mouth, even praise unto our God” (Ps 40:3). On 22 occasions, the Scriptures reiterate the phrase, I will sing.

It is the nature of the birds to sing. It is their waking thought as morning guilds the sky, and it flows from within them like a fountain. Not all of their songs are alike. Some are elaborate in their duration, meter, and pitch, while others are plain. Some merely chirp with a merry heart. The robin opens up the choir in early spring, but his song is soon surpassed in beauty by the song sparrow and again by the rose-breasted grosbeak. The song of the wren trumps them all for longevity and vibrancy. The canary sings in a cage, while the nightingale sings in the dark. The robins sing in the rain. The buntings fill in the heat of the day when other birds are silent. As diverse as their song may be, they all commonly burst forth in exuberant happiness. It is here that they shall instruct us.

“Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord” (Eph 5:19). The advent of Christ was marked by the angelic host announcing peace and goodwill toward men. All those who will bear His name must deliver the same tidings. In John 4, we happen upon the scene at Jacob’s well, where Christ asks the woman for a drink. Her reply seems to bear a tinge of bitterness. “Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.” Though she esteemed herself as a spiritual person and willingly followed Him into religious discourse, she had no song. Like the well that they speak over, her water was buried deep below the surface and how laborious the effort to bring it forth. Christ offers another alternative. “But the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life” (John 4:14).

The well of Christ is an artesian well. One needs neither pitcher nor labor to draw it out, for it spews forth abundantly on its own accord. While Christ is probably speaking of the Spirit as in John 7:38, surely this may be just as applicable to a joy-laden heart. What is a more apt outpouring to flow from a Christ-inspired wellspring than the rapture of a song? “Behold, my servants shall sing for joy of heart” (Is 65:14). Now this should all seem plain enough to understand and easy enough to do but, alas, we find we have a constant and persistent adversary who seeks to thwart our song. We are not unaware of his devices...

Sin. Not all birds sing. There are some whose visage is black as sin. These only seem to screech and scream and are no example for the saints of God to emulate. The babbling noise we hear emanating from many passing vehicles certainly parallels the songs of such foul fowl. “Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen, and is become the habitation of devils, and the hold of every foul spirit, and a cage of every unclean and hateful bird” (Rev 18:2). These abundant creatures are the fallen spirits, the fowls waiting to devour the seed sown by the wayside. Of such are the worthless blackbirds, starlings, and grackles. The crows show themselves also at the roadside, feeding on rotting carcasses. Often you will find them in large numbers feeding themselves on the corn the farmer painstakingly planted for himself. So transgresses the selfish soul in his pursuit of happiness, feeding gleefully on the calamity of another and exploiting their sin. He bears no song, for his day is constantly clouded by the misdeeds of others who cross his path.

Neglect. The cowbird is also black (the female is brown/gray). She will be found sitting on a high vantage, shamelessly calling to her lovers by her shrill screeching. She then has the audacity to lay her egg in another bird’s nest, forcing them to raise her offspring. This is certainly a fitting emblem for a good number of females in our day. Though justified by circumstances, these women care not for their own, but are products of neglect. They have no lullaby to share with their young, for they have escorted them to the nest of another while her mind is preoccupied with work and business. “But thou art he that took me out of the womb: thou didst make me hope when I was upon my mother’s breasts” (Ps 22:9). No doubt that the singing mother can implant copious songs in her infant and set the stage for a happy and hope-filled life. While we may show mercy to a woman in dire circumstances, the major song of modern women bears chords that are but dissident and melancholy. These are stopped-up wells like unto the wells that Isaac found upon his return to Gerar. The Philistines “had filled them with earth” (Gen 26:15). So run the spiritually neglected homes of many families today, who pack their schedules so full of earthly commitments that they have no time to spend an hour in song together. If the birds stopped singing, would they even notice?

Ingratitude. Find a soul bathed in unthankfulness, and you will find a soul without a song. If the canary were to refuse to sing in captivity, few of us would ever have heard his rollicking melody. “We hanged our harps upon the willows in the midst thereof. For there they that carried us away captive required of us a song; and they that wasted us required of us mirth, saying, Sing us one of the songs of Zion. How shall we sing the LORD’S song in a strange land?” (Ps 137:2-4). God’s people had been instructed by Jeremiah to build houses, plant gardens, and raise families. “… And seek the peace of the city whither I have caused you to be carried away captives, and pray unto the LORD for it: for in the peace thereof shall ye have peace” (Jer. 29:5-7). But they could see no worth in it. With their eyes fixed upon the dismal scene around them, they lost their song. Israel had within its history a rich tradition of song. Their singing erupted at the passage of the Red Sea in the days of Jehoshaphat and had been known to defeat armies. Earthly discomfort is no excuse to withhold gratitude, for our God reigns, and we are His children. Such were the conditions of the Philippian prison where two jailbirds, Paul and Silas, opened the concert at midnight and rocked the corridors with their joyful singing.

When we open our mouths and stretch our vocals in praise, we enact the grace of God. We join the faithful choir alongside Miriam, Deborah, and Hannah, and blend harmoniously with Moses, David, Paul, and Barnabas. At evening, we sing with our Lord and His disciples after supper, and with legions of angels “giving glory to God in the highest.” If that isn’t enough, perhaps we should consider rising at early dawn and singing with the innumerable hosts of our feathered friends who are thankful for God’s loving providence. “Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord … And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men” (Col 3:16, 23).

我们天父的世界是一个未被人类发明与干预所玷污的世界。尽管罪恶与科技扭曲并窃取了许多美好的事物，人类仍然能看到一些未被文明破坏的景象。清晨里还保持着纯真无瑕的小孩子，堪称人间一隅天堂，能将所有旁观者的心向上提升。另一类则如创世记所指称的空中的飞鸟。保罗恳求哥林多教会：“Doth not nature itself teach you?” 我们被劝勉去细看百合花、乌鸦，以及田间的草。每一者在其存在中都显出永恒之神的一面，且为我们指明创造主的属性。或许若有时间与眼光，整个自然都能为我们提供通往天国的瞬间映像。

鸟在神的创造中占有独特之地，因为它们的活动领域在诸天。人可以乘飞机振翅，暂时脱离下方的大地，但诸天永远不会成为他常属的辖区。鸟类是天上子民的写照，因为它们以诸天为家。它们自然地代表了神的圣徒与天使，所以我们理当给予适当的关注。虽然从这些恩典与美丽的器皿中或可引出数十条教训，但其中最显着、最突出的一项美德便是它们所发之歌。许多栖居于地的动物几乎默不作声。那些会发声的，往往是用以威吓或表达不满。“Doth the wild ass bray when he hath grass? Or loweth the ox over his fodder?” (Job 6:5)。当它们快乐与满足时，通常无话可说。狗会对入侵者吠叫以驱赶之，猫则会喵叫以求关注。它们在受威胁或不满、恐惧或疼痛时才发声。尘世的人也在本性上与田野的哺乳动物相仿。

鸟类多样。它们频繁地用愉悦的歌声表达自己，以致成为快乐的化身。短语“happy as a lark”（像云雀一样快乐）如此常见，甚至被那些从未走进草地去看或听云雀的人使用。虽然有人会告诉我们这些歌声不过是求偶呼喊，与情感无多大关联，我们却无法摆脱内心的确信：无论是否为求偶，这些鸟确实乐于把欢欣的表情呈上，我们理当让它们教导我们。“Is any merry? Let him sing psalms” (James 5:13)。鸟儿不停如此行，似乎无法得出别的结论，除了它们在歌唱时是快乐的。接近燕子的巢，你会发现它们也有表达不满的方式。killdeer（防守地盘的鸻类）也毫不避讳向侵入者表现激烈的不悦，但这些不可与歌声混淆。会歌唱的鸟是神的圣徒与天使的美丽图画。

我们对天堂所知甚少。启示录中为我们铺陈的诸天景象，几乎无法将我们有限的心智带入其无限的境域。我们能连接上的一方面是：那里充满了歌声。并不奇怪，因为那是满足且充满喜乐之神子民的终极归处，在那里他们要唱新歌。“And he hath put a new song in my mouth, even praise unto our God” (Ps 40:3)。经文在二十二处重申短语“I will sing”。

歌唱是鸟类的本性。清晨当曙光涂抹天空时，这是它们醒来时的思绪，从内心涌出如泉源。它们的歌并不尽相同。有些在时长、节拍与音高上极为复杂，另一些则朴素。有些只是愉快地吱喳。知更鸟在早春开启合唱，但很快便被歌雀（song sparrow）与玫胸秋沙鸟（rose-breasted grosbeak）的歌声在美感上超越。侏鸫（wren）的歌以持久与生动胜过众鸟。金丝雀在笼中歌唱，而夜莺在黑暗中歌唱。知更鸟在雨中歌唱。燕雀在白日炎热时补上当其他鸟缄默之处。尽管歌声各异，它们共同之处在于都洋溢着欢欣雀跃。这正是它们要教导我们的地方。

“Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord” (Eph 5:19)。基督的降临以天使军团宣告人间和平与善意为标志。凡要承受他名号的人也当传扬相同的消息。约翰福音第四章我们来到雅各井处，基督向那妇人要水喝。她的回答似带些苦涩。“Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.” 虽然她自以为属灵，乐意与他进入宗教对话，但她没有歌曲。正如他们谈及的那口井，她的活水埋在深处，取出极为费力。基督提供了另一种选择。“But the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life” (John 4:14)。

基督的井是自涌的泉。人不需水罐亦无须劳力去汲取，它自会丰盛涌出。虽然基督很可能在此指圣灵（John 7:38），但这同样适用于充满喜乐的心。还有什么比从基督所激发的泉源涌出的更恰当的倾流，若不是赞叹的歌声呢？“Behold, my servants shall sing for joy of heart” (Is 65:14)。这一切本应显而易见且易于实行，然我们有一位恒常且执着的敌人，寻求阻挠我们的歌声。我们并非不知其伎俩……

罪。并非所有鸟都歌唱。有些鸟的面容黑暗如罪，它们只会尖叫与嚎叫，不值得神的子民效法。我们从许多行驶车辆中听到的喋喋不休之声，确实与这些污秽飞禽的叫声相似。“Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen, and is become the habitation of devils, and the hold of every foul spirit, and a cage of every unclean and hateful bird” (Rev 18:2)。这些众多的生物是堕落的灵，是等待吞食路旁所撒种子的飞鸟。诸如无用的黑鸟、椋鸟（starlings）与八哥（grackles）均属此类。乌鸦也在路旁出现，以腐烂的尸体为食。你常会见到它们成群地啄食农人辛苦栽种的玉米。自私的灵魂亦如此越界追逐所谓的快乐，在他人的灾祸中欢喜地充盈自己，剥削他人的罪恶。他无歌可唱，因为他的日子常被过犯他人的事所蒙蔽。

忽视。牛鸟（cowbird）也是黑色（雌鸟为棕/灰色）。她常栖于高处，大胆地以尖厉的啼叫呼唤伴侣，之后竟厚颜无耻地把自己的卵产在别鸟的巢里，逼迫他人为其抚养后代。这无疑是当今许多妇女的恰当象征。尽管可能为境遇所逼，这些妇女并不关心自己的儿女，乃为忽视的产物。她们没有摇篮曲与孩子共寝，因为她们把孩子送到他人的巢中，而自己心思却被工作与事务占据。“But thou art he that took me out of the womb: thou didst make me hope when I was upon my mother’s breasts” (Ps 22:9)。无疑，会歌唱的母亲能在婴儿心中植入丰厚的歌声，为充满喜乐与盼望的人生奠定基础。虽可怜困境中的妇女并施怜悯，然现代许多妇女的主旋律却偏为异端与忧郁。这些正如以撒回到基拉耳所遇之井：那些井“had filled them with earth” (Gen 26:15)。如今许多家庭灵里被忽略的井亦然，他们把时间表填满世俗的事务，致无暇共度一小时歌唱。若鸟停止歌唱，他们会注意到吗？

忘恩。若找到一个沉浸在忘恩中的灵魂，你将发现一个无歌的心。若金丝雀在囚笼中拒绝歌唱，我们中的许多人就永远听不到它那欢快的旋律。“We hanged our harps upon the willows in the midst thereof. For there they that carried us away captive required of us a song; and they that wasted us required of us mirth, saying, Sing us one of the songs of Zion. How shall we sing the LORD’S song in a strange land?” (Ps 137:2-4)。耶利米曾吩咐神的子民建造房屋、栽种园圃、建立家室。“… And seek the peace of the city whither I have caused you to be carried away captives, and pray unto the LORD for it: for in the peace thereof shall ye have peace” (Jer. 29:5-7)。但他们看不见其中的价值。眼目定睛在周遭凄凉之景，他们失去了歌声。以色列历史中有丰富的歌唱传统：过红海时的歌在约沙法时代显现，且曾被知为能打败军队。尘世的不适不是扣留感恩的借口，因为我们的神掌权，我们是祂的子民。腓立比监狱中的情形便是，两名囚徒保罗与西拉在午夜开启唱歌，喜乐的歌声震动了囚室走廊。

当我们张口并伸展声带以赞美，我们就是在践行神的恩典。我们与米利暗、底波拉、哈拿并肩加入那忠心的合唱，与摩西、大卫、保罗及巴拿巴和谐相和。夜间饭后我们与主和门徒一同歌唱，与无数天使“giving glory to God in the highest”同声。如果这还不足以打动你，也许该考虑在黎明时分起身，与无数羽翼的朋友一起歌唱，感谢神的慈爱供应。“Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord … And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men” (Col 3:16, 23).

“Dr. Waldron, Elsie needs help!” Elsie’s husband was adamant, almost angry, as he stared at me. On the other hand, Elsie stared at the floor, almost as though she wasn’t present. I had never met either of the couple before and was struggling just a little to figure out what was needed from me to help her.

“What is going on?” I asked as I flipped through her chart. This was still in the days of paper charts, and I headed to the lab section of her chart. There wasn’t anything too crazy that I could see there—her liver enzymes were a little elevated, but otherwise, everything seemed OK.

“It’s her drinking!” Her husband told me. “She is drinking more and more every night. She won’t go out except to get whiskey. She drinks till she passes out every night and has to have something every morning to get her started.”

“Is that true?” I asked Elsie, feeling like a judge overseeing a jury trial.

“Yes,” she said. Her face was emotionless, and I couldn’t tell if she wanted to be there or not.

“Do you want help?” I asked her. This was a loaded question. Many people who struggle with alcoholism aren’t ready to break free from its vice-like hold on them. Maybe Elsie was different.

“I guess so,” she said, indifferently. Once again, I couldn’t tell whether she wanted to be there or not.

“At the rate at which you are drinking, you will kill yourself within a year – maybe two at best – if you don’t give up alcohol entirely,” I told her. “If you want to, I will try to find you an inpatient program to detox you and get you off of alcohol.”

“She’s ready,” he husband said firmly.

When dealing with someone who drinks heavily, it is crucial that they don’t simply stop drinking without medical support. Abrupt cessation of alcohol use causes the body to go into withdrawal which can produce a state called Delirium Tremens and even seizures.

I stepped out of the exam room and to make phone calls. It is never easy to find a place for someone to attempt to rehabilitate from any kind of substances, and it was over an hour and a half before I found a facility that was willing to take Elsie and try to help her get off of the whiskey.

I sighed as I reentered her exam room. I had been afraid that I wouldn’t find anywhere for her to go.

I told them about the plan, and her husband nodded vigorously, while Elise continued to stare silently at the floor. “Can we pray together before you go?” I asked them, and when they nodded assent, I prayed with them, asking for freedom and Jesus’ presence in both of their lives.

They left my office with marching orders and directions on where to go. I had a happy glow about me for the rest of the morning, knowing that I had gone the extra mile and had really made a difference in this middle-aged couple’s life.

Around 2 pm, I got a call from the rehab facility. They hadn’t seen even a shadow of Elsie or her husband, which was surprising, since it was a bright sunny day and the facility wasn’t that far away. With a sinking feeling, I dialed the couple’s phone number.

“She won’t go!” Her husband told me. “She tells me that she told me this ahead of time. She’ll try to cut back, but she isn’t willing to go into a rehab facility or any such thing. I guess just tell them that we’ll let them know if she changes her mind.”

My nurse called the rehab facility and told them the bad news, and I sat down in my chair, stunned. What else could I have done? Was there a solution for Elsie—something different that I could have said that would have made a difference in her life?

About a year later, I received the sad news that Elsie had died at home. I was certain that things would have been different if she had gone to rehab and if she had given control to Jesus. None of that had happened, and I felt cynicism pushing into my heart.

Cynicism

We live in an age of cynicism. In ancient Greece, the cynics were an odd assortment of men who specialized in being grouchy and saying mean (they would have said truthful) things to people. They often dressed in rags and behaved in such a way that most of the polite Athenians did not want to be close to them.

Today, cynicism means a tendency to believe the worst about people and circumstances. Cynical people believe that all people are motivated purely by selfishness and that bad events will tend to prevail.

Many young doctors are idealistic and very hopeful. They believe that if they exert the utmost effort, they can make a real, positive impact on their patient’s lives. Unfortunately, as time goes by and they try their hardest and their patients don’t change, they can give up. These doctors still try, but they no longer really hope that their efforts will make much of a difference.

It seems as though people who get involved with politics often have the best of intentions. They see this as a path to changing society for the better. Unfortunately, as time goes by and the faces in charge change, the policies don’t really change, they tend to become cynical.

Sometimes this cynicism is directed against all politicians. Sometimes it is only anger directed against members of the party that opposes their party’s positions. Hope is replaced by cynicism.

Cynicism in the Bible

If there is a book in the Bible that seems to have been written by a cynical man, it is the book of Ecclesiastes. The Preacher, who we understand to be Solomon, lists all of the things that he endeavored in an attempt to find joy.

In chapter 2:17-23 Solomon describes work as futile. He finishes by saying, “For what hath man of all his labour, and of the vexation of his heart, wherein he hath laboured under the sun? For all his days are sorrows, and his travail grief; yea, his heart taketh not rest in the night. This is also vanity.” (Ecclesiastes 2:22,23)

He saw the world as being dominated by tyrants and there was little that the people could do about it. Solomon went so far as to say that political power was meaningless “Better is a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished. For out of prison he cometh to reign; whereas also he that is born in his kingdom becometh poor” (Ecclesiastes 4:13).

In Ecclesiastes 6:6, he seems to disparage long life. “Yea, though he live a thousand years twice told, yet hath he seen no good: do not all go to one place?”

Of course, he finishes his short book with the instruction to remember our Creator in the days of our youth. There is a blessing for those who choose to focus on God when they have a little bit of energy left and not, when they are old and jaded, like Solomon.

Later on, it almost seemed as though God had given up on His people. He still sent prophets to them, but He knew without a doubt that the people would refuse to respond. “Therefore thou shalt speak all these words unto them; but they will not hearken to thee: thou shalt also call unto them; but they will not answer thee” (Jeremiah 7:27).

Even in the New Testament, Paul told Timothy that the time was coming when people would no longer listen to sound doctrine. “For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine; but after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears;” (2 Timothy 4:3).

By picking and choosing these passages, we can come away with a very gloomy view of the future and, more specifically, of human’s willingness to change. It seems there is little point of investing ourselves in the people around us. They are full of woe and are as likely to change as a chipmunk is to master differential calculus.

The Opposite of Cynicism

The opposite of cynicism is hope. It is the belief that the future could be better.

It is interesting that the Apostle Paul spoke of tribulations in the Epistle to the Romans, “And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; and patience, experience; and experience, hope: and hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us” (Romans 5:3-5).

We may not have reached the place where we glory in the trials we experience, but certainly, they should bring us these other things that he mentions. For, we grow in patience and experience, even as we deal with trials, but more than that, we come to realize that we have hope for tomorrow because we serve a great God.

The contrast in the story of the Prodigal Son in Luke 15 teaches us much about hope. The father and the older brother were strikingly different in their attitudes.

The father had never given up hope – he knew that his son had failed him and gone far from what he knew was right and yet, the father still desired to see the prodigal come to himself and return home.

On the other hand, the older brother not only had no hope for his younger brother, but he was also angry with him. The prodigal had wasted his money, he had lived in sin, and now, he had returned home just because he was out of money.

Certainly, there was no reason to trust the younger son. Yet, that is exactly what our Heavenly Father does for us.

Look for Hope in the Right Places

Part of the problem is that we look for hope in the wrong places. A number of years ago, a presidential candidate ran for office under the slogan “Hope and Change,” and yet, even though he was elected, I imagine most folks did not feel that their lives were significantly changed for the better.

Pursuing the things this world values—political power and wealth is guaranteed to bring emptiness. This is Satan’s pattern—he always over-promises and under-delivers.

This was what he did when he tempted Jesus, “All these things will I give thee, if thou wilt fall down and worship me” (Matthew 4:8). All of the things Satan offered, nothing compared with the glory that Jesus eventually received from the road that led to the cross.

In the same way, Satan would like to distract Christians from seeking the things that are valuable, and that will bring hope. Satan tells Christians that politics will not only change the world for the better, it is an easier way to change the world.

The Bible is clear that we build hope as we nurture our relationship with God and then work to help our brothers and sisters build that same relationship in their own lives. The reason that we can hope is not because people are so wonderful—we don’t have to live very long to realize that they aren’t. The reason we hope is because we serve an awesome, faithful God who walks with us through the worst of our trials.

Remember that We Have Undeserved Hope

Jesus’ messages about forgiveness make it clear that one of the major reasons that we have for forgiving others in our lives is that we have received great and undeserved forgiveness. The same is true for hope.

Each one of us was hopeless and without reason to expect to receive hope and we were still given a ray of light in the midst of our darkness. Maybe part of the reason that we have so much trouble hoping for good things for the people around us is that we do not remember how hopeless we were before we found grace.

If Jesus was able to bring hope to our hopeless existence, then certainly He can do wonderful things in the hearts and lives of others around us. The only people we should give up on are the ones that our Savior has given up on as well.

Small Efforts Do Make a Difference

I remember having a conversation with a young person who was planning to go into medicine and had a plan to go to a foreign country and serve the people there. As we were talking, an older man entered the conversation and shared that he saw little hope for change in developing countries.

The people in those countries just weren’t interested in getting better and didn’t do the minimum necessary to stave off things like worms and parasites. Doctors and nurses couldn’t make a difference in such an environment.

I could sense the heart of the youth sinking as this older man shared. He had experience, and he had given up hope. The sad thing was that he was also stealing the hope of someone who still had a desire to serve.

When I was in training, I had a surgeon tell me that family doctors didn’t really do anything. They simply kept their patients alive till their next office visit, whereas surgeons really “fixed” people—taking out (or off) the offending body part.

At the end of the day, small efforts do make a difference. I don’t do brain surgery, but I still can make a difference in someone else’s life— maybe just by spending a little time and listening and praying. This is true for all of us.

More than that, we come to realize that making this effort changes our own lives for the better. Jesus told the sheep that as they ministered to “the least of these my brethren,” they were ministering to Him.

Even if no one’s life is improved, our Savior knows our desires and feels our efforts, and will reward them someday.

A Few Things to Remember

When we face failures, we tend to move in one of two directions. Those of us who are optimists tend to believe that this episode was an isolated event and that the future is still bright. On the other hand, pessimists believe that failures are permanent, personal, and pervasive.

Pessimists believe that their failures are the result of intrinsic character flaws that they have and that these things affect all of their lives and are unlikely to change. Unlike the righteous man who falls to rise again, these people fall and lie where they fall, defeated at the outset.

When we are dealing with other people, we need to give them the same grace that we should give ourselves. They, too, are growing, and if they have a failure today, they will do better tomorrow. Maybe they will fail again, but they will at least “fail better.”

Conclusion

Cynicism is rife in our world. Many have given up hope for a better future, and it is understandable for those who have invested their hope in this world’s institutions. There is no real hope in government or in armies or in bureaucracy.

The song says, “Oh to have no hope in Jesus, how dark this world must be!” For, Jesus is the one who brings light into our darkness and allows us to continue, even when others fail us.

God is the one who redeems us. He is the one who sent the prophets, even though their messages were ignored, and the prophets were persecuted. He is the one who continues to hope for us, even when we have failed Him so many times in the past.

He is the reason we carry on. He is the reason that we have hope, not only for ourselves but also for our brothers.

“¡Dr. Waldron, Elsie necesita ayuda!” El marido de Elsie estaba firme, casi enfadado, mientras me miraba fijamente. Por otro lado, Elsie miraba al suelo, como si casi no estuviera presente. No había conocido a ninguno de los dos antes y me costaba un poco entender qué necesitaban de mí para ayudarla.

“¿Qué está pasando?” pregunté mientras hojeaba su historial. Esto todavía era en los días de los expedientes en papel, y fui a la sección de laboratorio de su carpeta. No había nada demasiado extraño que pudiera ver allí: sus enzimas hepáticas estaban un poco elevadas, pero por lo demás, todo parecía estar bien.

“¡Es su bebida!” me dijo su marido. “Bebe cada vez más cada noche. No sale salvo para comprar whisky. Bebe hasta desmayarse cada noche y necesita algo cada mañana para arrancar.”

“¿Es verdad?” le pregunté a Elsie, sintiéndome como un juez supervisando a un jurado.

“Sí,” dijo ella. Su rostro estaba sin expresión y no pude decir si quería estar allí o no.

“¿Quieres ayuda?” le pregunté. Era una pregunta cargada. Muchas personas que luchan contra el alcoholismo no están listas para liberarse de su agarre en forma decisiva. Quizá Elsie fuera diferente.

“Supongo que sí,” dijo indiferente. De nuevo, no pude saber si quería estar allí o no.

“Al ritmo al que estás bebiendo, te vas a matar en un año — quizá dos como mucho — si no dejas el alcohol totalmente,” le dije. “Si quieres, intentaré encontrar un programa de internación para desintoxicarte y sacarte del alcohol.”

“Ella está lista,” dijo su marido con firmeza.

Al tratar con alguien que bebe en exceso, es crucial que no deje de beber de golpe sin apoyo médico. La cesación brusca del consumo de alcohol hace que el cuerpo entre en abstinencia, lo que puede producir un estado llamado Delirium Tremens e incluso convulsiones.

Salí de la sala de examen para hacer llamadas. Nunca es fácil encontrar un lugar para que alguien intente rehabilitarse de cualquier tipo de sustancias, y pasaron más de hora y media antes de que encontrara una instalación dispuesta a aceptar a Elsie e intentar ayudarla a dejar el whisky.

Suspiré al volver a la sala de examen. Temía no haber encontrado ningún lugar para ella.

Les conté el plan, y su marido asintió vigorosamente, mientras Elsie siguió mirando en silencio al suelo. “¿Podemos orar juntos antes de que se vaya?” les pregunté, y cuando asintieron, oré con ellos, pidiendo libertad y la presencia de Jesús en la vida de ambos.

Salieron de mi consultorio con instrucciones y direcciones sobre adónde ir. Sentí una agradable sensación el resto de la mañana, sabiendo que había ido más allá y realmente había marcado una diferencia en la vida de esta pareja de mediana edad.

Alrededor de las 2 p.m., recibí una llamada de la clínica de rehabilitación. No habían visto ni una sombra de Elsie ni de su marido, lo cual fue sorprendente, ya que era un día soleado y la instalación no quedaba tan lejos. Con un sentimiento de desánimo, marqué el número de la pareja.

“¡No quiere ir!” me dijo su marido. “Me dice que eso ya me lo dijo antes. Intentará reducirlo, pero no está dispuesta a entrar en un centro de rehabilitación ni nada por el estilo. Supongo que dígales que les avisaremos si cambia de opinión.”

Mi enfermera llamó a la clínica y les informó la mala noticia, y me senté en mi silla, atónito. ¿Qué más podría haber hecho? ¿Había alguna solución para Elsie —algo diferente que pudiera haber dicho que habría marcado la diferencia en su vida?

Un año más tarde, recibí la triste noticia de que Elsie había muerto en su casa. Estaba seguro de que las cosas habrían sido diferentes si ella hubiera ido a rehabilitación y si hubiera entregado el control a Jesús. Nada de eso ocurrió, y sentí que el cinismo se iba abriendo paso en mi corazón.

Cinismo

Vivimos en una era de cinismo. En la antigua Grecia, los cínicos eran una extraña mezcla de hombres que se especializaban en ser malhumorados y decir cosas desagradables (ellos hubieran dicho verdaderas) a la gente. A menudo vestían andrajos y se comportaban de tal manera que la mayoría de los atenienses educados no querían estar cerca de ellos.

Hoy, el cinismo significa una tendencia a creer lo peor sobre las personas y las circunstancias. Las personas cínicas creen que toda la gente está motivada únicamente por el egoísmo y que los sucesos malos tenderán a prevalecer.

Muchos médicos jóvenes son idealistas y muy esperanzados. Creen que si se esfuerzan al máximo, pueden tener un impacto positivo real en la vida de sus pacientes. Desgraciadamente, con el paso del tiempo y aunque den lo mejor, sus pacientes no cambian y pueden rendirse. Estos médicos todavía lo intentan, pero ya no esperan realmente que sus esfuerzos hagan mucha diferencia.

Parece que las personas que se involucran en política a menudo tienen las mejores intenciones. Ven en ello una vía para cambiar la sociedad para mejor. Desgraciadamente, con el tiempo y cuando las caras en el poder cambian, las políticas no cambian realmente y tienden a volverse cínicos.

A veces este cinismo se dirige contra todos los políticos. Otras veces es solo ira dirigida contra los miembros del partido contrario. La esperanza se reemplaza por cinismo.

El cinismo en la Biblia

Si hay un libro en la Biblia que parece haber sido escrito por un hombre cínico, es el libro del Eclesiastés. El Predicador, a quien entendemos como Salomón, enumera todas las cosas en las que se empeñó en su intento de encontrar alegría.

En el capítulo 2:17-23 Salomón describe el trabajo como inútil. Termina diciendo, “For what hath man of all his labour, and of the vexation of his heart, wherein he hath laboured under the sun? For all his days are sorrows, and his travail grief; yea, his heart taketh not rest in the night. This is also vanity.” (Ecclesiastes 2:22,23)

Vio el mundo dominado por tiranos y había poco que la gente pudiera hacer al respecto. Salomón llegó a decir que el poder político no tenía sentido: “Better is a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished. For out of prison he cometh to reign; whereas also he that is born in his kingdom becometh poor” (Ecclesiastes 4:13).

En Eclesiastés 6:6, parece menospreciar la larga vida. “Yea, though he live a thousand years twice told, yet hath he seen no good: do not all go to one place?”

Por supuesto, termina su breve libro con la instrucción de recordar a nuestro Creador en los días de nuestra juventud. Hay una bendición para quienes eligen concentrarse en Dios cuando tienen un poco de energía todavía y no, cuando son viejos y cínicos, como Salomón.

Más adelante, casi parece que Dios hubiera desistido de su pueblo. Aun así envió profetas, pero sabía sin duda que la gente se negaría a responder. “Therefore thou shalt speak all these words unto them; but they will not hearken to thee: thou shalt also call unto them; but they will not answer thee” (Jeremiah 7:27).

Incluso en el Nuevo Testamento, Pablo le dijo a Timoteo que vendría el tiempo en que la gente ya no escucharía la sana doctrina. “For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine; but after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears;” (2 Timothy 4:3).

Al seleccionar y elegir estos pasajes, podemos salir con una visión muy sombría del futuro y, más específicamente, de la disposición de los seres humanos a cambiar. Parece que tiene poco sentido invertirnos en las personas que nos rodean. Están llenas de desgracia y son tan propensas a cambiar como una ardilla a dominar el cálculo diferencial.

Lo opuesto al cinismo

Lo opuesto al cinismo es la esperanza. Es la creencia de que el futuro podría ser mejor.

Es interesante que el apóstol Pablo hablase de tribulaciones en la Epístola a los Romanos: “And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; and patience, experience; and experience, hope: and hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us” (Romans 5:3-5).

Puede que no hayamos llegado al punto en que nos gloriemos en las pruebas que experimentamos, pero ciertamente deberían traernos estas otras cosas que él menciona. Pues, crecemos en paciencia y experiencia mientras enfrentamos pruebas, y más que eso, llegamos a darnos cuenta de que tenemos esperanza para el mañana porque servimos a un gran Dios.

El contraste en la historia del Hijo Pródigo en Lucas 15 nos enseña mucho sobre la esperanza. El padre y el hermano mayor eran notablemente diferentes en sus actitudes.

El padre nunca perdió la esperanza: sabía que su hijo lo había defraudado y se había alejado de lo que él sabía que era correcto y, sin embargo, el padre aún deseaba ver que el pródigo volviera en sí y regresara a casa.

Por otro lado, el hermano mayor no solo no tenía esperanza en su hermano menor, sino que además estaba enojado con él. El pródigo había malgastado su dinero, había vivido en pecado y ahora había vuelto a casa solo porque se había quedado sin dinero.

Sin duda, no había razón para confiar en el hijo menor. Sin embargo, eso es exactamente lo que nuestro Padre Celestial hace por nosotros.

Busca esperanza en los lugares correctos

Parte del problema es que buscamos esperanza en los lugares equivocados. Hace algunos años, un candidato presidencial se presentó con el lema “Hope and Change,” y aun cuando fue elegido, me imagino que la mayoría de la gente no sintió que sus vidas mejoraran significativamente.

Perseguir las cosas que valora este mundo —el poder político y la riqueza— está garantizado para traer vacío. Este es el patrón de Satanás: siempre promete de más y cumple de menos.

Esto fue lo que hizo cuando tentó a Jesús: “All these things will I give thee, if thou wilt fall down and worship me” (Matthew 4:8). De todas las cosas que Satanás ofreció, nada se comparaba con la gloria que Jesús recibió finalmente por el camino que condujo a la cruz.

De la misma manera, a Satanás le gustaría distraer a los cristianos de buscar las cosas que son valiosas y que traerán esperanza. Satanás les dice a los cristianos que la política no solo cambiará el mundo para mejor, sino que es una vía más fácil para cambiarlo.

La Biblia es clara en que construimos esperanza al nutrir nuestra relación con Dios y luego trabajar para ayudar a nuestros hermanos y hermanas a construir esa misma relación en sus propias vidas. La razón por la que podemos esperar no es porque la gente sea tan maravillosa —no hace falta vivir mucho para darse cuenta de que no lo es—. La razón por la que esperamos es porque servimos a un Dios asombroso y fiel que nos acompaña en las peores pruebas.

Recuerda que tenemos una esperanza inmerecida

Los mensajes de Jesús sobre el perdón dejan claro que una de las principales razones para perdonar a otros en nuestras vidas es que hemos recibido un gran y no merecido perdón. Lo mismo ocurre con la esperanza.

Cada uno de nosotros estaba sin esperanza y sin motivo para esperar recibir esperanza y, aun así, se nos dio un rayo de luz en medio de nuestra oscuridad. Quizá parte de la razón por la que tenemos tanto problema para esperar cosas buenas de las personas que nos rodean es que no recordamos lo desesperanzados que estábamos antes de encontrar la gracia.

Si Jesús pudo traer esperanza a nuestra existencia desesperada, ciertamente Él puede hacer cosas maravillosas en los corazones y las vidas de aquellos que nos rodean. Las únicas personas de las que deberíamos desistir son aquellas de las que nuestro Salvador también haya desistido.

Los pequeños esfuerzos sí hacen una diferencia

Recuerdo haber tenido una conversación con un joven que planeaba dedicarse a la medicina y tenía un plan para ir a un país extranjero a servir a la gente allí. Mientras hablábamos, un hombre mayor se unió a la conversación y compartió que veía poca esperanza de cambio en los países en desarrollo.

La gente en esos países simplemente no estaba interesada en mejorar y no hacía lo mínimo necesario para evitar cosas como lombrices y parásitos. Los médicos y las enfermeras no podían hacer una diferencia en tal ambiente.

Pude sentir cómo el ánimo del joven se hundía mientras este hombre mayor hablaba. Tenía experiencia y había perdido la esperanza. Lo triste era que también le estaba robando la esperanza a alguien que todavía deseaba servir.

Cuando estaba en formación, un cirujano me dijo que los médicos de familia realmente no hacían nada. Simplemente mantenían a sus pacientes con vida hasta la próxima visita, mientras que los cirujanos realmente “arreglaban” a la gente —quitando (o separando) la parte del cuerpo ofensiva.

Al final del día, los pequeños esfuerzos sí hacen una diferencia. No hago neurocirugía, pero aún puedo marcar una diferencia en la vida de otra persona —quizá simplemente dedicando un poco de tiempo a escuchar y a orar. Esto es verdad para todos nosotros.

Más que eso, llegamos a darnos cuenta de que hacer este esfuerzo cambia también nuestras propias vidas para mejor. Jesús dijo a las ovejas que al ministrar a “the least of these my brethren,” estaban ministrando a Él.

Incluso si la vida de nadie mejora, nuestro Salvador conoce nuestros deseos, siente nuestros esfuerzos y los recompensará algún día.

Algunas cosas para recordar

Cuando enfrentamos fracasos, tendemos a movernos en una de dos direcciones. Los que somos optimistas tendemos a creer que este episodio fue un evento aislado y que el futuro sigue siendo brillante. Por otro lado, los pesimistas creen que los fracasos son permanentes, personales y generalizados.

Los pesimistas creen que sus fracasos son el resultado de defectos de carácter intrínsecos que poseen y que estas cosas afectan todas sus vidas y es poco probable que cambien. A diferencia del hombre justo que cae para levantarse de nuevo, estas personas caen y yacen donde cayeron, derrotadas desde el principio.

Cuando tratamos con otras personas, necesitamos darles la misma gracia que deberíamos darnos a nosotros mismos. Ellos también están creciendo, y si hoy tienen un fracaso, mañana lo harán mejor. Quizá vuelvan a fallar, pero al menos “fallarán mejor.”

Conclusión

El cinismo está muy extendido en nuestro mundo. Muchos han perdido la esperanza de un futuro mejor, y es comprensible para quienes han puesto su esperanza en las instituciones de este mundo. No hay una esperanza real en el gobierno ni en los ejércitos ni en la burocracia.

La canción dice, “Oh to have no hope in Jesus, how dark this world must be!” Porque Jesús es quien trae luz a nuestra oscuridad y nos permite continuar, incluso cuando otros nos fallan.

Dios es quien nos redime. Él es quien envió a los profetas, aunque sus mensajes fueran ignorados y los profetas perseguidos. Él es quien continúa esperando por nosotros, aun cuando le hemos fallado tantas veces en el pasado.

Él es la razón por la que seguimos adelante. Él es la razón por la que tenemos esperanza, no solo para nosotros mismos sino también para nuestros hermanos.

The urgency of the last minute is something that many homemakers deal with regularly. No matter how organized we are, sometimes we put off tasks because we dislike them or wait until we are under pressure.

Habitual procrastination potentially leads to higher levels of stress. Maybe I’m odd, but it is hard for me to stay calm and collected when the pressure is mounting. By the time the last minute things are completed I’m too exhausted to enjoy the planned event.

Toothaches and Road Trips

It is a mystery to me why a family member ends up in a dentist chair a day or two before we leave on a trip. Maybe it hasn’t happened as often as I think, but the frustration of an unplanned trip to the dentist at an inopportune time is riveted in my mind. Now I schedule an imaginary appointment before a trip. If it is not a dental emergency, some other issue is bound to fill that time slot.

Deadlines are a normal part of life. Without them we would be unmotivated, and our days would lack purpose. Interruptions are also a normal part of life. They constantly give an unpredictable twist to our days and weeks. If we let too many tasks wait until the last minute, interruptions and deadlines collide, and chaos reigns.

Change the Last-Minute Scenario

Deadlines and interruptions cannot be eliminated but we can limit last-minute tasks. Sometimes it takes some honest looking back to figure out what caused our stress. Often, we blame it on interruptions and fail to realize that poor planning or procrastination might have been the culprit.

For example, if guests are coming and we plan to wash windows and make a dessert along with a dozen more tasks on the day of their arrival, there is no room for disruptions. From experience, we know interruptions will come. So, isn’t it better to “plan” for a bee sting and a stubbed toe?

Why not schedule window washing and dessert another day? That might mean some fingerprints on the windows and a simpler dessert, but isn’t that better than a great deal of stress at the last minute?

Do some tasks ahead of time

Deciding early in the day what to make for supper and packing the diaper bag in advance are little things that can make a big difference at the last minute. When our children were young, I started packing suitcases a day before a trip versus the day of leaving. I was better able to cope with the last-minute rush if that job was out of the way.

Do the most important tasks first

This approach gives freedom to skip jobs of lesser importance when up against a time crunch.

Sometimes not everything on the task list is of equal value. Dropping a task is difficult for a perfectionist, but it is possible to develop new habits.

Break work into smaller bits

Sometimes the enormity of a task makes it seem too huge to start. Break down the large task into smaller components. Completing a smaller task is much more manageable. Deep cleaning my kitchen is a task that I do not enjoy. If my planner says, “deep-clean kitchen,” it’s easy to ignore.

But if my planner says, “clean appliances, wipe out cupboards, and wash windows,” it seems more doable.

There are so many joyful events in life; why be hassled by procrastination? Give yourself the liberty to live life differently. A few minor changes can make the biggest difference between a blessed or stressed last minute.

Brådska i sista minuten är något som många hemmavarande möter regelbundet. Oavsett hur organiserade vi är skjuter vi ibland upp uppgifter för att vi ogillar dem eller väntar tills vi är under press.

Vanemässig uppskjutning kan leda till högre stressnivåer. Kanske är jag ovanlig, men det är svårt för mig att hålla mig lugn och samlad när trycket ökar. När sista-minuten-sakerna är avklarade är jag ofta för utmattad för att njuta av det planerade evenemanget.

Tandvärk och bilresor

Det är ett mysterium för mig varför en familjemedlem hamnar i tandläkarstolen en dag eller två innan vi åker på en resa. Kanske har det inte hänt så ofta som jag tror, men frustrationen över ett oplanerat tandläkarbesök vid ett olämpligt tillfälle sitter kvar i mitt minne. Numera bokar jag en inbillad tid före en resa. Om det inte är ett tandläkarakutfall kommer något annat säkert att fylla den tiden.

Tidsfrister är en normal del av livet. Utan dem skulle vi vara omotiverade och våra dagar skulle sakna mening. Avbrott är också en normal del av livet. De ger ständigt oväntade vändningar åt våra dagar och veckor. Om vi låter för många uppgifter vänta till sista minuten krockar avbrott och tidsfrister, och kaos uppstår.

Ändra sista-minuten-scenariot

Tidsfrister och avbrott kan inte elimineras men vi kan begränsa uppgifter i sista minuten. Ibland krävs det att vi är ärliga mot oss själva och ser tillbaka för att ta reda på vad som orsakade vår stress. Ofta skyller vi på avbrotten och inser inte att dålig planering eller uppskjutande kan ha varit boven.

Till exempel, om gäster kommer och vi planerar att putsa fönster och göra en efterrätt tillsammans med ett dussin andra saker på dagen för deras ankomst, finns det inget utrymme för störningar. Av erfarenhet vet vi att avbrott kommer. Så är det inte bättre att "planera" för ett bistick och en stukad tå?

Varför inte schemalägga fönsterputsning och efterrätt en annan dag? Det kan innebära en del fingeravtryck på fönstren och en enklare efterrätt, men är inte det bättre än en massa stress i sista minuten?

Gör vissa uppgifter i förväg

Att bestämma tidigt på dagen vad som ska lagas till middag och att packa skötväskan i förväg är små saker som kan göra stor skillnad i sista minuten. När våra barn var små började jag packa resväskor en dag före en resa istället för på avresedagen. Jag kunde hantera sista-minuten-ruschen bättre om den uppgiften var ur vägen.

Gör de viktigaste uppgifterna först

Detta förhållningssätt ger frihet att hoppa över mindre viktiga uppgifter när tiden är knapp.

Ibland är inte allt på uppgiftslistan lika värdefullt. Att stryka en uppgift är svårt för en perfektionist, men det är möjligt att utveckla nya vanor.

Dela upp arbetet i mindre bitar

Ibland gör uppgiftens enorma omfattning att den känns för stor för att börja. Dela upp den stora uppgiften i mindre delar. Att slutföra en mindre uppgift är mycket mer hanterbart. Att grundligt rengöra mitt kök är en uppgift jag inte tycker om. Om min planeringsbok säger "grundlig rengöring av kök" är det lätt att ignorera.

Men om min planeringsbok säger "rengör apparater, torka ur skåp och tvätta fönster" känns det mer genomförbart.

Det finns så många glädjefyllda händelser i livet; varför låta uppskjutande störa dem? Ge dig själv friheten att leva annorlunda. Några små förändringar kan göra största skillnaden mellan en välsignad eller stressad sista minut.

Arise be glad! For dawn is here!
Rejoice and sing! The night is past,
The Dayspring shineth from on high,
The grace of God to man is nigh!
Rejoice and praise the King of Kings!
Give thanks and laud, for more is here!

Arise and glorify the Lord!
Extol and praise His worthy name!
He shineth from the heav’ns in love,
And showers blessings from above,
His mercy reaches down to men-
Adore and praise our mighty Lord!

Give thanks and sing to Christ our King
And worship Him with reverent praise;
Bow down in awful, holy fear-
The Holiness of God is here;
In wondrous beauty bend the knee;
Adore th’ almighty King of Kings!

I can still smell the tantalizing cacophony of odors as I clutched my father’s strong hand, weaving our way through the masses of tourists that crowded the building. The vendors at the Green Dragon Farmer’s Market in Ephrata, PA, were trying their best to entice buyers with their rows of fresh fish over ice, cheeses of every variety, deli meat and sandwiches, and piles of fresh fruit. And, oh, the candy! My young preschool mind had never seen so many delectable sweets in one place at one time.

The past two days for me were like the boy at the candy store. I had the privilege of attending Christian Aid Ministries’ first Annual Writers’ Conference. I brushed shoulders with well-known authors such as Katrina Hoover Lee, Johnny Miller, and Ruthann Stelfox. I chatted with aspiring writers and seasoned school teachers. I had the opportunity to sit under hours of inspirational and educational workshops on how to write to communicate, using realistic dialog, descriptive writing, and much more. We all had one common goal in mind. Together, we share and learn how to effectively communicate what is in our hearts, and through the power of the written word, transmit those thoughts to your hearts.

The Heartbeat of the Remnant is a means to communicate inspirational thoughts to eager readers scattered across the globe. Courageous writers step forward with pen and paper or keyboard and monitor and help spread the Good News of the Word of God with caution, correction, and edification. Yet, we need more such writers. We need young believers who bravely submit their first children’s stories. Seasoned grandfathers who bring words of admonishment to the younger generation. Mothers who share experiences and trials with other mothers who are in the throes of raising little ones. Youth encouraging fellow youth to press toward the mark of the prize of the high calling in Christ Jesus. Fathers who with a concerned eye watch the world pressing in on the Christian homes. Together, these aspiring writers will produce a periodical that will endure on the family coffee table for many years. I encourage you, fellow believers, to give it a try. Nelson Mandela, former president of South Africa wrote, “Failure is a teacher, and at the end of your life, what do you think you’ll feel worst about, failing or never trying?”

The Berean Voice has a goal to provide printed material that will help readers navigate through the varied and difficult seasons of life. All our material is available at no charge, but we are dependent on the donations of our supporters. Here is a list of books we have available:

The Power of the Love of Truth
Christian Counseling- Counterfeit?
The Heart of God
Free Indeed!
Pilgrims and Politics
Cup & Cross
The High Cost of Holistic Healing
Secrets of Successful Writing
The Catholic Connection
Psychiatry and Mood altering Medications
The Mennonite Church and Modernism

In 2017 and 2018, the Berean Voice printed a series of vaccine articles in The Heartbeat of the Remnant magazine. These articles were a sincere effort to examine various aspects of vaccine usage with an unbiased approach. We attempted to present the facts as clearly as possible and let the readers draw their own conclusions.

Since then, we have received numerous requests from our readers to publish all the vaccine articles in a booklet, which we agreed to do. But then along came 2019, bringing coronavirus with it. This monumental event upended the vaccine debate and ushered in a frenzied rush to market COVID-19 remedies, many of which were not properly tested. We put the printing on hold, unsure whether to include information on these new and unproven COVID-19 “vaccines.” As time progressed and the deadly nature of COVID-19 abated, we decided to publish the original vaccine articles in a booklet without any additional articles on the COVID-19 debate. We are pleased that the project is nearing completion and will be announced when it is released.

Blessings to all,

Edward Martin

Saya masih bisa mencium paduan aroma yang menggoda ketika saya menggenggam tangan ayah yang kuat, menenun jalan kami melalui kerumunan wisatawan yang memenuhi gedung itu. Para penjual di Green Dragon Farmer’s Market di Ephrata, PA, melakukan yang terbaik untuk memikat pembeli dengan deretan ikan segar di atas es, keju dari segala jenis, daging deli dan sandwich, serta tumpukan buah segar. Dan, oh, permen! Pikiran saya yang masih prasekolah belum pernah melihat begitu banyak manisan lezat di satu tempat sekaligus.

Dua hari terakhir bagi saya seperti anak laki-laki di toko permen. Saya mendapat kehormatan menghadiri Konferensi Penulis Tahunan pertama Christian Aid Ministries. Saya bersinggungan dengan penulis terkenal seperti Katrina Hoover Lee, Johnny Miller, dan Ruthann Stelfox. Saya berbincang dengan penulis pemula dan guru sekolah berpengalaman. Saya berkesempatan mengikuti berjam-jam lokakarya yang inspiratif dan mendidik tentang cara menulis untuk berkomunikasi, menggunakan dialog yang realistis, penulisan deskriptif, dan banyak lagi. Kita semua memiliki satu tujuan bersama. Bersama, kita berbagi dan belajar bagaimana secara efektif mengomunikasikan apa yang ada di hati kita, dan melalui kuasa kata-kata tertulis, mentransmisikan pikiran-pikiran itu ke dalam hati Anda.

The Heartbeat of the Remnant adalah sarana untuk mengomunikasikan pemikiran yang menginspirasi kepada pembaca yang bersemangat yang tersebar di seluruh dunia. Penulis-penulis yang berani maju dengan pena dan kertas atau papan ketik dan monitor membantu menyebarkan Kabar Baik dari Firman Allah dengan kehati-hatian, koreksi, dan penguatan. Namun, kami membutuhkan lebih banyak penulis seperti itu. Kami membutuhkan orang-orang percaya muda yang dengan berani mengajukan cerita anak pertama mereka. Kakek-kakek berpengalaman yang membawa kata-kata teguran kepada generasi yang lebih muda. Ibu-ibu yang berbagi pengalaman dan pergumulan dengan ibu-ibu lain yang sedang disibukkan oleh membesarkan anak-anak kecil. Pemuda yang mendorong sesama pemuda untuk mengejar tanda dari hadiah panggilan tinggi dalam Kristus Yesus. Para ayah yang dengan mata cemas mengamati dunia yang mendesak masuk ke rumah-rumah Kristen. Bersama, penulis-penulis yang bercita-cita ini akan menghasilkan sebuah terbitan berkala yang akan bertahan di meja kopi keluarga selama bertahun-tahun. Saya mendorong Anda, saudara seiman, untuk mencobanya. Nelson Mandela, mantan presiden Afrika Selatan menulis, “Failure is a teacher, and at the end of your life, what do you think you’ll feel worst about, failing or never trying?”

The Berean Voice memiliki tujuan menyediakan bahan cetak yang akan membantu pembaca menavigasi melalui musim-musim kehidupan yang beragam dan sulit. Semua bahan kami tersedia tanpa biaya, tetapi kami bergantung pada sumbangan dari para pendukung kami. Berikut adalah daftar buku yang kami miliki:

The Power of the Love of Truth
Christian Counseling- Counterfeit?
The Heart of God
Free Indeed!
Pilgrims and Politics
Cup & Cross
The High Cost of Holistic Healing
Secrets of Successful Writing
The Catholic Connection
Psychiatry and Mood altering Medications
The Mennonite Church and Modernism

Pada 2017 dan 2018, The Berean Voice mencetak serangkaian artikel vaksin dalam majalah The Heartbeat of the Remnant. Artikel-artikel ini merupakan upaya tulus untuk memeriksa berbagai aspek penggunaan vaksin dengan pendekatan yang tidak memihak. Kami mencoba menyajikan fakta sejelas mungkin dan membiarkan pembaca menarik kesimpulan mereka sendiri.

Sejak itu, kami menerima banyak permintaan dari pembaca kami untuk menerbitkan semua artikel vaksin dalam sebuah buku kecil, yang kami setujui untuk dilakukan. Tetapi kemudian datanglah 2019, membawa coronavirus bersamanya. Peristiwa monumental ini mengubah pembahasan vaksin dan mengantar pada euforia buru-buru memasarkan obat COVID-19, banyak di antaranya tidak diuji dengan benar. Kami menunda pencetakan, ragu apakah akan menyertakan informasi tentang “vaksin” COVID-19 baru dan belum terbukti ini. Seiring berjalannya waktu dan sifat mematikan COVID-19 mereda, kami memutuskan untuk menerbitkan artikel vaksin asli dalam sebuah buku kecil tanpa artikel tambahan tentang perdebatan COVID-19. Kami gembira bahwa proyek ini hampir selesai dan akan diumumkan ketika dirilis.

Berkat bagi Anda semua,

Edward Martin
