’n Christus-gesentreerde hofmakery is ’n reeks boodskappe oor godvrugtige hofmakery, gepreek deur Paul Hershberger. Hy het hierdie boodskappe verskeie kere op verskillende plekke oor die afgelope tien jaar gepreek. Onlangs het ons dit laat transkribeer en ingekort vir leesduidelikheid. Nadat ons al ses artikels in The Heartbeat of the Remnant geplaas het, sal ons dit in ’n brosjure publiseer. Dit is die eerste artikel van ses.

Inleiding

My vrou en ek het die voorreg gehad om ’n hofmakery sonder berou of skuldgevoelens te hê. Ons is geseën met ouers wat ons op die regte pad gelei het en ons geleenthede gegee het wat hulle self nie gehad het nie.

As jy daardie getuienis of herinnering nie het nie, moet asseblief nie op ’n skuldreis gaan nie. My gebed vir jou is egter dat jy ’n brandende belas-ting en visie in jou hart kry om dit vir jou kinders te hê. Dit kan jou beloning wees.

’n Christus-gesentreerde hofmakery is ’n tydperk tussen ’n enkellopende lewe en ’n getroude lewe. Die besluite wat jy in hierdie tydperk neem, sal julle lewens vir altyd beïnvloed. Met God se seën oor jou lewe kan julle eindig sonder berou of skuldgevoelens.

Vyf doelwitte vir hierdie reeks oor Christus-gesentreerde hofmakery.

Doel #1. Om die harte van die vaders na hul kinders te draai.

Doel #2. Om die harte van die kinders na hul vaders te draai.

Doel #3. Dat ouers ’n belas-ting kry om elkeen van hul kinders te lei in die volmaakte wil van God vir hul lewens.

Doel #4. Dat jongmense ’n belas-ting kry om God te soek, vervulling en doel te vind in die wandel met God, en dat julle volwassenheid sal soek in julle maniere en julle karakter.

Doel #5. Dat jong mans en jong vroue sal opstaan om godvrugtige vaders en godvrugtige moeders te wees met ’n visie om nog ’n godvrugtige geslag groot te maak, sodat die Evangelie van Jesus Christus voort kan gaan.

God se Plan vir Man en Vrou

Prediker 12:1 sê, “Remember now thy Creator in the days of thy youth, while the evil days come not, nor the years draw nigh, when thou shalt say, I have no pleasure in them.” My begeerte is dat elkeen van julle jou Skepper kan onthou in die dae van julle jeug. Draai julle hart, julle fokus, en julle lewe om om julle Skepper, die Almagtige God in die hemel, na te jaag.

Wat beteken hy met “while the evil days come not” en “the years draw nigh”? Dit beteken die Here te soek wanneer jy jonk is. Neem die energie van jou jeug en soek God. Jongmense, julle is jonk en vol idees, visies, planne en drome. Ek dink nie daar is enige van julle wat net daarvan hou om in ’n gemaksstoel te sit, jou voete op te lig en te droom oor hoe verskriklik en afgryslik die lewe gaan wees nie. Ons doen dit nie, nè? Maar as ons nie met God wandel en God se plan volg nie, sal moeilike dinge op ons kom. Wanneer moeilike dinge in die lewe kom, het ons geen plek om na toe te draai nie. Ons droom dat die lewe goed sal uitwerk. Die besluite en optrede in ons jeug beïnvloed ons vir die res van ons lewens. Die goeie nuus is dat dit ons op ’n goeie manier kan beïnvloed. Die slegte nuus is dat dit ons op ’n slegte manier kan beïnvloed. Dit hang af van watter besluite en keuses ons maak. Maar jongmense, julle is jonk, en julle het die geleentheid om te kies.

Kom ons gaan na die begin van Genesis.

“And the LORD God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him. And out of the ground the LORD God formed every beast of the field, and every fowl of the air; and brought them unto Adam to see what he would call them: and whatsoever Adam called every living creature, that was the name thereof. And Adam gave names to all cattle, and to the fowl of the air, and to every beast of the field; but for Adam there was not found an help meet for him. And the LORD God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, and he slept: and he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh instead thereof; And the rib, which the LORD God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man. And Adam said, This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man. Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh” (Genesis 2:18-24).

“And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth. So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them. And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth” (Genesis 1:26-28).

“And the Lord God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him” (Genesis 2:18). “I’ll make him an help that is meet for him.” God said He would do that.

“So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them” (Genesis 1:27). God het gemaak. God het ons manlik en vroulik geskep. Dit verg ’n groot mate van blinde geloof om te glo dat ons perfek as man en vrou geëvolueer het. Die skepping van man en vrou is God se plan. Dit is een van die lewende bewyse van Skepping. God het gemaak. God het geskep. Dit is God se plan. God is die Skrywer. En God se plan bring seën.

Ek wil graag tien verskillende aspekte van hierdie seën van God se plan beskou.

1) God bring Eva na Adam toe.

“And the rib, which the Lord God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man. And Adam said, This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man” (Genesis 2:22-23).

God het Adam in ’n diepe slaap laat val. Toe het God Eva geskep en haar na Adam gebring. Adam het ontwaak en besef, “Hierdie een is vir my!” Hy het al die diere sien verbygaan toe hy hulle name gegee het. Nou bring God vir hom iemand wat vir hom bestem is. Hy het ook besef, “Sy is uit my sy geneem.” Sy is naby sy hart. “Dit is been van my bene en vleis van my vlees.” Dit is nie ’n hond nie; dit is nie ’n kameelperd, of ’n aap nie. Hierdie een wat God vir hom gebring het, is soos hy. God se plan het ’n seën.

Adam en Eva het nog nooit ’n metgesel gehad nie. Adam en Eva het nog nooit toeelaat dat die emosies van hul harte voorgegaan het nie. Iets het in Adam en Eva se harte gebeur. Adam was ’n “een-vrou man,” en Eva was ’n “een-man vrou.” Hulle het hul hartpassies nooit aan iemand anders gegee nie. God het daardie plan ook vir ons. God se plan bring seën.

2) Verlaat en heg in eenheid vir die lewe.

“Therefore Bshall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh” (Genesis 2:24).

Hierdie vers sê, “Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother,” maar Adam en Eva het nie ’n vader en moeder gehad nie. Wat God sê is dit werk nie dat daar hegting kan wees sonder verwerping nie. Ook in Markus 10:7 lees ons, “For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother, and cleave to his wife.” Dit is God se plan, en God se plan bring seën.

Verlaat beteken om agter te laat, om te verlaat. “For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother” beteken om ouers agter te laat. Kom ons dink aan ’n jong man wat ’n baie goeie tuisondervinding het. Hy is geseën en het alles wat hy nodig het. Tog, sodra God sy Eva in sy lewe bring, kom daar iets binne-in hom op en sê hy: “Ek verlaat!” Maar dit is God se plan. En God se plan bring seën.

Dit is nie net om sy vader en moeder te verlaat nie; hy heg ook aan sy vrou. Heg beteken “om vas te plak, om te kleef.” Ons ken goed aanmekaargeplakte houtpanele. Allerhande stewige meubels is gemaak uit gepaarde panele wat aanmekaargeplak is. En as dit reg geplak is, sal dit nie by die samesmeltings uitmekaar kom nie. As jy dit uitmekaar ruk, sal jy die hout self moet skeur. God se gom werk dieselfde manier en plak twee mense aanmekaar. Die enigste manier om hulle uitmekaar te ruk is deur te splinter en te skeur, en God seën dit nie. Maar verlaat en heg, saambly en vasplak—dit is God se plan en dit bring seën.

3) Hulle sal een vlees wees.

“Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh” (Genesis 2:24). Twee enkellopende mense wat een getroude paar word, word een eenheid voor God en ’n familie voor God. Hulle word een vlees, waar God hulle as tesame en een sien.

“And they twain shall be one flesh: so then they are no more twain, but one flesh. What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder” (Mark 10:8-9). God se plan vir man en vrou is dat Hy Eva na Adam bring. Dan moet die verlaat en heg plaasvind. Hy veroorsaak dat hulle een vlees word. Afskeur bring geen seën nie maar bringsagony,pain,travail, and hurt. Daar is geen seën in skeiding nie. Maar God se plan bring seën.

4) Nie ’n ongelyke juk nie.

“Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers: for what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness” (2 Corinthians 6:14-15). “The wife is bound by the law as long as her husband liveth; but if her husband be dead, she is at liberty to be married to whom she will; only in the Lord” (1 Corinthians 7:39).

God se plan is dat huwelik ’n gelyke juk is. God sal nie ’n Eva na ’n Adam bring in ’n huwelik wat ’n ongelyke juk is nie. Kom ons dink aan verlaat en heg, aan mekaar vasplak, en twee wat een word. In die huwelik is daardie twee nou een voor God. Stel jou ’n slegte huweliksverhouding voor—’n gesin soos dit wat probeer funksioneer. Daar sal geen seën wees nie.

Maar ’n gelyke juk bring seën! God begeer dat ons in een vlees, een hart en een gedagtes verbintenis sal wees. Hy wil ons sien verenig in hart, verstand en vleis—die hele wese, een wees. God se plan bring seën.

5) God het beplan dat ons kinders sal hê.

“And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth” (Genesis 1:28). Dink aan die vreugde en die wonder elke keer as nog ’n kind in ’n Christelike huis gebore word. God het dit so beplan. En as God Adam sy Eva gebring het, en hulle verlaat en heg, hulle een vlees, een hart, een gedagte word—indien hulle gelyk gebind is en God seën hulle met kinders—word dit ’n vreugdevolle toevlug waar God kan woon. “And God blessed Noah and his sons, and said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth” (Genesis 9:1). “And you, be ye fruitful, and multiply; bring forth abundantly in the earth, and multiply therein” (Genesis 9:7). God se plan bring seën.

6) Hoofskapsorde.

“But I would have you know, that the head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God” (1 Corinthians 11:3). Dit is God, dan Christus, die man, en die vrou. God het ’n hoofskapsorde ingestel, en hierdie hoofskapsorde is ’n seën. Dit is God se plan, en dit is ’n seën.

“Children, obey your parents in the Lord: for this is right. Honor thy father and mother; which is the first commandment with promise; That it may be well with thee, and thou mayest live long on the earth” (Ephesians 6:1-3). Kinders, gehoorsaam julle ouers in die Here is deel van die hoofskapsorde. Dit is nie moeilik om te verstaan nie, of hoe? ’n Huis wat God se plan volg is net ’n geseënde omstandigheid. Jongmense leer om onder gesag te wees. Maak dit julle prioriteit. Hoe vinniger julle leer om onder gesag te wees, hoe beter sal julle voorberei wees vir die verantwoordelikhede in die lewe.

Ek onthou dat ek na die getroude lewe gekyk het en aspirasies gehad het oor om kinders te leer en ’n godvrugtige gesin groot te maak. Ek het na die “Godly Home” reeks geluister en gedink ek is gereed. Maar toe het die dag aangebreek toe dit my beurt en my verantwoordelikheid was, en skielik wou my hart verwelk. Verantwoordelikheid voel nie dieselfde as daaroor droom nie. JY moet iets doen! JY is verantwoordelik. JY moet dit laat gebeur. En tog, nie net laat dit gebeur nie; jy moet dit laat gebeur op ’n Christus-agtige wyse. Jy moet dit laat gebeur op ’n manier waarop die salwing van die Gees van God oor jou gesin kan kom. Hoe meer ons leer om onder gesag te wees, hoe beter sal ons voorbereid wees vir daardie verantwoordelikhede. Hoe meer ons besef ons het God nodig, hoe beter is ons af. Maak ’n hoë prioriteit daarvan om te leer om onder gesag te wees as kinders en as jongmense. “My son, forget not my law; but let thine heart keep my commandments: For length of days, and long life, and peace, shall they add to thee” (Proverbs 3:1-2).

God sal sy seën byvoeg as ons in hierdie hoofskapsorde bly. Hoe meer jy leer om onder gesag te wees, hoe meer sal jy geseën word wanneer jy jou huis vestig. God se plan het seëninge.

7) ’n Godvrugtige huwelik.

Ephesiers 5:21,22,24 sê, “Submitting yourselves one to another in the fear of God. Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord. . . Therefore as the church is subject unto Christ, so let the wives be to their own husbands in every thing.”

Kyk eers na vers 21, “submitting yourselves one to another.” Daar is ’n vermenging wat in ’n godvrugtige huis moet plaasvind. Hierdie vermenging behoort in die vrees van God te gebeur. As ons die een aan die ander onderwerp in die vrees van God, sal ons God gehoorsaam omdat ons Sy seëninge wil hê.

Ephesiers 5:22, 24 “Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord. . . Therefore as the church is subject unto Christ, so let the wives be to their own husbands in every thing.” Jong dames, julle kan daarop staatmaak: onderdanigheid aan Pa is dieselfde as onderdanigheid aan ’n man. Julle kan dit oefen terwyl julle enkel is. Dit sal help om karakter in julle lewe te bou. ’n Rebelserige en ongeskikte vrou gaan nie die seën van God bring nie.

Dit gaan voort en sê, in Ephesiers 5:25,28,29. “Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it . . . So ought men to love their wives as their own bodies. He that loveth his wife loveth himself. For no man ever yet hated his own flesh; but nourisheth and cherisheth it, even as the Lord the church.” Jong mans, dit sê dat mans hul vroue moet liefhê. Wie dink julle het God in jul lewens geplaas om julle voor te berei om julle vrou te lief te hê? Julle ma! Wil julle leer hoe om julle vrou te lief te hê? Leer hoe om met jou ma oor die weg te kom, jou ma te lief te hê en omgee vir haar. Wil julle oefen om julle toekomstige vrou lief te hê? Gaan aan en liefhê jou ma.

Vers 33, “Nevertheless let every one of you in particular so love his wife even as himself; and the wife see that she reverence her husband.” God se plan bring seëninge.

8) Saam erfgename van die genade van die lewe.

1 Petrus 3:7 “Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honor unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel, and as being heirs together of the grace of life; that your prayers be not hindered.” As mans gee ons eer aan die vrou. Sy is die swakker vat en die een wat die kinders gebaar het! Sy het baie traumatiese veranderinge in haar lewe deurgegaan. Sy is die een wat gouer uitput en moeg word.

En hy sê, “Husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge.”

Jong mans, leer om jou ma en jou susters te verstaan. Dit sal jou help nadat jy getroud is. Moenie aflei dat—ah, dit is net vroue nie. Nee, jy wil God se seën hê. Leer hulle ken en verstaan.

“Being heirs together of the grace of life.” God wil hê ons moet saam erfgename wees van die genade van die lewe. As ons nie saam erfgename van die genade van die lewe is nie, kan ons dan afsonderlik erfgename wees van die genade van die lewe? Ek dink nie so nie. Hy sê ons moet saam erfgename wees sodat ons gebede nie belemmer word nie. As ons dus afsonderlike erfgename is, kan ons dan sê ons gebede sal belemmer word? Ja, ons gebede sal belemmer word. Laat ons eer aan die vrou gee as aan die swakker vat. Elke klein bietjie wat jy in hierdie gebied kan bykry sal jou later alleenlik seën. Dit is die moeite werd. God se plan bring seën.

9) ’n Geseënde en veilige huis.

Dit kom deels uit 1 Petrus 3:7, maar ook uit Psalm 144:12 “That our sons may be as plants grown up in their youth; that our daughters may be as corner stones, polished after the similitude of a palace.” Die genade van God is op ’n veilige huis waar daar eenheid is. Waar Pa Ma verstaan, waar Pa omgee vir Ma. Pa dien en is daar om te help en te lei. Hy is daar om rigting te gee met ’n hart van deernis. God se plan vir man en vrou—God se plan bring seëninge.

10) Soos Christus en die kerk.

“Therefore as the church is subject unto Christ, so let the wives be to their own husbands in every thing. Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it; That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word, That he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish. So ought men to love their wives as their own bodies. He that loveth his wife loveth himself. For no man ever yet hated his own flesh; but nourisheth and cherisheth it, even as the Lord the church” (Ephesians 5:24-29).

“Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave Himself for it.” God soek na mans wat bereid is om hul lewens te gee. Enkellopende jong mans, is julle bereid om die roep te beantwoord en julle lewe te gee? Dit is ’n hoë roeping van God. Dit is God se plan.

Jong mans, is julle bereid om julle lewe, julle eie agenda, en daardie onafhanklike dinge wat julle graag doen, neerlê? Is julle bereid om geduldig, sagmoedig en begripvol te wees? Is julle bereid om slaap te verloor en voort te gaan selfs wanneer julle moeg is? Is julle bereid om kalm te bly en nie te reageer in stresvolle omstandighede nie? Is julle bereid om ’n vrou en kinders te lei en te begelei, ewige siele, deur hierdie lewe?

My pleidooi is egter dat julle sal vrywillig aanmeld en sê, “Ek is bereid om my toe te lê op die Woord van God, die wil van God, die plan van God, en ek sal my lewe gee. Ek is bereid om dit op die altaar te lê.” Jesus het Sy lewe vir ons gegee, en Hy vergelyk die huwelik met die kerk en Homself.

Daar is ook ’n behoefte aan moeders wat onderdanig en toegeeflik aan gesag is. Moeders wat nie die vroueligtingsbeweging van ons tyd volg nie, maar eerder tevrede is om huisvroue en bewaarders van die huis te wees.

Jong dames, is julle bereid om in te teken? Sal julle julle harte gee om gelei en bestuur te word? Is julle bereid om te volg en getroulik ondergeskik te wees aan julle gesag? Is julle bereid om te dien en uitgeput te word vir julle gesin? Is julle bereid om te dien en uitgeput te word vir JOU gesin? As julle eendag trou, sal dit JOU gesin wees waarvoor julle sal dien en uitgeleef word. Is julle bereid om pyn en ongemak te dra? Is julle bereid om ’n helpgenote te wees en julle self te gee vir sy las en visie?

Maar soos ons na God se plan en seëninge kyk, wil julle God se seën hê, jongmense! Dit beteken egter dat julle ooreenkomstig keuses moet maak. Staak op en maak besluite wat tot volwassenheid lei. Volwassenheid kom deur die proses om God te soek. Maak ’n toewyding in julle harte om julself oop te stel vir God se seëninge en beginsels. Ek moedig julle aan om met God te wandel, om ’n verhouding met Jesus Christus te hê, en om dit in nederigheid te doen.

Soek na Christus-agtige karakter, en doen dit doelbewus. Dit is so maklik vir ons om net die lewe te leef soos dit gebeur. Maar as ons doelbewuste besluite neem, sal dit ons êrens neem! Daardie besluite maak saak. Doen dinge volgens God se plan.

God het ’n plan vir man en vrou en Hy het ’n plan vir jou.

Circumstantial overload might be the most difficult. We can choose not to go to a Norwex party if we need to give our schedule some space. But if a child breaks a leg in the middle of wedding preparations, we have no choice other than to make the best of the situation.

Circumstantial overload may happen slowly, as in the following story, or it may happen quickly as in the case of an accident in which a family member is injured.

Becky is in her thirties with seven children under seventeen. A few years ago, one of their chicken houses burned down. At the time, they were thankful that the chickens had left the day before and that no one was close by when the propane tank exploded.

“My husband faced the disaster like a man,” says Becky. “His calm spirit helped me relax. I felt certain that we could make the financial adjustments and life would go on as before. But I was wrong. Very wrong.”

“In time the mess was cleaned up, and Rick looked into rebuilding. The quotes were higher than expected, so he opted to do some of the work himself. He also took on a part-time job to provide more income. Our boys were old enough to help, yet they couldn’t do much without Rick’s direction.”

“I first felt the adjustment in my wallet, but I consoled myself that this was only temporary. Then the spark in Rick’s eyes was replaced with a dull stare. He became distant from us. I knew something wasn’t right, but I couldn’t put my finger on it.”

“Then he was elected to finish the last four months of secretarial duties for a brother who spent some time in Bulgaria. That night he came home and wept. ‘Doesn’t anyone understand what I’m going through? Every time I turn around, there is something to do. The boys want to go fishing, you need a new clothesline, and the chicken house needs to be finished in six months! I am not mentally capable of handling one more duty.’”

“That was the straw that broke the camel’s back,” Becky said. “I became alarmed when I heard him yawning in the middle of the night and knew that he was not sleeping.”

“It was clear to me that my perfectionist husband was overloaded. More and more Rick leaned on me. I cut back on my commitments and tried to keep my time free so that I was available to help lessen his load.”

“I felt like a lifeguard trying to keep a man from drowning while taking in a bit too much water myself. Many of the home-life responsibilities fell on my shoulders. Then I was asked to fill the position of food committee for Mrs. ‘Going-to-Bulgaria.’”

Unfortunately, circumstantial stress is often unnoticed. Worse yet, the victim can be misunderstood or misjudged. Becky said, “My darkest day came when I was accused of being selfish with my time because I declined the food committee request.”

Prolonged overload can be emotionally and mentally damaging

Intense, long-lasting pressures or troubles shouldered alone can cause severe stress. Minor stress is normal, but prolonged stress can cause depression, anxiety, heart disease, and high blood pressure. How you handle prolonged stress is important.

Sometimes this type of overload is not public knowledge. Traumatic events in our plain circles tend to receive prayer, finances, and weekly budget updates. At the same time, other saints are suffering deeply on the sidelines with little recognition or financial aid. It could be strained relationships or little bills that add up to a big sum. Betrayal and rejection cause stress beyond measure. There are no quick fixes to circumstantial stress, but little sparks of light can help you navigate the darkness.

Talk about your situation with someone you trust

Sometimes just talking about problems can help you to put issues in perspective. Hearing yourself verbalize a stressful situation somehow clears brain fog and gives a clearer path forward.

Find routine

When stress prevails, racing thoughts, forgetfulness, and inability to focus comes uninvited. Having a routine can bring some rhythm to your mental well-being. The smallest normalcy brings a moment of pleasure, and it is soothing to the soul.

Intentionally seek a breather

Lingering stress can cause agitation, moodiness, and the desire to take control. Sometimes it is hard to think beyond mental fog, but it is so important to find refreshment for your mental wellbeing. Stress hormones can speed up your heart rate and tighten your blood vessels. That temporarily raises your blood pressure. The opposite happens when you relax. Being relaxed helps you have a calmer, clearer mind which improves your concentration and decision-making.

Believe that God cares

Say it. Read the Psalms over and over. Listen to good music. Take short walks and pray aloud. Keep your eyes on Jesus. Believe “Weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning” (Psalm 30:5).

If you are facing circumstantial overload, be patient and realistic. God will make a way for you. Many times, He opens doors just when we are running out of options. He will supply the needed grace for that hour. And the next hour. And the next. At times, surprising opportunities come, and prayers are answered in unexpected ways. However He chooses to work on your behalf, hold to His unchanging hand.

Regardless of the type of overload you might be encountering, turn to your Heavenly Father.

Ask Him for direction and wisdom. And say with the Psalmist, “In thee, O LORD, do I put my trust: let me never be put to confusion” (Psalm 71:1).

Umständebedingte Überlastung kann die schwierigste sein. Wir können uns dafür entscheiden, einer Norwex-Party fernzubleiben, wenn wir unserem Zeitplan etwas Luft geben müssen. Aber wenn ein Kind sich mitten in den Hochzeitsvorbereitungen das Bein bricht, haben wir keine Wahl, außer das Beste aus der Situation zu machen.

Umständebedingte Überlastung kann sich langsam einstellen, wie in der folgenden Geschichte, oder sie kann schnell eintreten, etwa bei einem Unfall, bei dem ein Familienmitglied verletzt wird.

Becky ist in ihren Dreißigern und hat sieben Kinder unter siebzehn. Vor einigen Jahren brannte eines ihrer Hühnerställe ab. Damals waren sie dankbar, dass die Hühner am Tag zuvor weggegangen waren und dass niemand in der Nähe war, als der Propantank explodierte.

„Mein Mann stellte sich der Katastrophe wie ein Mann“, sagt Becky. „Sein ruhiger Geist half mir, mich zu entspannen. Ich war sicher, dass wir die finanziellen Anpassungen vornehmen könnten und das Leben wie zuvor weitergehen würde. Aber ich lag falsch. Sehr falsch.“

„Mit der Zeit wurde das Durcheinander beseitigt, und Rick prüfte den Wiederaufbau. Die Angebote waren höher als erwartet, also entschied er sich, einen Teil der Arbeit selbst zu machen. Er nahm auch eine Teilzeitstelle an, um mehr Einkommen zu erzielen. Unsere Jungen waren alt genug, um zu helfen, doch ohne Ricks Anweisung konnten sie nicht viel tun.“

„Zuerst spürte ich die Umstellung in meinem Portemonnaie, aber ich tröstete mich damit, dass das nur vorübergehend sei. Dann wurde der Funke in Ricks Augen durch einen stumpfen Blick ersetzt. Er zog sich von uns zurück. Ich wusste, dass etwas nicht stimmte, aber ich konnte es nicht benennen.“

„Dann wurde er gewählt, die letzten vier Monate der Sekretariatsaufgaben für einen Bruder zu übernehmen, der einige Zeit in Bulgarien verbrachte. An jenem Abend kam er nach Hause und weinte. ‚Versteht denn niemand, was ich durchmache? Jedes Mal, wenn ich mich umdrehe, gibt es etwas zu tun. Die Jungen wollen angeln gehen, du brauchst eine neue Wäscheleine und der Hühnerstall muss in sechs Monaten fertig sein! Ich bin geistig nicht in der Lage, noch eine weitere Aufgabe zu übernehmen.‘”

„Das war der Tropfen, der das Fass zum Überlaufen brachte“, sagte Becky. „Ich wurde alarmiert, als ich ihn mitten in der Nacht gähnen hörte und wusste, dass er nicht schlief.“

„Mir war klar, dass mein perfektionistischer Mann überlastet war. Mehr und mehr lehnte sich Rick an mich. Ich reduzierte meine Verpflichtungen und versuchte, meine Zeit frei zu halten, damit ich verfügbar war, um seine Last zu verringern.“

„Ich fühlte mich wie eine Rettungsschwimmerin, die versucht, einen Mann vor dem Ertrinken zu retten, während ich selbst ein wenig zu viel Wasser schluckte. Viele der häuslichen Aufgaben lagen auf meinen Schultern. Dann wurde ich gebeten, die Position im Essenskomitee für Mrs. ‚Going-to-Bulgaria‘ zu übernehmen.“

Leider bleibt umständebedingter Stress oft unbemerkt. Schlimmer noch: Das Opfer kann missverstanden oder falsch beurteilt werden. Becky sagte: „Mein dunkelster Tag kam, als man mir Vorwurf machte, ich sei egoistisch mit meiner Zeit, weil ich die Anfrage des Essenskomitees ablehnte.“

Lang andauernde Überlastung kann emotional und mental schädlich sein

Intensiver, lang andauernder Druck oder Belastungen, die man allein trägt, können schweren Stress verursachen. Geringer Stress ist normal, aber anhaltender Stress kann Depressionen, Angstzustände, Herzkrankheiten und Bluthochdruck verursachen. Wie man mit andauerndem Stress umgeht, ist wichtig.

Manchmal ist diese Art von Überlastung nicht öffentlich bekannt. Traumatische Ereignisse in unserem unmittelbaren Umfeld erhalten eher Gebet, finanzielle Hilfe und wöchentliche Budget-Updates. Zur gleichen Zeit leiden andere Heilige abseits tief und erhalten wenig Anerkennung oder finanzielle Unterstützung. Es können angespannte Beziehungen oder kleine Rechnungen sein, die sich zu einer großen Summe addieren. Verrat und Zurückweisung verursachen Stress ohne Maß. Es gibt keine schnellen Lösungen für umständebedingten Stress, aber kleine Lichtfunken können Ihnen helfen, durch die Dunkelheit zu navigieren.

Sprechen Sie mit jemandem, dem Sie vertrauen, über Ihre Situation

Manchmal kann allein das Aussprechen von Problemen helfen, die Dinge ins rechte Licht zu rücken. Sich selbst eine stressvolle Situation laut aussprechen, löst auf irgendeine Weise den Nebel im Gehirn und eröffnet einen klareren Weg nach vorn.

Finden Sie eine Routine

Wenn Stress vorherrscht, treten ungebetene Renn-Gedanken, Vergesslichkeit und Unfähigkeit zur Konzentration auf. Eine Routine kann Ihrem geistigen Wohlbefinden Rhythmus geben. Die kleinste Normalität bringt einen Moment des Vergnügens und beruhigt die Seele.

Suchen Sie absichtlich nach einer Atempause

Anhaltender Stress kann Unruhe, Launenhaftigkeit und den Wunsch nach Kontrolle verursachen. Manchmal ist es schwer, über den mentalen Nebel hinauszudenken, aber es ist so wichtig, Erfrischung für Ihr geistiges Wohlbefinden zu finden. Stresshormone können Ihre Herzfrequenz beschleunigen und Ihre Blutgefäße verengen. Das erhöht vorübergehend Ihren Blutdruck. Das Gegenteil geschieht, wenn Sie sich entspannen. Entspannt zu sein hilft, einen ruhigeren, klareren Geist zu haben, was Ihre Konzentration und Entscheidungsfähigkeit verbessert.

Glauben Sie, dass Gott sich kümmert

Sagen Sie es. Lesen Sie die Psalmen immer wieder. Hören Sie gute Musik. Machen Sie kurze Spaziergänge und beten Sie laut. Halten Sie Ihre Augen auf Jesus gerichtet. Glauben Sie: „Weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning" (Psalm 30:5).

Wenn Sie mit umständebedingter Überlastung konfrontiert sind, seien Sie geduldig und realistisch. Gott wird einen Weg für Sie schaffen. Oft öffnet er Türen genau dann, wenn uns die Optionen ausgehen. Er wird die nötige Gnade für diese Stunde geben. Und für die nächste Stunde. Und für die nächste. Manchmal kommen überraschende Möglichkeiten, und Gebete werden auf unerwartete Weise erhört. Wie er sich auch entscheidet, in Ihrem Interesse zu wirken, halten Sie seine unveränderliche Hand fest.

Unabhängig von der Art der Überlastung, der Sie begegnen, wenden Sie sich an Ihren himmlischen Vater.

Bitten Sie ihn um Leitung und Weisheit. Und sprechen Sie mit dem Psalmisten: „In thee, O LORD, do I put my trust: let me never be put to confusion" (Psalm 71:1).

Do you believe in miracles? Do you believe in the supernatural? What about divine intervention? Or a better question might be, have you seen God working in your life? Do others see God working in your life?

My brother was working in the greenhouse when a customer walked in and marveled at the beauty of all the plants. He then exclaimed how impressed he was at all our hard work. My brother responded with, “Some plant, some water, but God gives the increase.” To which the customer responded with, “No, no, don’t give the credit to God. You came out here and did all this work. You planted, watered, and fertilized all these plants, and you all deserve the credit, not God!” The reason the man felt this way is because he was a humanist.

What is Humanism?

The dictionary defines humanism like this; an outlook or system of thought attaching prime importance to human rather than divine or supernatural matters. Humanist beliefs stress the potential value and goodness of human beings, emphasize common human needs, and seek solely rational ways of solving human problems.

If God does exist, then we will have to recognize this fact and answer to Him. Humanists attempt to prove that God does not exist, so they can freely live their lives as they please. According to humanism, there is no God. If so, then we, the human race, are superior to God. Everything is for us and our ultimate happiness. This is the definition of humanism.

Two Types of Humanism

There are two types of humanistic beliefs, and we will look at both. The first belief is the theory that there is no God. In reality, this seems to be the only rational way to be a humanist. Everything is created by man and for man. There are no other factors or supernatural involvement. Everything happens by reason and common sense. There is a logical explanation for everything that happens. Of course, some things do not make sense, but humanists brush those aside and look only at the things that can be explained. Like the plants in the greenhouse, they look at all that man does and ignore the supernatural part of a plant springing forth with new life. Scientists around the world are working diligently to put human reasoning into everything that has ever happened, even the creation of the world. Scientists, with all their learning and wisdom, attempt to give logical explanations for why natural disasters and global crises happen. If they can explain everything, then they can rule out God and His existence. This allows the human race to do as it pleases without eternal consequences. This, in turn leads to a great sense of false peace.

The humanists, with all their reasoning, mock the very existence of God. If you go to most colleges in America and talk to people about Christianity, they laugh at you and mock the fact that Christians actually believe in God.

The second type of humanistic belief is a theory of humanism that acknowledges the existence of God. One anthropologist argued that humanism is a project of modernity and a secularized continuation of Western Christian theology. But if you ask people what they think humanism means, you will likely get different responses, and it becomes very confusing. But why the confusion? Because people are trying to be Christian humanists. Christian Humanism has frequently been criticized for its vagueness and difficulty to define. The reason it has become so confusing is that people want to believe in God but also believe in themselves and that the world revolves around them.

In Romans, we read, “For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them. For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse: Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things. Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen. For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections: for even their women did change the natural use into that which is against nature: And likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust one toward another; men with men working that which is unseemly, and receiving in themselves that recompence of their error which was meet. And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient; Being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers, Backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents, Without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful: Who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them” (Romans 1:18-32).

So how can one be a humanist and believe in God? This is where we hit a little closer to home. This type of humanist believes God wants him to be happy. He believes in a Creator God but does not believe he has to serve Him In reality. He doesn’t believe in the true God but, in his mind, created a fictitious god that does not exist. This allows him to live for himself and his own happiness. This type of person will talk about God, go to church, sing songs, and say prayers. However, he will look only to man for all his needs. If he is sick, he calls a doctor. If he needs money, he goes to the banker. If the need is a break from reality, he takes a vacation or retreat. He lives life for his own happiness and then thanks God though he did not look to God for his needs. These people are dependent on themselves. They have confidence in themselves.

Here is an example: A Christian plants a garden and takes care of it each day. He waters and fertilizes weeds and prunes. Finally, his plants all begin to bear fruit, nice fruit. He thanks God for the plentiful harvest. His neighbor, an atheistic humanist, also planted a garden. He, too, went out each day and watered, pruned, weeded, and fertilized. He also received a bountiful harvest. This man, however, boasted of all that he had accomplished. Both men did the same things and had similar results. One gave God the credit, and one credited himself. He will say he accomplished the same thing without God that his neighbor did with God. Christians know that he is wrong and that he actually did need God to grow his garden.

When something happens that requires supernatural intervention, the Christian humanist prays and asks others to pray. However, he does not believe God will answer their prayers and instantly gets to work to solve his problem, with only human reasoning. Then, if the problem is resolved, he thanks God for it. This type of humanism has confused the modern world. It has caused unbelievers to mock the Christian faith and to call it a false religion with no power.

The Christian does not believe in human reasoning. The Christian believes that the God of heaven is the reason for everything. “For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him” (Colossians 1:16). We are nothing without Him, and without Him, we can do nothing. Christianity is the opposite of humanism. When the Christian does something supernatural, something the humanist or atheist cannot do, then we have something that will confound the wise.

When the neighbor sees the Christian loving his enemies, forgiving someone who wronged him, and doing things that he cannot do, he then begins to wonder where the power to do these things came from. This then leads him to the Father. When there is nothing supernatural that we are doing, he is confused.

What About Us?

I fear that we are falling into this trap of ‘Christian Humanism.’ We talk the talk; we say we believe in God. We go to church, sing songs, and say prayers. However, from outward appearances, we trust in ourselves. Because we have centered our lives around ourselves and our well-being, the God of heaven does not hear us. Our prayers are not answered, and the time on our knees is a struggle at best. We go through the motions because that is how we’ve been taught, but our faith lies in human reasoning.

It can be extremely difficult to seek the Lord while living in a humanistic society. A society that has perfected the pursuit of liberty and happiness. Slowly, the church is caving to the ways of this world.

A minister from China was visiting the churches in America. Before departing back to China, he was asked what impressed him most about the churches in America. He replied, “I am amazed at what all they have accomplished without God.”

We would do well to simplify the modern definition of humanism. The humanist proudly denies that there is a God when he boasts of his own strength and abilities. He proclaims the great accomplishments of man and mocks the humble Christian.

The Christian denies himself, picks up his cross, and follows his Master. The Christian thinks nothing of himself or the ability of man, confidently admitting that he is merely dust and back to that dust he will quickly go. The Christian looks for the good in others and trusts God for all his daily needs and cares.

Christians believe they are merely servants to their master. They are hated by the world and despised by most, rejected. “If the world hate you, ye know that it hated me before it hated you. (John 15:18)” To them, this life is not the pursuit of happiness. The things of this world do not even interest them. Their joy and peace comes solely from serving their master, from pleasing their Heavenly Father. To the world, they are strange. Fools. To God, they are His dear children.

God is still looking for people today who will put their trust in Him. He is looking over all the earth for someone, somewhere, who will put aside human reasoning and common sense and obey the voice from heaven. God wants men with faith who will step out into the supernatural, like Abraham, Moses, David, and the thousands of believers that followed. Someone who will deny himself and this world and follow the Savior.

When this life is over, the humanists, whether they say they believe in God or not, will perish. And the Christians will go on to live forever in glory.

Humanist? Christian? Christian Humanist? Which one are you?

Glo jy in wonderwerke? Glo jy in die bonatuurlike? Wat van goddelike ingryping? Of dalk – – – – – – – – is die beter vraag: het jy God in jou lewe sien werk? Sien ander God in jou lewe werk?

My broer was besig in die kweekhuis toe ’n kliënt ingeloop het en verstom geraak het oor die skoonheid van al die plante. Hy het toe uitgeroep hoe beïndruk hy was met al ons harde werk. My broer het gereageer met, “Sommige plant, sommige water, maar God gee die toename.” Waarop die kliënt geantwoord het, “Nee, nee, gee nie die kredit aan God nie. Julle het hier uitgekom en al hierdie werk gedoen. Julle het al die plante geplant, bewater en bemes, en julle verdien die krediet, nie God nie!” Die rede dat die man so gevoel het, is omdat hy ’n humanis was.

Wat is Humanisme?

Die woordeboek omskryf humanisme soos volg; ’n siening of denkstelsel wat primêre belang aan die mens eerder as die goddelike of bonatuurlike heg. Humanistiese oortuigings beklemtoon die potensiële waarde en goedheid van mense, beklemtoon algemene menslike behoeftes, en soek uitsluitlik rasionele maniere om menslike probleme op te los.

As God wel bestaan, dan sal ons hierdie feit moet erken en aan Hom moet antwoord. Humaniste probeer bewys dat God nie bestaan nie, sodat hulle vryelik hul lewens kan leef soos hulle wil. Volgens humanisme bestaan daar geen God nie. As dit so is, dan is ons, die menslike ras, superieur aan God. Alles is vir ons en ons uiteindelike geluk. Dit is die definisie van humanisme.

Twee soorte Humanisme

Daar is twee soorte humanistiese oortuigings, en ons sal na albei kyk. Die eerste oortuiging is die teorie dat daar geen God is nie. In werklikheid lyk dit asof dit die enigste rasionele manier is om ’n humanis te wees. Alles is deur die mens geskep en vir die mens. Daar is geen ander faktore of bonatuurlike betrokkenheid nie. Alles gebeur deur rede en gesonde verstand. Daar is ’n logiese verklaring vir alles wat gebeur. Natuurlik maak sommige dinge geen sin nie, maar humaniste vee daardie sake ter syde en kyk net na die dinge wat verduidelik kan word. Soos die plante in die kweekhuis, kyk hulle na alles wat die mens doen en ignoreer die bonatuurlike deel van ’n plant wat met nuwe lewe opstaan. Wetenskaplikes regoor die wêreld werk ywerig om menslike redenasie in alles wat ooit gebeur het te plaas, selfs die skepping van die wêreld. Wetenskaplikes, met al hul kennis en wysheid, probeer logiese verduidelikings gee vir hoekom natuurlike rampe en globale krisisse plaasvind. As hulle alles kan verduidelik, kan hulle God en Sy bestaan uitskakel. Dit stel die menslike ras in staat om te doen soos hy wil sonder ewige gevolge. Dit lei op sy beurt tot ’n groot gevoel van vals vrede.

Die humaniste, met al hul redenasie, bespot die very bestaan van God. As jy na die meeste kolleges in Amerika gaan en met mense oor die Christendom praat, lag hulle jou uit en spot oor die feit dat Christene werklik in God glo.

Die tweede tipe humanistiese oortuiging is ’n teorie van humanisme wat die bestaan van God erken. ’n Antropoloog het geredeneer dat humanisme ’n projek van moderniteit is en ’n gesekulariseerde voortsetting van Westerse Christelike teologie. Maar as jy mense vra wat hulle dink humanisme beteken, sal jy waarskynlik verskillende antwoorde kry, en dit raak baie verwarrend. Maar waarom die verwarring? Omdat mense probeer om Christen‑humaniste te wees. Christelike Humanisme is dikwels gekritiseer oor sy vaagheid en moeilike definisie. Die rede waarom dit so verwarrend geword het, is omdat mense wil glo in God, maar ook in hulself glo en dat die wêreld om hulle draai.

In Romans, we read, “For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them. For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse: Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things. Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen. For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections: for even their women did change the natural use into that which is against nature: And likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust one toward another; men with men working that which is unseemly, and receiving in themselves that recompence of their error which was meet. And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient; Being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers, Backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents, Without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful: Who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them” (Romans 1:18-32).

Hoe kan iemand dus ’n humanis wees en in God glo? Hier kom ons ’n bietjie nader aan huis. Hierdie tipe humanis glo God wil hê hy moet gelukkig wees. Hy glo in ’n Skepper‑God maar glo nie dat hy Hom in werklikheid moet dien nie. Hy glo nie in die ware God nie, maar in sy gedagtes het hy ’n fiktiewe god geskep wat nie bestaan nie. Dit stel hom in staat om vir homself en sy eie geluk te leef. Hierdie soort persoon sal oor God praat, na die kerk gaan, liedere sing, en gebede sê. Hy sal egter net na die mens kyk vir al sy behoeftes. As hy siek is, bel hy ’n dokter. As hy geld nodig het, gaan hy na die bankier. As die behoefte ’n pouses van die werklikheid is, neem hy ’n vakansie of wegbreek. Hy leef vir sy eie geluk en dank dan God, alhoewel hy nie na God gekyk het vir sy behoeftes nie. Hierdie mense is afhanklik van hulself. Hulle het vertroue in hulself.

Hier is ’n voorbeeld: ’n Christen plant ’n tuin en sorg elke dag daarvoor. Hy water en bemes, wied en snoei. Uiteindelik begin sy plante vrug dra, mooi vrug. Hy dank God vir die ryk oes. Sy buurman, ’n ateïstiese humanis, het ook ’n tuin geplant. Hy het ook elke dag uitgegaan en water gegee, gesnoei, gewied en bemes. Ook hy het ’n oorvloedige oes ontvang. Hierdie man het egter gepronk oor alles wat hy bereik het. Beide mans het dieselfde dinge gedoen en soortgelyke resultate gehad. Een het God die krediet gegee, en een het homself gekrediteer. Hy sal sê hy het dieselfde ding bereik sonder God as wat sy buurman met God gedoen het. Christene weet hy is verkeerd en dat hy eintlik God nodig gehad het om sy tuin te laat groei.

Wanneer iets gebeur wat bonatuurlike ingryping vereis, bid die Christen‑humanis en vra ander om te bid. Hy glo egter nie God sal hulle gebede beantwoord nie en begin dadelik werk om sy probleem op te los, slegs met menslike redenasie. Dan, as die probleem opgelos word, bedank hy God daarvoor. Hierdie tipe humanisme het die moderne wêreld verwar. Dit het ongelowiges veroorsaak om die Christelike geloof te bespot en dit ’n vals godsdiens sonder krag te noem.

Die Christen glo nie in menslike redenasie nie. Die Christen glo dat die God van die hemel die rede vir alles is. “For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him” (Colossians 1:16). Ons is niks sonder Hom nie, en sonder Hom kan ons niks doen nie. Christenskap is die teenoorgestelde van humanisme. Wanneer die Christen iets bonatuurliks doen, iets wat die humanis of ateïs nie kan doen nie, dan het ons iets wat die wyse sal verstom.

Wanneer die buurman die Christen sien sy vyande liefhet, iemand vergewe wat hom onreg aangedoen het, en dinge doen wat hy nie kan doen nie, begin hy wonder waarvandaan die krag gekom het om hierdie dinge te doen. Dit lei hom dan na die Vader. Wanneer daar niks bonatuurliks is wat ons doen nie, is hy verward.

En wat van ons?

Ek vrees ons val in hierdie val wat ’n ‘Christen‑Humanisme’ is. Ons praat die praat; ons sê ons glo in God. Ons gaan kerk toe, sing liedere, en sê gebede. Maar van buite af lyk dit asof ons op onsself vertrou. Omdat ons ons lewens om onsself en ons welstand gesentreer het, hoor die God van die hemel ons nie. Ons gebede word nie beantwoord nie, en ons tyd op ons knieë is op sy beste ’n stryd. Ons gaan deur die bewegings omdat dit is hoe ons geleer is, maar ons geloof lê in menslike redenasie.

Dit kan buitengewoon moeilik wees om die Here te soek terwyl jy in ’n humanistiese samelewing woon. ’n Samelewing wat die strewe na vryheid en geluk perfek gemaak het. Stadigaan gee die kerk toe aan die maniere van hierdie wêreld.

’n Predikant van China het die kerke in Amerika besoek. Voordat hy terug China toe vertrek het, is hy gevra wat hom die meeste beïndruk het aan die kerke in Amerika. Hy het geantwoord, “Ek is verbaas oor wat hulle alles sonder God bereik het.”

Ons sou goed doen om die moderne definisie van humanisme te vereenvoudig. Die humanis ontken trots dat daar ’n God is wanneer hy oor sy eie krag en vermoëns opschep. Hy proklameer die groot prestasies van die mens en bespot die nederige Christen.

Die Christen ontken homself, neem sy kruis op, en volg sy Meester. Die Christen dink niks van homself of die vermoë van die mens nie, en erken met vertroue dat hy bloot stof is en vinnig na daardie stof sal terugkeer. Die Christen soek die goeie in ander en vertrou God vir al sy daaglikse behoeftes en sorg.

Christene glo hulle is bloot diensknechte van hul Meester. Hulle word deur die wêreld gehaat en deur die meeste verag en verwerp. “If the world hate you, ye know that it hated me before it hated you. (John 15:18)” Vir hulle is hierdie lewe nie die strewe na geluk nie. Die dinge van hierdie wêreld interesseer hulle glad nie. Hul vreugde en vrede kom uitsluitlik uit die diens aan hul Meester, uit die behae van hul Hemelse Vader. Vir die wêreld is hulle vreemd. Dwase. Vir God is hulle Sy dierbare kinders.

God soek steeds mense vandag wat op Hom sal vertrou. Hy kyk oor die hele aarde vir iemand, êrens, wat menslike redenasie en gesonde verstand opsy sal sit en die stem uit die hemel sal gehoorsaam. God wil manne met geloof hê wat in die bonatuurlike sal tree, soos Abraham, Moses, Dawid, en die duisende gelowiges wat gevolg het. Iemand wat homself en hierdie wêreld sal ontken en die Verlosser sal volg.

Wanneer hierdie lewe verby is, sal die humaniste, hetsy hulle sê hulle glo in God of nie, verderf. En die Christene sal voortgaan om vir ewig in heerlikheid te lewe.

Humanis? Christen? Christen‑Humanis? Watter een is jy?

I can still smell the tantalizing cacophony of odors as I clutched my father’s strong hand, weaving our way through the masses of tourists that crowded the building. The vendors at the Green Dragon Farmer’s Market in Ephrata, PA, were trying their best to entice buyers with their rows of fresh fish over ice, cheeses of every variety, deli meat and sandwiches, and piles of fresh fruit. And, oh, the candy! My young preschool mind had never seen so many delectable sweets in one place at one time.

The past two days for me were like the boy at the candy store. I had the privilege of attending Christian Aid Ministries’ first Annual Writers’ Conference. I brushed shoulders with well-known authors such as Katrina Hoover Lee, Johnny Miller, and Ruthann Stelfox. I chatted with aspiring writers and seasoned school teachers. I had the opportunity to sit under hours of inspirational and educational workshops on how to write to communicate, using realistic dialog, descriptive writing, and much more. We all had one common goal in mind. Together, we share and learn how to effectively communicate what is in our hearts, and through the power of the written word, transmit those thoughts to your hearts.

The Heartbeat of the Remnant is a means to communicate inspirational thoughts to eager readers scattered across the globe. Courageous writers step forward with pen and paper or keyboard and monitor and help spread the Good News of the Word of God with caution, correction, and edification. Yet, we need more such writers. We need young believers who bravely submit their first children’s stories. Seasoned grandfathers who bring words of admonishment to the younger generation. Mothers who share experiences and trials with other mothers who are in the throes of raising little ones. Youth encouraging fellow youth to press toward the mark of the prize of the high calling in Christ Jesus. Fathers who with a concerned eye watch the world pressing in on the Christian homes. Together, these aspiring writers will produce a periodical that will endure on the family coffee table for many years. I encourage you, fellow believers, to give it a try. Nelson Mandela, former president of South Africa wrote, “Failure is a teacher, and at the end of your life, what do you think you’ll feel worst about, failing or never trying?”

The Berean Voice has a goal to provide printed material that will help readers navigate through the varied and difficult seasons of life. All our material is available at no charge, but we are dependent on the donations of our supporters. Here is a list of books we have available:

In 2017 and 2018, the Berean Voice printed a series of vaccine articles in The Heartbeat of the Remnant magazine. These articles were a sincere effort to examine various aspects of vaccine usage with an unbiased approach. We attempted to present the facts as clearly as possible and let the readers draw their own conclusions.

Since then, we have received numerous requests from our readers to publish all the vaccine articles in a booklet, which we agreed to do. But then along came 2019, bringing coronavirus with it. This monumental event upended the vaccine debate and ushered in a frenzied rush to market COVID-19 remedies, many of which were not properly tested. We put the printing on hold, unsure whether to include information on these new and unproven COVID-19 “vaccines.” As time progressed and the deadly nature of COVID-19 abated, we decided to publish the original vaccine articles in a booklet without any additional articles on the COVID-19 debate. We are pleased that the project is nearing completion and will be announced when it is released.

Blessings to all,

Edward Martin

아직도 나는 관광객들로 붐비는 건물 속을 아버지의 굳센 손을 잡고 헤치며 다니던 때의, 유혹적인 냄새들의 소란스러운 혼합을 맡을 수 있다. 펜실베이니아 에프라타의 그린 드래곤 농부 시장에선 상인들이 얼음 위에 진열한 신선한 생선, 각종 치즈, 델리 고기와 샌드위치, 산더미처럼 쌓인 신선한 과일들로 손님들을 끌어들이기 위해 최선을 다하고 있었다. 그리고, 아, 사탕들! 어린 유치원생이었던 내 마음은 한 장소에서 이렇게 많은 맛있는 단 것을 본 적이 없었다.

지난 이틀은 나에게 사탕가게에 있는 소년과 같았다. 나는 Christian Aid Ministries의 첫 연례 작가 회의에 참석하는 특권을 누렸다. 카트리나 후버 리, 조니 밀러, 루탄 스텔폭스 같은 잘 알려진 작가들과 어깨를 나란히 했다. 야심 있는 작가들과 경험 많은 학교 교사들과 이야기했다. 소통을 위한 글쓰기, 현실적인 대화 사용, 묘사적 글쓰기 등 여러 시간의 영감 주는 교육적 워크숍을 들을 기회가 있었다. 우리 모두의 공통된 목표는 하나였다. 함께 우리는 마음에 있는 것을 효과적으로 전달하는 법을 나누고 배우며, 글의 힘으로 그 생각들을 여러분의 마음에 전하는 것이다.

The Heartbeat of the Remnant은 전 세계에 흩어져 있는 열독자들에게 영감을 주는 생각들을 전달하는 수단이다. 용기 있는 작가들이 펜과 종이나 키보드와 모니터를 들고 나와 신중함과 교정, 그리고 덕을 세우는 마음으로 하나님의 말씀의 복된 소식을 전파하는 데 도움을 준다. 그럼에도 우리는 더 많은 작가들을 필요로 한다. 처음으로 동화책을 내어놓을 용기 있는 젊은 신자들. 젊은 세대에게 권면의 말을 전하는 경험 많은 할아버지들. 어린 자녀를 양육하는 한복판에 있는 다른 어머니들과 경험과 시련을 나누는 어머니들. 그리스도 예수 안에서 높은 부르심의 상을 향해 나아가도록 또래를 격려하는 청소년들. 기독교 가정 위로 세상이 밀려오는 것을 염려스러운 눈길로 지켜보는 아버지들. 이들 모두가 함께 모여 여러 해 동안 가족들의 커피 테이블 위에 놓일 수 있는 정기간행물을 만들어 낼 것이다. 신자 여러분, 도전해 보시길 권면한다. 남아프리카 공화국의 전 대통령 넬슨 만델라는 이렇게 썼다. “실패는 스승이다. 그리고 인생의 끝에서, 당신은 무엇이 더 더 나쁘다고 느끼겠는가, 실패인가 아니면 시도조차 하지 않은 것인가?”

The Berean Voice는 독자들이 삶의 다양한 어려운 계절을 헤쳐 나가는 데 도움이 되는 인쇄물을 제공하는 것을 목표로 한다. 우리의 모든 자료는 무료로 제공되지만, 우리는 지지자들의 기부에 의존하고 있다. 다음은 우리가 보유한 책들의 목록이다:

The Power of the Love of Truth

2017년과 2018년에 The Berean Voice는 The Heartbeat of the Remnant 잡지에 백신 관련 연재 기사를 실었다. 이 기사들은 백신 사용의 여러 측면을 편견 없는 접근으로 살펴보려는 진지한 시도였다. 우리는 가능한 한 사실을 명확히 제시하고 독자들이 스스로 결론을 내리도록 하려 노력했다.

그 이후로 독자들로부터 모든 백신 기사를 소책자로 발행해 달라는 많은 요청을 받았고, 우리는 그렇게 하기로 동의했다. 그러나 2019년 코로나바이러스가 등장하면서 상황이 바뀌었다. 이 거대한 사건은 백신 논쟁을 뒤흔들었고, 많은 부분에서 적절한 시험을 거치지 않은 COVID-19 치료제들을 시장에 급히 내놓는 광란을 촉발시켰다. 우리는 인쇄를 보류했고, 이 새로운 입증되지 않은 COVID-19 "백신"들에 대한 정보를 포함할지 여부를 확신하지 못했다. 시간이 흐르고 COVID-19의 치명성이 누그러지자, 우리는 원래의 백신 기사들을 COVID-19 논쟁에 관한 추가 기사 없이 소책자로 발행하기로 결정했다. 이 프로젝트가 거의 완료되어 출간 시에 발표하게 됨을 기쁘게 생각한다.

모든 분들에게 축복이 있기를,

Edward Martin

Eight-year-old Jamin wasn’t very smart. Or at least that’s what his older brother told him. Almost daily, brother Kenny found ways to remind Jamin of his shortcomings and laugh at his blunders.

“Jamin, you will never be smart”, Kenny said. Deep inside Jamin felt resigned to a life of muddled trip-ups. Would he always be clumsy? Would he always say things wrong? That’s what Kenny said.

Jamin believed Kenny’s lectures with wide-eyed belief. Kenny was three years older than him, so he must be right. Very well, then Jamin would be simple. Kenny would be smart. Life was not fair. Dad and Mom disliked Kenny’s proud talk and punished him whenever they walked in on one of his speeches. But Kenny had a way of avoiding earshot. So he continued mocking Jamin.

Grandma Otto watched these trials from her rocker on the porch. She was a quiet old lady.

“Jamin, do you know where Kenny is?” Mom asked with a smile. “It’s almost supper time.”

“He went to check his coyote traps. I’ll go find him.”

There was a chill in the air as he tramped up over the lawn, and the sun was growing old as he crossed the border of the woods. The fleeting shadows scurried over the hills. The chill deepened as he stumped further in. He breathed the rich air and followed Kenny’s trail. Eventually, the trail would end up in a meadow, but Jamin hoped he would find Kenny before he had to go that far. The various traps had been checked already, so Jamin knew Kenny had come this way. Jamin trudged on resolutely. His golden head caught the tired beams that fled from the sun as they flickered through the trees. And soon those too had faded leaving behind the musky smell of the woods. The fall webworms had been at work, and their web curtains shuttered from branches overhead.

At length, as the trees subdued and thinned, and the meadow appeared Jamin knew this was the end of his brother’s trap route. If Kenny wasn’t here, he wouldn’t know where else to look.

But Kenny was there. As Jamin clumped into the meadow, he could see a frustrated heap to his right. The heap’s voice had a familiar ring. The heap’s face was lit in pain. The heap was Kenny. “Are you alright? What happened?” Jamin felt strange, seeing Kenny scrunched in the dirt. Kenny was smart. “Did you step in a trap?”

“Yes, Jamin. I..I wasn’t looking where I was going. Help me. Please.”

Jamin bent and found an ankle firmly held in the jaws of a steel trap. Darkness stained the ground around Kenny. Quickly, Jamin’s strong arms pried open the jaws. Kenny reeled free. “Can you walk?”

“Yes. I think so. If you support me, I can hobble along.”

“Dad and Mom will be worried. We’ve missed supper.”

Sure enough, as the brothers hobbled back through the woods, they heard the long calling of their father. Jamin called back, and he was by their side in a moment, seeing the ankle and scooping up Kenny like a hurt sheep. The odd little band hurried home, and the screen door banged shut as Dad swept across the porch. Jamin went to the wash house and scrubbed his hands. He headed for the front door.

“Jamin.” It was Grandma. The porch light showed her in her old rocker. A heavy comforter lay on her shoulders.

“Yes, Grandma?”

“Do you think you are not very smart?”

“That’s what Kenny says.” Jamin squirmed.

“You were strong enough to open the trap, and Kenny wasn’t. You were brave enough to find him in the dark. Lots of young boys wouldn’t be.” Jamin was silent. Grandma Otto rocked some more, then smiled. “God made you the way you are for a reason, Jamin. He made Kenny the way he is for a reason. He has a plan for you, and a place only you can fill, you know.”

Jamin turned and walked into the warm kitchen. He was smiling.

آٹھ سالہ جیمِن بہت ہوشیار نہیں تھا۔ یا کم از کم ایسا اُس کا بڑا بھائی اُسے بتاتا تھا۔ تقریباً روزانہ، بھائی کینی کسی نہ کسی طرح جیمِن کو اس کی خامیوں کی یاد دلاتا اور اُس کی غلطیوں پر ہنستا رہتا۔

“جیمِن، تم کبھی ہوشیار نہیں بنو گے”، کینی نے کہا۔ اندر سے جیمِن زندگی بھر کی الجھنوں اور ٹھوکر کھانے کے لیے مایوس محسوس کرنے لگا۔ کیا وہ ہمیشہ بے پاؤں رہے گا؟ کیا وہ ہمیشہ غلط باتیں کہتا رہے گا؟ یہی تو کینی کہتا تھا۔

جیمِن نے بڑی کھلی آنکھوں کے ساتھ کینی کی نصیحتیں مان لیں۔ کینی اُس سے تین سال بڑا تھا، اس لیے وہ درست ہو گا۔ ٹھیک ہے، تو جیمِن سادہ ہوگا۔ کینی ہوشیار ہوگا۔ زندگی منصفانہ نہیں تھی۔ پاپا اور ماما کو کینی کی غرور بھری باتیں ناپسند آتیں اور جب بھی وہ اس کے سخن سن لیتے تو اُسے سزا دیتے۔ مگر کینی نے کانوں سے دور رہنے کا راستہ نکال رکھا تھا۔ لہٰذا وہ جیمِن کا مذاق بنائے رہا۔

دادی اوٹو ان آزمائشوں کو اپنے برِکر پر بیٹھ کر دیکھتی رہیں۔ وہ ایک خاموش بوڑھی عورت تھیں۔

“جیمِن، کیا تم جانتے ہو کینی کہاں ہے؟” ماما نے مسکراہٹ کے ساتھ پوچھا۔ “شام کا کھانا قریب ہے۔”

“وہ اپنے کایٔوٹ پھندے چیک کرنے گیا تھا۔ میں اسے ڈھونڈ لاؤں گا۔”

جب وہ لان پر چلتا ہوا اوپر کی طرف گیا تو ہوا میں سردی تھی، اور جب وہ جنگل کے کنارے سے گزرا تو سورج بوڑھا ہوتا گیا۔ عارضی سائے پہاڑیوں پر دوڑ رہے تھے۔ جوں جوں وہ اور اندر گیا سردی گہری ہوتی گئی۔ اُس نے خوشگوار ہوا سانس میں لی اور کینی کا نشان تلاش کیا۔ بالآخر یہ راستہ ایک چراگاہ تک جا پہنچتا، مگر جیمِن امید کرتا تھا کہ اتنا دور جانے سے پہلے وہ کینی ڈھونڈ لے گا۔ مختلف پھندے پہلے ہی چیک کیے جا چکے تھے، لہٰذا جیمِن جانتا تھا کہ کینی اسی راستے سے آیا تھا۔ جیمِن پختگی سے آگے بڑھتا رہا۔ اُس کا سنہری سر اُن تھکے ہوئے شعاعوں کو پکڑتا جو درختوں کے بیچ جھلملاتے سورج سے بھاگ رہی تھیں۔ اور جلد ہی وہ شعاعیں بھی مدھم پڑ گئیں، پیچھے جنگل کی مَسکی بو چھوڑ گئیں۔ فال ویب ورمز نے کام کیا تھا، اُن کے جال شاخوں سے اوپر پردے کی طرح جھول رہے تھے۔

آخر کار، جب درخت پتلے ہوئے اور چراگاہ نمودار ہوئی تو جیمِن جان گیا کہ یہ اُس کے بھائی کے پھندے کے راستے کا اختتام ہے۔ اگر کینی یہاں نہ ہو تو وہ نہیں جانتا تھا کہ اور کہاں دیکھے۔

مگر کینی وہاں تھا۔ جب جیمِن چراگاہ میں گھسا تو وہ اپنی دائیں جانب ایک مایوس ڈھیر دیکھ سکا۔ اس ڈھیر کی آواز مانوس تھی۔ اُس کے چہرے پر درد کی روشنی تھی۔ وہ کینی تھا۔ “کیا تم ٹھیک ہو؟ کیا ہوا؟” جیمِن کو عجیب سا محسوس ہوا کہ کینی مٹی میں دوُبھا ہوا ہے۔ کینی ہوشیار تھا۔ “کیا تم کسی پھندے میں پھنس گئے ہو؟”

“ہاں، جیمِن۔ میں… میں جہاں جا رہا تھا وہاں نہیں دیکھ رہا تھا۔ میری مدد کرو۔ براہِ کرم۔”

جیمِن جھکا اور ایک ٹخنے کو سٹیل کے پھندے کے جبڑوں میں پھنسا ہوا پایا۔ اندھیرا کینی کے اردگرد زمین پر چھایا ہوا تھا۔ جلدی سے، جیمِن کی مضبوط بانہیں جبڑوں کو کھول ڈالیں۔ کینی آزاد ہو کر جھٹکا۔ “کیا تم چل سکتے ہو؟”

“ہاں۔ میرے خیال میں ہاں۔ اگر تم میری حمایت کرو تو میں ٹٹول کر چل سکتا ہوں۔”

“پاپا اور ماما فکر مند ہوں گے۔ ہم نے کھانا چھوڑ دیا ہے۔”

بے شک، جب بھائی جنگل سے واپس لنگڑاتے ہوئے آئے تو انہوں نے اپنے والد کی طویل آواز سنی۔ جیمِن نے پکارا، اور وہ ایک لمحے میں اُن کے پاس تھا، ٹخنے کو دیکھ کر کینی کو ایک زخمی بھیڑ کی طرح اٹھا لیا۔ وہ عجیب چھوٹا سا گروہ تیزی سے گھر لوٹا، اور جب باپ نے برِکر عبور کیا تو اسکرین دروازہ زور سے بند ہو گیا۔ جیمِن واش ہاؤس گیا اور اپنے ہاتھ رگڑے۔ وہ سامنے کے دروازے کی طرف گیا۔

“جیمِن۔” وہ دادی تھیں۔ پورچ کی روشنی میں وہ اپنی پرانی کرسی میں دکھائی دیں۔ اُن کے کندھوں پر ایک موٹا کمبل پڑا تھا۔

“جی، دادی؟”

“کیا تم سمجھتے ہو کہ تم بہت ہوشیار نہیں ہو؟”

“یہی تو کینی کہتا ہے۔” جیمِن شرمندگی محسوس کرتے ہوئے ہلانے لگا۔

“تم اتنے مضبوط تھے کہ پھندے کھول دیے، اور کینی نہیں تھا۔ تم اتنے بہادر تھے کہ اندھیرے میں اسے ڈھونڈ نکالا۔ بہت سے نوجوان لڑکے ایسا نہ کر پاتے۔” جیمِن خاموش رہا۔ دادی اوٹو نے مزید جھٹکے میں کرسی ہلائی، پھر مسکرائیں۔ “خدا نے تمہیں جیسا بنایا، کسی مقصد کے لیے بنایا۔ اس نے کینی کو ویسا بنایا، کسی مقصد کے لیے۔ اُس کے پاس تمہارے لیے ایک منصوبہ ہے، اور ایک جگہ جو صرف تم ہی بھر سکتے ہو، معلوم ہے۔”

جیمِن مڑا اور گرم باورچی خانے میں چلا گیا۔ وہ مسکرا رہا تھا۔

I can still smell the tantalizing cacophony of odors as I clutched my father’s strong hand, weaving our way through the masses of tourists that crowded the building. The vendors at the Green Dragon Farmer’s Market in Ephrata, PA, were trying their best to entice buyers with their rows of fresh fish over ice, cheeses of every variety, deli meat and sandwiches, and piles of fresh fruit. And, oh, the candy! My young preschool mind had never seen so many delectable sweets in one place at one time.

The past two days for me were like the boy at the candy store. I had the privilege of attending Christian Aid Ministries’ first Annual Writers’ Conference. I brushed shoulders with well-known authors such as Katrina Hoover Lee, Johnny Miller, and Ruthann Stelfox. I chatted with aspiring writers and seasoned school teachers. I had the opportunity to sit under hours of inspirational and educational workshops on how to write to communicate, using realistic dialog, descriptive writing, and much more. We all had one common goal in mind. Together, we share and learn how to effectively communicate what is in our hearts, and through the power of the written word, transmit those thoughts to your hearts.

The Heartbeat of the Remnant is a means to communicate inspirational thoughts to eager readers scattered across the globe. Courageous writers step forward with pen and paper or keyboard and monitor and help spread the Good News of the Word of God with caution, correction, and edification. Yet, we need more such writers. We need young believers who bravely submit their first children’s stories. Seasoned grandfathers who bring words of admonishment to the younger generation. Mothers who share experiences and trials with other mothers who are in the throes of raising little ones. Youth encouraging fellow youth to press toward the mark of the prize of the high calling in Christ Jesus. Fathers who with a concerned eye watch the world pressing in on the Christian homes. Together, these aspiring writers will produce a periodical that will endure on the family coffee table for many years. I encourage you, fellow believers, to give it a try. Nelson Mandela, former president of South Africa wrote, “Failure is a teacher, and at the end of your life, what do you think you’ll feel worst about, failing or never trying?”

In 2017 and 2018, the Berean Voice printed a series of vaccine articles in The Heartbeat of the Remnant magazine. These articles were a sincere effort to examine various aspects of vaccine usage with an unbiased approach. We attempted to present the facts as clearly as possible and let the readers draw their own conclusions.

Since then, we have received numerous requests from our readers to publish all the vaccine articles in a booklet, which we agreed to do. But then along came 2019, bringing coronavirus with it. This monumental event upended the vaccine debate and ushered in a frenzied rush to market COVID-19 remedies, many of which were not properly tested. We put the printing on hold, unsure whether to include information on these new and unproven COVID-19 “vaccines.” As time progressed and the deadly nature of COVID-19 abated, we decided to publish the original vaccine articles in a booklet without any additional articles on the COVID-19 debate. We are pleased that the project is nearing completion and will be announced when it is released.

Blessings to all,

Edward Martin

אני עדיין מריח את התערובת המפתה של ריחות כשאחזתי בידו החזקה של אבי, שוזר את דרכנו בין המוני התיירים שצפפו בבניין. הסוחרים בשוק האיכרים גרין דרגון באפרטה שבפנסילבניה עשו את מיטב מאמציהם לפתות קונים בשורות של דגים טריים על קרח, גבינות מכל הסוגים, סלמי וסנדוויצ’ים, וערימות של פירות טריים. ואוי, הממתקים! מוחי הצעיר לפני בית־הספר לא ראה מעולם כל כך הרבה ממתקים טעימים במקום אחד ובאותו זמן.

שני הימים האחרונים עבורי היו כמו הילד בחנות הממתקים. הייתה לי הזכות להשתתף בכנס הכותבים השנתי הראשון של Christian Aid Ministries. נגעתי בכתפיהם של מחברים ידועים כגון Katrina Hoover Lee, Johnny Miller ו-Ruthann Stelfox. שוחחתי עם כותבים שואפים ומורים ותיקים. הייתה לי ההזדמנות לשבת תחת שעות של סדנאות מעוררות השראה וחינוכיות על איך לכתוב כדי לתקשר, שימוש בדיאלוג מציאותי, כתיבה תיאורית, ועוד. היה לנו יעד משותף. יחד, אנו משתפים ולומדים איך לתקשר ביעילות את מה שבלבנו, ובאמצעות כוח המילה הכתובה להעביר את אותם המחשבות אל לבבכם.

The Heartbeat of the Remnant הוא אמצעי לתקשר מחשבות מעוררות השראה לקוראים צמאים הפזורים ברחבי העולם. כותבים אמיצים עולים עם עט ונייר או מקלדת ומסך ועוזרים להפיץ את הבשורה הטובה של דבר־אלוהים בזהירות, בתיקון ובעידוד רוחני. ועדיין, אנו זקוקים לעוד כותבים כאלה. אנו זקוקים למאמינים צעירים שמגישים באומץ את סיפוריהם הראשונים לילדים. סבים מנוסים שמביאים דברי מוסר לדור הצעיר. לאמהות שמשתפות חוויות וניסיונות עם אמהות אחרות השוקעות בגידול הקטנים. לנוער המעודד נוער לחתור אל המטרה של פרס הקריאה הנשגב במשיח ישוע. לאבות שמתבוננים בדאגה בעולמנו הלוחץ על בתי־נוצרי. יחד, כותבים שואפים אלה יפיקו תקופתון שיישאר על שולחן הקפה המשפחתי לשנים רבות. אני מעודד אתכם, חברים מאמינים, לנסות. נלסון מנדלה, נשיא דרום־אפריקה לשעבר, כתב: “Failure is a teacher, and at the end of your life, what do you think you’ll feel worst about, failing or never trying?”
